1.meaning: Alif-Lam-Mim: three Arabic letters recited individually as separate letter-names. They belong to the 'disconnected letters' (al-huruf al-muqattaʿa) that open certain chapters of the Qur'an. They are not a word with lexical meaning; their precise significance is regarded as known to Allah, though they draw attention to the inimitability of the revelation, which is composed from these very letters of the Arabic alphabet.
1.grammar: These are letter-names spelled out and recited one by one, not an inflected word, so they carry no case ending, tense, person, or number. They function as a self-standing opening and take no grammatical role within a sentence.

1.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
1.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
3.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
3.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

4.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
4.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

5.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
5.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

6.meaning: 'the Ever-Living / the Living One' — possessing life in the fullest, absolute, and eternal sense: life that never began and never ends, the source of all life. As a divine name it affirms perfect, undying life.
6.grammar: A definite adjective/noun ('the Living'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun in apposition (a descriptive title) to such a subject.

7.meaning: A divine attribute meaning the Self-Subsisting, Ever-Living Sustainer: the One who exists eternally by Himself, needing nothing, while everything else depends on Him for its continued existence and upkeep. It conveys both perpetual self-existence and the active maintaining of all creation.
7.grammar: An intensive noun built on the qayyūm pattern, which signals a permanent, exaggerated quality (one who unceasingly sustains). The definite article al- marks it as the unique, well-known One. The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate identifying who or what something is.
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, establish, maintain

1.meaning: A verb meaning 'he sent down / brought down', especially in stages or portions. The Form II shape adds intensity or gradualness to the basic 'descend', hence 'to send down piece by piece'.
1.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular, Form II. The doubled middle letter marks the intensive/gradual sense; the final -a is the standard ending for a completed past-tense action done by 'he'.
1.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, send down

2.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

3.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
3.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

4.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
4.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
4.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

5.meaning: Confirming, verifying, attesting to the truth of something — declaring that a thing is true and corroborating it.
5.grammar: An active participle of the intensive (fa''ala) pattern, naming the doer of the action ('one confirming'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, often marking a noun as an object or describing the manner/state in which something occurs ('as a confirmer').

6.meaning: To / for that which — a preposition 'to, for' joined to a relative word meaning 'what' or 'that which'.
6.grammar: A combination of the preposition li- ('to, for') with the relative pronoun mā ('that which'). Together they introduce something toward or for which an action is directed; mā itself does not change for case.

7.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
7.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

8.meaning: 'His two hands' — literally a dual 'two hands' with 'his' attached. Often used idiomatically for what lies 'in front of' or 'before' someone (i.e. between his hands).
8.grammar: The noun 'yad' (hand) in its dual form 'two hands'. The -ay ending is the dual in the genitive/accusative state (as opposed to -ā for the subject case), used after prepositions or in possessive links. The attached 'hi' means 'his' (the -i vowel of 'hi' harmonizing after the -ay). In construct, the dual's final -n drops before the pronoun.
8.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand

9.meaning: 'And He sent down / caused to descend'. It denotes bringing something down from a higher place to a lower one — characteristically the sending down of revelation. Past tense, third person masculine singular.
9.grammar: 'wa-' is the connector 'and'. 'anzala' is a past-tense verb of the causative pattern (form IV) meaning 'to make descend / send down', with the third-person masculine singular subject ('he') built in; the final '-a' is the standard past-tense ending.
9.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, send down

10.meaning: The Torah: the scripture revealed to the Prophet Moses. A proper name for that divinely revealed Book.
10.grammar: A proper noun (a name of a revealed Book). It carries the definite article al-, whose l (the lām of the article) assimilates into the following t sound, since t is a 'solar' letter that absorbs the article's lām. The final -a ending is accusative, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or after certain particles.
10.root: — (proper name of a scripture; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

11.meaning: The Gospel (Injīl): the scripture revealed to the Prophet Jesus. A proper name for that divinely revealed Book.
11.grammar: A proper noun (a name of a revealed Book) prefixed with the connector wa- ('and') and the definite article al-. The final -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb or a word governed by certain particles.
11.root: — (proper name of a scripture; of non-Arabic origin, so no Arabic triliteral root)

1.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
1.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

2.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
2.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
2.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

3.meaning: Guidance — right direction, the showing of the correct way and the leading along it. The term combines pointing out the path and granting success in following it; more than mere information, it is direction toward what is right.

parts.en: indefinite (tanwin) ending on a shortened final vowel

3.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun. The -an (tanwin) ending marks indefiniteness — 'a guidance' rather than 'the guidance'. Because the word ends in a weak final letter, its case is not audibly distinguished, so this single form covers more than one grammatical position.

4.meaning: For the people, for mankind, for humankind. The preposition 'for/to' joined to 'the people' as a collective term for human beings.
4.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') prefixed to the noun 'al-nās' ('the people'). The article 'al-' loses its 'a' sound after 'li-' and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's initial n (hence the doubled 'nn'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition.

5.meaning: 'And He sent down / caused to descend'. It denotes bringing something down from a higher place to a lower one — characteristically the sending down of revelation. Past tense, third person masculine singular.
5.grammar: 'wa-' is the connector 'and'. 'anzala' is a past-tense verb of the causative pattern (form IV) meaning 'to make descend / send down', with the third-person masculine singular subject ('he') built in; the final '-a' is the standard past-tense ending.
5.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, send down

6.meaning: The Criterion: that which decisively separates and distinguishes truth from falsehood, right from wrong. A name applied to divine revelation in its role as a clear standard of discernment.
6.grammar: A verbal noun on the fuʿlān pattern, expressing the act or means of separating and distinguishing, here taking on the sense of a standard of judgment. The definite article al- marks it as the well-known one. The final -a ending is accusative, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb or a word governed by certain particles.

7.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
7.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

8.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
8.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

9.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

10.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
10.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
10.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
12.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

13.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
13.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

14.meaning: Severe, intense, harsh, or mighty in force. Describes something powerful and unrelenting in its strength or rigor.
14.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting a firmly established quality (intensity, severity). The final -un ending combines the nominative case (used for the subject or a predicate describing who/what something is) with nunation (the -n sound), which marks the word as indefinite, i.e. 'a severe one' rather than 'the severe one'.
14.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, firm, severe

15.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
15.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
15.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

16.meaning: Mighty, invincible, and supremely honoured; one who possesses overwhelming power and dignity such that none can overcome or resist Him. As a divine descriptor it conveys unassailable might joined with exalted worth.
16.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as a predicate describing something ("is mighty").

17.meaning: Owner of / possessor of / endowed with — a word that does not stand alone but means 'the one who has' whatever noun follows it, ascribing that quality or possession to someone.

parts.en: possessor of, owner of, endowed with

17.grammar: A possessive noun meaning 'owner/possessor of', always followed by another noun in the genitive. The final -ū form here is the nominative case, used when this word names the subject or is the thing being described; it inherently requires a following noun to complete its sense ('owner OF …').
17.root: — (no triliteral root; an irregular noun of possession)

18.meaning: Retribution, requital, or just vengeance: the act of exacting due penalty for wrongdoing. It carries the sense of a rightful, measured response to offense rather than arbitrary revenge.
18.grammar: A verbal noun of the eighth verb form (the iftiʿāl pattern), naming the action of exacting requital. The final -in ending combines the genitive case (used after prepositions, after an oath, or to link a word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship) with nunation (the -n sound), which marks it as indefinite.
18.root: ن-ق-م (n-q-m) — to avenge, exact penalty, requite

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: To be hidden, concealed, or unseen; to remain out of sight or knowledge. The verb describes something escaping notice or being kept from view.
4.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he' or 'it'). The verb ends in a fixed final long vowel -ā (a 'weak' final-letter verb), and in this prefixed present form it conveys an ongoing or general action: 'is/remains hidden'.
4.root: خ-ف-ي (kh-f-y) — to be hidden, concealed, unseen

5.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
5.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

6.meaning: A thing, something, anything — an indefinite term for any item, matter, or entity, however small. In negations it yields the sense 'nothing at all'.
6.grammar: The final -un (an 'n'-sound called nunation) marks the noun as indefinite — 'a thing / some thing' rather than 'the thing' — and the -u within it is the nominative case, typically the subject form.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
8.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

9.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
11.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: To form, fashion, shape, or give a figure to. The verb conveys deliberate, detailed crafting of a thing's shape and features, combined here with an object 'you (plural)'.
3.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of the intensive second form (which adds the sense of careful, repeated shaping). The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the -u on the stem is the indicative ending of the ongoing present tense. The attached -kum is an object pronoun meaning 'you' (plural), the ones being shaped.
3.root: ص-و-ر (ṣ-w-r) — to form, shape, fashion, give figure

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: The wombs; by extension, ties of kinship and blood relationship. The plural of the noun for the womb, often evoking the bonds among relatives.
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun on the afʿāl pattern, made definite by the article al-. The final -i ending is genitive, the case typically used after a preposition, after an oath, or to link the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

6.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
6.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

7.meaning: "He wills / wishes / desires" — denotes an act of will or volition, the choosing of something. As an ongoing/present-tense verb it expresses willing as a continuous, sovereign act.
7.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'he' form. The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('he wills').

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
9.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
9.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

10.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
10.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

11.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
11.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

12.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
12.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

13.meaning: The All-Wise — one possessing perfect wisdom, who puts everything in its right place and acts with flawless judgment; can also carry the sense of one who decrees and decides soundly.
13.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) stressing the depth and constancy of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a describing predicate.
13.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, to be wise

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
3.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

4.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

5.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
5.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

6.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
6.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
6.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

7.meaning: Signs, tokens, or evidences; also the discrete verses of revelation. Each is a clear indicator pointing to a greater truth or to its divine source.
7.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun. The ending -tun consists of the feminine plural marker -āt together with the nominative case (used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing who/what something is) and nunation (the -n sound) marking it as indefinite ('signs', not 'the signs').

8.meaning: Made firm, clear, and precise; perfectly settled and unambiguous. Describes statements whose meaning is fixed and free of confusion.
8.grammar: A passive participle of the fourth verb form (one that has been made firm/precise), here in the sound feminine plural. The ending -tun combines the feminine plural marker -āt with the nominative case (for a subject or descriptive predicate) and nunation (the -n sound) marking it as indefinite.
8.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to be firm, wise; to judge, make precise

9.meaning: 'They / them' — the detached subject pronoun for a group of females, standing on its own to mean 'they (feminine)' or to emphasize the female group as the topic.
9.grammar: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' for a group of females. Because it is a separate word, it normally serves as the subject of a sentence or gives emphasis ('they themselves'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

10.meaning: Mother; and by extension the source, origin, or foundation from which other things derive. Conveys the idea of an original, governing basis to which the rest is referred.
10.grammar: A noun whose final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate identifying who/what something is. Without nunation, it reads as definite or as the first term of a possessive ('mother/foundation OF …'), being joined to a following noun.
10.root: أ-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — to head toward; source, origin, mother

11.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
11.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

12.meaning: And others; further ones besides those mentioned. A plural word referring to additional, different items of the same kind.
12.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a plural noun/adjective meaning 'others'. It belongs to a class of words that are 'diptote' (they resist nunation), so it ends in a plain -u without the -n sound; that final -u marks the nominative case, used for a subject or a predicate describing who/what something is.
12.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to come after; other, latter

13.meaning: Resembling one another; ambiguous because of mutual likeness. Describes things so alike that their precise meaning is not immediately distinct and can be understood in more than one way.
13.grammar: An active participle of the sixth verb form (which conveys a mutual or reciprocal action — resembling one another), in the sound feminine plural. The ending -tun combines the feminine plural marker -āt with the nominative case (for a subject or descriptive predicate) and nunation (the -n sound) marking it indefinite.
13.root: ش-ب-ه (sh-b-h) — to resemble, be similar, be ambiguous

14.meaning: 'Then as for …' A connective opening that introduces and singles out a topic for comment, often paired later with a response. The fa- means 'then/so,' and 'ammā' sets up 'as for (such-and-such)…' to highlight one case among others.
14.grammar: A connector fa- ('then, so') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā introduces a subject for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that gives the comment about it. Neither part takes case endings.
14.root: — (particles; no root)

15.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
15.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
16.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

17.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the plural of qalb ('heart'), joined to the pronoun 'their'. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' (qalb) is the seat of understanding, intention, faith, and feeling, not merely the physical organ.
17.grammar: Qulūb is the broken (irregular) plural of qalb, 'hearts'. The -i ending is genitive: here it appears because the noun follows a preposition and because it is possessed by an attached pronoun. The suffix -him means 'their' (a masculine plural group), and its -i- vowel matches the preceding genitive ending. So the whole means 'hearts belonging to them'.
17.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about, change

18.meaning: A swerving or deviation: a turning away from what is straight and true, especially an inclination of the heart toward crookedness or doubt.
18.grammar: A verbal noun naming the act of swerving from straightness. The final -un ending combines the nominative case (used for the subject of a sentence or a descriptive predicate) with nunation (the -n sound), marking the word as indefinite ('a deviation').
18.root: ز-ي-غ (z-y-gh) — to swerve, deviate, turn aside

19.meaning: Then/so they follow, pursue, or go after; to take something as a thing to be imitated or adhered to. The verb implies actively following on behind and conforming to it.
19.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of the eighth form (which adds a sense of personally taking up the action of following). The opening fa- means 'so/then', linking it to what precedes. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the -ūna ending is the indicative form used for an ongoing, unconditioned present action.
19.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, pursue, come after

20.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
20.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

21.meaning: It resembled or was alike; it became mutually similar (and so ambiguous). The verb expresses two or more things being like one another to the point of being hard to tell apart.
21.grammar: A past/perfect verb of the sixth form, which conveys a mutual or reciprocal action — being alike to one another. The final -a marks a completed action with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he' or 'it'). The perfect tense presents the action as a finished whole.
21.root: ش-ب-ه (sh-b-h) — to resemble, be similar, be ambiguous

22.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
22.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
22.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

23.meaning: Seeking, earnestly pursuing, desiring to attain — the act of going after something diligently. As a verbal noun it means 'a seeking / out of desire for.'

parts.en: seeking / earnest pursuit (the final -a is the accusative case ending, here expressing purpose/motive)

23.grammar: A verbal noun (the 'act of seeking') in the accusative case, shown by the final -a. In this role the accusative commonly expresses purpose or motive — 'out of a desire for / in seeking.' It is built on a Form VIII pattern conveying earnest, deliberate pursuit.
23.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after something

24.meaning: Trial, temptation, and discord: a testing affliction that puts faith and loyalty to the proof, and the strife or sedition that can result from it. A heavily loaded term spanning persecution, civil strife, and seductive enticement away from truth.
24.grammar: A feminine noun made definite by the article al-. The final -i (on the feminine ending) is genitive, the case typically used after a preposition, after an oath, or to link the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
24.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — to test by fire/trial; to tempt, afflict

25.meaning: And the seeking, desiring, or pursuit of something: actively striving after a goal. A verbal noun denoting the act of looking for and wanting.
25.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a verbal noun of the eighth form, naming the act of seeking. The final -a ending is accusative, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb or to express purpose ('out of / seeking'); it can also follow certain particles.
25.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after

26.meaning: Its interpretation, ultimate meaning, or final outcome: tracing a thing back to what it really signifies or to how it ultimately turns out. The '-its' refers to a masculine singular thing being interpreted.
26.grammar: A verbal noun of the second form (denoting the act of carrying a matter back to its origin or true sense), with an attached possessive pronoun -hi ('its/his'). The -i before the pronoun is the genitive case, used after prepositions, after an oath, or in an 'of' relationship; the pronoun also takes the -i vowel form when it follows that genitive ending.
26.root: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to return, trace back to origin; interpret

27.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
27.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
27.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

28.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
28.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
28.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

29.meaning: Its interpretation, ultimate meaning, or final outcome: tracing a thing back to what it really signifies or to how it ultimately turns out. The '-its' refers to a masculine singular thing being interpreted.
29.grammar: A verbal noun of the second form (the act of carrying a matter back to its origin or true sense), with an attached possessive pronoun -hu ('its/his'). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative case, typically marking the direct object of a verb or a word governed by certain particles; the pronoun keeps its base -hu form after that -a vowel.
29.root: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to return, trace back to origin; interpret

30.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
30.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

31.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
31.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

32.meaning: And those firmly grounded; the ones deeply rooted and well-established (especially in knowledge). Describes people whose footing in something is secure and unshakeable.
32.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the definite article al- (whose l, the lām of the article, assimilates into the following r, a 'solar' letter) on a sound masculine plural active participle ('those who are firmly rooted'). The plural ending -ūna is the nominative form, used when the plural noun is the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing who someone is.
32.root: ر-س-خ (r-s-kh) — to be firmly rooted, deeply established

33.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
33.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

34.meaning: The knowledge; sure and certain knowing, established information and understanding (with the definite article).
34.grammar: A definite verbal noun: al- means 'the'. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship. It denotes knowledge as a settled, certain thing.

35.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
35.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

36.meaning: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
36.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.

37.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
37.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

38.meaning: A noun meaning 'all,' 'each,' 'every,' or 'the whole.' It denotes totality — that the entirety of a group or thing is included.
38.grammar: A noun in the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (the -un ending), which marks it as indefinite and as the subject or doer of a sentence. Standing alone with tanwīn it carries the sense 'everyone / all of them' as an independent subject.

39.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
39.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

40.meaning: 'In the presence of / from with / from the side of' — a noun of place and source meaning nearness or 'with,' used for what is in someone's keeping, possession, or vicinity, and figuratively what proceeds from them.
40.grammar: An adverbial noun meaning 'at / with / in the presence of,' here in the genitive case (the -i ending), as happens when it follows a preposition or links to a following noun ('the presence OF …'). It typically expresses 'from the side of' or 'in the keeping of' someone.
40.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — being at, near, or with; presence and proximity

41.meaning: Our Lord, Master, and Sustainer: the One who owns, governs, nurtures, and brings to completion. Rabb combines ownership, authority, and loving cultivation of what He sustains; the '-our' joins the speakers to Him as those under His care.
41.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Master, Sustainer') with the attached possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). The -i before the pronoun is the genitive case, used after a preposition, after a calling/oath, or to link the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
41.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, own

42.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
42.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

43.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'he is mindful, takes heed, calls (it) to mind' — to reflect and let oneself be reminded, taking a lesson to heart.
43.grammar: Present/future verb of a reflexive pattern (originally yatadhakkaru, with the t assimilated into the following letter, giving the doubled dh). The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'); the doubling and pattern convey doing the action to/for oneself — i.e. letting oneself be reminded. The final -u is the indicative ending, the default for an ongoing or habitual statement.
43.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

44.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
44.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

45.meaning: 'Possessors of / owners of / people of' — a plural construct word meaning those endowed with or characterized by whatever follows it (e.g. 'those of understanding'). It has no singular of its own form and is always joined to a following noun.
45.grammar: A masculine plural noun used only in the construct state (always followed by another noun, 'possessors OF ...'). The -ū ending is the nominative plural form, marking it as the subject or doer of a sentence. The trailing alif is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
45.root: — (a word for 'possessors of', having no verbal root)

46.meaning: The kernels, cores, or innermost parts — figuratively the faculties of sound reason and understanding, the discerning intellect that grasps the heart of a matter. The prefixed "al-" makes it definite ("the").
46.grammar: A definite plural noun (singular "lubb"). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… OF …") or follows a preposition. Here the genitive marks it as the thing possessed after a possessor-word.

1.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

1.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
1.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: To cause to swerve or deviate; to make a heart turn away from straightness and truth. The transitive counterpart of swerving — making something incline toward crookedness.
3.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of the fourth (causative) form, meaning 'to make (something) swerve'. The tu- prefix marks a second-person singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The stem ends in a vowelless final consonant (jussive/clipped mood), the form that typically follows a negating or requesting particle such as 'do not …'.
3.root: ز-ي-غ (z-y-gh) — to swerve, deviate, turn aside

4.meaning: Our hearts. The base noun is the plural of qalb, the heart, understood not merely as the physical organ but as the seat of understanding, intention, feeling, and faith — the inner core of a person. With the attached possessive it means 'our hearts'.
4.grammar: A plural noun carrying the -a (accusative) ending, which generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb or the subject of certain particles. The suffix -nā is a possessive pronoun meaning 'our' when attached to a noun (and 'us' when attached to a verb or preposition).
4.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over, turn about; hence 'heart' as that which turns and fluctuates

5.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
5.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
5.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

7.meaning: You have guided us. From a verb meaning to guide, to lead rightly, to show the way — especially guidance toward truth and right conduct. The form expresses a completed act of guiding directed by 'You' (a single addressee) toward 'us'.
7.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb denoting a completed action. The -ta ending marks the doer as 'you' (a single masculine person being addressed). The suffix -nā here is the object 'us', so the whole says 'You guided us'.
7.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead to the right way

8.meaning: Grant! Bestow! A command from a verb meaning to give freely as a gift, to bestow without expectation of return. It conveys pure, gratuitous giving rather than payment or exchange.
8.grammar: An imperative (command) addressed to a single person, asking them to give freely. The bare consonantal ending with a vowelless final letter is typical of the command form of this verb. The prefixed wa- means 'and', linking it to what precedes.
8.root: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — to give freely, to bestow as a gift

9.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
9.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: From Yourself; from Your presence. The base word ladun means 'the presence of', 'the side of', or 'directly from' — pointing to something issuing straight from a source. Here it is preceded by the preposition min ('from'), whose final n assimilates into the following l so that the l is doubled. With the attached pronoun the whole conveys 'from Your own presence', stressing that what is given comes directly from the giver.

parts.en: from (preposition; its n merges into the following l)
presence / nearness / 'from with' (doubled l from the merged n)

11.grammar: An adverb of place/source ('at, by, in the presence of') joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'your/you' for a single masculine addressee, together conveying 'from Your presence'. The initial l is written with a shadda (doubled): this gemination results from the preceding preposition min, whose final n assimilates into the l. The word implies immediacy of source — something coming directly from the one referred to.
11.root: — (an adverbial particle of place; no triliteral verbal root)

12.meaning: Mercy: compassion that actively does good — tenderness joined with the will and power to relieve, forgive, and benefit. As a noun it names an instance or measure of such mercy.
12.grammar: An indefinite noun with the -an (accusative) ending, marked by tanwīn (the doubled-n sound). The accusative generally signals the word is a direct object or otherwise governed; the tanwīn marks it as indefinite — 'a mercy', 'some mercy'.

13.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
13.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

14.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
14.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

15.meaning: The Bestower; the One who gives lavishly and repeatedly. An intensive form built from the verb 'to give freely', describing one whose giving is abundant, habitual, and generous without limit.
15.grammar: A definite noun (with 'the') in an intensive pattern that denotes one who does an action abundantly or by nature — here, one who gives lavishly. The final -u is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or as a predicate naming the subject.
15.root: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — to give freely, to bestow as a gift

1.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

1.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
1.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

2.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
2.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

3.meaning: Gatherer; the one who gathers, assembles, and brings together what was scattered. An active participle — a noun describing the doer of the act of gathering.
3.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) meaning 'one who gathers'. The final -u is the nominative ending, typically marking a subject or predicate. Such a participle can also link to a following noun in a possessive-like construction ('gatherer of …'), in which case it conveys an act about to happen or characteristically done.
3.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — to gather, collect, bring together

4.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
4.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
4.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

5.meaning: For a day; toward a day. The noun yawm means 'day' — a defined period or appointed time, often a momentous occasion. With the prefixed particle it means 'for / to / on a day', pointing toward an appointed time.
5.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition li- ('for, to'). Because it follows a preposition, it takes the -i (genitive) ending, here with tanwīn (the doubled-n sound) marking it indefinite: '-in' = 'for a day'. The genitive is the case regularly required after prepositions.
5.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

6.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
6.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

7.meaning: Doubt, suspicion, disquieting uncertainty — the kind of wavering that unsettles the heart, stronger than a passing question. It names the state of not being at rest about whether something is true.
7.grammar: A masculine singular noun shown with an -a ending and no tanwin. This is the accusative (mansub) noun governed by the negating particle la — its ism — taking a bare form to express absolute negation, conveying that the whole category is ruled out ('there is no doubt whatsoever').

8.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

9.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
9.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

11.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

12.meaning: He breaks / fails to keep (a promise); He goes back on or leaves unfulfilled. From a verb whose core sense is 'to come after / be left behind', in this form meaning to default on a pledge or fail to deliver what was promised.
12.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The yu- prefix marks the doer as 'he' (third-person masculine singular) and, in this vowel pattern, indicates a causative-type form. The final -u is the indicative ending, which marks the plain factual present ('he does / will do'), as opposed to moods that drop or change that vowel.
12.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, succeed, be behind; hence to break a promise (leave it behind unfulfilled)

13.meaning: The appointment / the appointed promise or time; a fixed tryst — a settled commitment as to when (or where) something will occur. It names the promised meeting or deadline itself.
13.grammar: A definite noun (with 'the') on a pattern denoting the time, place, or instrument of an action — here the appointed time/promise. The final -a is the accusative ending, generally marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
13.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, to appoint a time

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
4.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

5.meaning: To avail / to be of use / to ward off need; from a verb meaning to enrich or make independent, hence 'to be of any benefit' or 'to suffice (someone) against' a threat — typically used to deny that something can help at all.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb in the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a on the stem-vowel (-iya). The tu- prefix marks the doer as 'it/she' (third-person feminine singular) or a second-person 'you'. The subjunctive typically appears after particles meaning 'that', 'so that', or 'will not', expressing a non-factual, hoped-for, or negated action rather than a plain statement.
5.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient; hence to avail/suffice

6.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
6.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

7.meaning: Their wealth / their possessions. The base noun amwāl is the plural of māl, meaning property, wealth, goods, or money — anything owned of value. With the attached pronoun it means 'their wealth'.
7.grammar: A plural noun with the -u (nominative) ending, which generally marks it as the subject of a sentence or a predicate. The attached pronoun -hum means 'their' (a group, grammatically masculine plural) when joined to a noun.
7.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property, to be wealthy

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: Their children / their offspring. The base noun awlād is the plural of walad, meaning a child or offspring (son or, broadly, descendant). With the attached pronoun it means 'their children'.
9.grammar: A plural noun with the -u (nominative) ending, generally marking it as a subject or predicate. The attached pronoun -hum means 'their' (a group, grammatically masculine plural) when joined to a noun.
9.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; hence child, offspring

10.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
10.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
12.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

13.meaning: 'And those' — the connective 'and' joined to the demonstrative 'those'. It both links to what precedes and points out a group ('and it is those who…').
13.grammar: A connecting particle wa ('and') prefixed to a plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. The wa simply joins what follows to what came before. The demonstrative is fixed in form (no case endings), and its -ka element marks distance; it may refer to people of either gender.

14.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
14.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

15.meaning: Fuel — the material that feeds a fire, the kindling and combustible matter by which a blaze is made to burn.
15.grammar: A noun with the -u (nominative) ending, which generally marks the word as the subject of a sentence or as a predicate naming the subject. It can also stand as the first term of a possessive pairing ('fuel of …').
15.root: و-ق-د (w-q-d) — to kindle, catch fire, blaze

16.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
16.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

1.meaning: Like the way / like the habitual practice (of someone). Daʾb means a settled custom, persistent habit, or characteristic manner of acting. With the prefixed particle of comparison it means 'like the manner/custom of …'.

parts.tr: daʾb (hamza often unwritten in transliteration as 'dab')

1.grammar: A noun preceded by the particle ka- ('like, as'). Because ka- functions like a preposition, the noun takes the -i (genitive) ending. The classical form has a hamza as its middle radical (dāl-hamza-bāʾ), so the careful pronunciation is 'daʾb' (full form ka-daʾb-i); simplified transliterations often drop the hamza and write it as 'dab' (ka-dab-i), but the hamza is a genuine sound of the word. The genitive is the case that follows prepositions and also links a noun to a following noun in a possessive sense ('the custom OF …').
1.root: د-أ-ب (d-ʾ-b) — to persist, toil habitually; hence a settled custom or habit

2.meaning: The family, folk, or close people of someone — those belonging to a person's household, following, or kin.
2.grammar: A singular collective noun in the genitive (-i ending), which typically links it to a following noun ('the folk OF …') or follows a preposition. It points to those associated with a named person.
2.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, kinsfolk (āl is derived from ahl by elision of the hāʾ)

3.meaning: Pharaoh — the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name for that figure.
3.grammar: A proper name. Being a foreign, non-inflecting (diptote) name, it takes a single -a for both the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn. Here it follows another noun in a possessive link ('… of Pharaoh').

4.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
4.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
6.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
6.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

7.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

7.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
7.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

8.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
8.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.
8.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, token, mark

9.meaning: So He seized them / took hold of them. From a verb meaning to take, grasp, or seize — often forcibly, as in gripping or punishing. The form expresses a completed seizing by 'He' of 'them', introduced by 'so/then' to mark consequence.
9.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb denoting a completed act. The bare -a on the stem marks the doer as 'he' (third-person masculine singular). The attached -hum(u) is the object 'them'; its final vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before a following word. The prefixed fa- means 'so/then', signalling result or sequence.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
10.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

11.meaning: For/because of their sins. Dhunūb is the plural of dhanb — a sin, fault, or offense; a wrongdoing that incurs blame. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'because of / for their sins'.
