18.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, to guide, to show the way

19.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
19.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

20.meaning: 'They turned away / they turned their backs / they turned aside'. It conveys turning oneself away from something, often implying rejection or withdrawal.
20.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine plural: the ending '-aw' means 'they (did) …'. The Form V pattern (with the 'ta-' prefix and doubled middle letter) gives a reflexive sense — turning oneself away. It states a completed act.
20.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near/turn toward; in this form, to turn away

21.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
21.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

22.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
22.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

23.meaning: The conveying / the delivering (of a message): the act of passing on and communicating something so it reaches its hearers fully and clearly; a verbal noun naming that act.
23.grammar: A definite verbal noun (a noun naming an action) with the prefixed article 'al-' ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('… is …').
23.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, to arrive at; to convey

24.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
24.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
24.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

25.meaning: 'All-Seeing / fully observant' — one who sees clearly and with complete insight; as a divine attribute, the One who perceives all things.
25.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting one who possesses sight to a high degree — 'all-seeing'. The -un ending (tanwīn) is nominative plus indefiniteness, the form used for a subject or for a predicate ('[He] is all-seeing').

26.meaning: With/of the servants (of Allah): 'with' or 'as to' joined to a word for human beings as the worshipping servants and creatures of Allah, wholly belonging to and dependent on Him.
26.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the servants') with the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('with / as to') and article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case ending, which is required after a preposition such as 'bi-'.
26.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, to worship; servitude

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieve / reject faith', or more literally 'they cover over (the truth), they are ungrateful'. An ongoing or habitual rejection and denial.
3.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a masculine plural 'they' acting now or habitually; the final -na (kept, not dropped) shows the verb is in its plain indicative form, stating an ongoing fact.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — covering over; hence disbelief and ingratitude

4.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
4.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
4.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: 'And they kill / slay'. Joins wa- ('and') to a present-tense verb of killing, expressed as ongoing or habitual action by a group.
6.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb preceded by wa- ('and'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks a masculine plural 'they' acting now or habitually; the retained -na shows the plain indicative form, simply asserting the action.

7.meaning: 'The prophets' — those whom Allah selects to receive revelation and convey His message. The plural of nabī, a prophet who brings news from Allah.
7.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the genitive-or-accusative case — the form used when the noun is a direct object or governed by a preposition, as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject.
7.root: ن-ب-ء (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; hence a prophet who brings news from Allah

8.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
8.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
8.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

9.meaning: Truth / right / a just claim: that which is real, true, and rightfully due — what genuinely is the case, and what is owed by justice. As an indefinite noun it means 'a right' or 'rightfully', with no article.
9.grammar: An indefinite noun. The ending -in carries two signals at once: the final -n (called nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a right', not 'the right'), and the -i vowel is the genitive case, the case used after prepositions or to link one noun to another ('… of …').
9.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, what is due/right

10.meaning: And they kill / and they keep killing: 'and' joined to the act of killing or slaying, done by a group as an ongoing or repeated action.
10.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb (Form I) meaning 'to kill', joined by 'wa-' ('and'). The 'ya-…-ūna' frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) shows the verb is in its plain, unrestricted present-tense state, expressing ongoing or habitual action.

11.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
11.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

12.meaning: They command / they enjoin: a group ordering, commanding, or urging that something be done, as an ongoing or habitual action.
12.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb (Form I) meaning 'to command' or 'to enjoin'. The 'ya-…-ūna' frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the full -ūna ending shows the plain, unrestricted present tense, expressing ongoing or habitual action.
12.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, to order; a matter/affair

13.meaning: In/with justice and equity — 'qisṭ' is fair, balanced dealing: giving each their due in full measure, without wronging anyone.
13.grammar: A masculine noun ('justice, equity') governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('in/with') and made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

14.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
14.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

15.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
15.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
15.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

16.meaning: Then give them glad tidings / then announce to them: a command to one person to bring news to a group, joined by 'then/so'. The verb's core sense is announcing news that visibly moves the hearer — usually good news, but the form can carry news of any kind.
16.grammar: A command (imperative) verb of the intensive pattern (Form II), addressed to a single person: 'announce / give tidings!'. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'then/so'. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them'.
16.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — glad tidings; (the skin's) glow of joy

17.meaning: With/of a punishment: 'with' joined to a word for a chastisement, torment, or penalty inflicted as recompense; indefinite ('a punishment').
17.grammar: An indefinite noun with the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('with / of'). The ending -in does two things: the final -n (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a punishment'), and the -i vowel is the genitive case required after the preposition 'bi-'.

18.meaning: Painful / agonizing: causing intense pain; said of something that grieves and torments deeply. An intensive adjective, so 'sorely painful'. Indefinite ('a painful …').
18.grammar: An indefinite adjective on an intensive pattern (conveying 'deeply/sorely painful'). The ending -in shows both indefiniteness (the final -n, nunation: 'a painful one') and the genitive case (the -i vowel), the case that an adjective takes to match a genitive noun it describes or that follows a preposition.
18.root: ا-ل-م (ʾ-l-m) — pain, to feel pain

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: It came to nothing / became void / was wasted — of deeds, to be rendered worthless and to lose all reward.

parts.en: to come to nothing / be nullified

3.grammar: A past-tense verb describing a completed event. The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject ('it/she'), used because the thing that becomes void (e.g. 'deeds') is grammatically feminine. The root pictures effort that swells up and then bursts into nothing.
3.root: ح-ب-ط (ḥ-b-ṭ) — coming to nothing, nullification of works

4.meaning: Their deeds / works / actions — the things they have done.
4.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'deed', meaning 'deeds/works'. The attached -hum means 'their' (masculine plural), forming a possessive link. The -u before the pronoun is nominative, marking the whole phrase ('their deeds') as a subject. The -hum form keeps its u-vowel after this nominative ending.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
6.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
6.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

7.meaning: And the Hereafter / and the next life: 'and' joined to 'the latter (abode)' — the life and final, lasting world that comes after this present one. From a root meaning 'last/later', it is the counterpart to this world (al-dunyā).
7.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the latter / the Hereafter') with conjunction 'wa-' ('and') and article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case ending, the case used after prepositions or to link one noun to another ('… of …').
7.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after; the end

8.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
8.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

9.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

11.meaning: Helpers / supporters: those who give aid, support, and victory to another, standing by them against an adversary; the plural of 'helper'.
11.grammar: A masculine plural active participle — a 'doer' word meaning 'ones who help'. The sound plural ending -īna marks more than two; this -īna form (rather than -ūna) is the case used for objects of verbs and after prepositions or in possession (the accusative/genitive).
11.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to give victory/support

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
5.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
5.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

6.meaning: A portion / a share / an allotted part: a fixed amount or lot assigned to someone — what falls to them as their due share. Indefinite ('a portion').
6.grammar: An indefinite noun. The ending -an does two things at once: the final -n (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a portion'), and the -a vowel is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or specifies amount/respect.
6.root: ن-ص-ب (n-ṣ-b) — to set up/allot; a fixed share/portion

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
8.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.
8.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — writing, inscribing, recording

9.meaning: They are called / they are invited / they are summoned: a group being called upon, invited, or summoned by another — the action falls upon them rather than being done by them.
9.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb in the passive voice ('they are being called/invited') — built on the pattern 'yu-…' with an inner vowel shift that signals the doer is unnamed and the subject receives the action. The -awna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); its 'aw' shape arises because the root's final weak letter blends into the plural ending.
9.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to summon, to invite; to supplicate

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
10.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

11.meaning: A scripture or book; in particular a written revelation. The word denotes something written down and consigned to record — a 'Book' in the sense of a divinely sent, recorded scripture, also carrying the broader sense of a binding decree or anything set down in writing.
11.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -i ending is genitive (the 'of' case): it typically marks the word as linked to a following noun ('… OF …'), or as governed by a preceding preposition or oath particle.

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: 'So that he may judge / decide / rule'. It denotes deciding between parties, passing judgement, and governing by a rule or verdict. Present tense, third person masculine singular, introduced by 'so that / in order to'.
13.grammar: The prefix 'li-' means 'so that' or 'in order to', expressing purpose. The 'ya-' marks a present-tense action by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). Because of the purpose particle, the verb takes the subjunctive '-a' ending, used for intended or hoped-for actions ('that he may …').
13.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, govern, wisdom

14.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
14.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
14.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

15.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
15.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

16.meaning: He turns away, turns his back, or takes charge by turning aside — to avert oneself from something, withdraw allegiance, or shift one's loyalty elsewhere. The form conveys a deliberate turning of one's whole self away.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reflexive/intensive (form V) pattern. The prefix complex yata- marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and carries the form V marker; the doubled-stem wallā is built on the root. The long -ā ending reflects the weak final root letter and is the present-tense form of this defective verb ('he turns away').
16.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, allegiance, turning toward/charge over

17.meaning: A group, party, or faction — a portion or section of people set apart from a larger body.
17.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The '-un' (tanwīn) marks it indefinite ('a group') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence.
17.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide; a division

18.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
18.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

19.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
19.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

20.meaning: Ones who turn away, who avert themselves and refuse — people who deliberately turn their faces and backs away, declining and shunning what is presented to them.
20.grammar: An active participle (a doer-noun: 'ones who turn away') from a verb meaning 'to turn aside / avert oneself'. The 'mu-' prefix marks the doer of this verb-pattern. The -ūna ending marks the masculine-plural nominative case — typically the subject of a sentence or what something is being described as.
20.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — to be wide, present sideways; (this pattern) to turn away, avert oneself

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
1.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

2.meaning: A connector meaning 'because they…' or 'by reason that they…'. It fuses the preposition bi- (here giving a cause, 'because of') with anna ('that', an emphatic particle introducing a fact) and the attached pronoun -hum ('they').
2.grammar: bi- here gives a causal sense ('because of'). anna is an emphatic particle meaning 'that' which introduces a statement of fact and takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; the attached -hum is that pronoun, a masculine plural 'they'. Together they give a reason: 'because they …'.

3.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

4.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
4.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

5.meaning: It will touch us / it touches us — for something to make contact with, reach, or afflict 'us'; 'touch' here often carries the sense of being struck or affected by something (such as harm or fire).
5.grammar: Present-tense verb with the 'ta-' prefix marking a feminine singular subject ('it/she'). The attached '-nā' is the object pronoun 'us'. The final '-a' on 'massa' is the inherent stem vowel of this doubled (geminate) root م-س-س in the present tense, not a mood marker; with the object pronoun attached directly there is no separate spot for a case/mood ending.

6.meaning: The Fire — a definite noun for fire; frequently the term for the blazing punishment of the Hereafter (Hell).
6.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', heard as 'an-nār'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

7.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
7.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

8.meaning: Days — the plural of 'day'; a span of days, a period of time.
8.grammar: 'ayyām' is the plural of 'yawm' (day). The '-an' ending (nunation) is indefinite accusative; on a noun of time it often functions adverbially, expressing duration — 'for (a number of) days'.
8.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day

9.meaning: Counted out, numbered, a limited tally — describing things few enough to be reckoned and therefore finite and soon ended. The sense is of a fixed, countable quantity rather than something boundless.
9.grammar: A passive participle (meaning 'counted / numbered') in the sound feminine plural, agreeing with a feminine plural noun. The -āt is the feminine plural ending; the final -in (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('some numbered ones') and in the genitive case, typical after a preposition or as a description of a genitive noun.

10.meaning: And it deluded them / led them astray — to deceive by false hope or vain confidence, to lull someone into a misleading sense of security. The verb names the act of beguiling a person with empty assurance.
10.grammar: Past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it deceived'), with the prefixed 'and' (wa-) and the attached object pronoun -hum ('them'). The bare past-tense stem with no subject suffix indicates a single masculine (or neuter 'it') subject acting in completed time.

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

12.meaning: Their way of life, religion, or binding code — dīn denotes the whole system of belief, obedience, judgment and recompense by which one lives and to which one is answerable. It carries at once the senses of religion, divine law, accountability and requital.
12.grammar: A masculine noun with the attached possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here triggered because the word is possessed (in a possessive construction) or governed by a preposition. The pronoun -him refers to a masculine/mixed plural ('their').
12.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — debt, obligation, judgment, requital, religion

13.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
13.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

14.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
14.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

15.meaning: They fabricate or invent falsely — to forge a lie, concoct something untrue and attribute it where it does not belong. The verb specifically names inventing falsehood and slander out of nothing.
15.grammar: Present-tense verb in the (form VIII) pattern, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks the third person and, together with the -ūna ending, yields 'they' (masculine plural) acting in ongoing/present time. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative ('they are fabricating / they fabricate').

1.meaning: So how? / Then in what manner or state? — kayfa is the interrogative 'how', asking after the manner, condition or circumstance of something. With the prefixed 'so/then' it introduces a question following from what precedes, often expressing wonder or warning.
1.grammar: An interrogative particle ('how') carrying the connective prefix fa- ('so / then'), which links it to a preceding statement as a consequence or follow-up. As a particle, kayfa is indeclinable: its fixed final -a is not a case ending and does not change.

2.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

3.meaning: We gathered / assembled them — to bring scattered people or things together into one place or whole. The verb denotes collecting and uniting what was dispersed.
3.grammar: Past-tense verb, completed action. The suffix -nā marks the subject as 'we', and the attached -hum is the object 'them'. So the form means 'we gathered them' — the -nā ending is the first-person plural doer of a finished act.

4.meaning: For a day; toward a day. The noun yawm means 'day' — a defined period or appointed time, often a momentous occasion. With the prefixed particle it means 'for / to / on a day', pointing toward an appointed time.
4.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition li- ('for, to'). Because it follows a preposition, it takes the -i (genitive) ending, here with tanwīn (the doubled-n sound) marking it indefinite: '-in' = 'for a day'. The genitive is the case regularly required after prepositions.
4.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

5.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
5.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

6.meaning: Doubt, suspicion, disquieting uncertainty — the kind of wavering that unsettles the heart, stronger than a passing question. It names the state of not being at rest about whether something is true.
6.grammar: A masculine singular noun shown with an -a ending and no tanwin. This is the accusative (mansub) noun governed by the negating particle la — its ism — taking a bare form to express absolute negation, conveying that the whole category is ruled out ('there is no doubt whatsoever').

7.meaning: In it / within it / concerning it — the preposition fī ('in, inside, during, about') joined to a pronoun referring back to a masculine thing. It expresses being inside, present within, or in regard to that thing.
7.grammar: A preposition ('in / within') with the attached third-person masculine singular pronoun. Because it follows a preposition, the pronoun takes the -hi vowelling. The whole phrase functions adverbially, locating something inside or in connection with a masculine referent ('in it').

8.meaning: And it was paid in full / fully rendered — to discharge a due completely, giving every part of what is owed without shortfall. The (form II) passive stresses thoroughness: each soul or claim receives its full measure.
8.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (intensive form II), so the subject receives the action: 'it was paid in full'. The vowel pattern wuffiya marks it as passive and completed; the final -t (tāʾ) is the feminine ending, showing the subject is grammatically feminine singular ('it/she was fully repaid').
8.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — fulfilling, completing, paying in full

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'all, every, each, the whole of.' It expresses totality — when joined to a following noun it means 'every (one)' or 'the entirety of' that thing.
9.grammar: A noun of totality with the final -u ending (nominative). The -u typically marks it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It normally attaches to a following noun to mean 'every / all of' it.

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'soul, self, person, living being.' It denotes the inner self or the whole individual — the seat of life and identity, and by extension a 'person' as a single unit.
10.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a soul'). This form appears after prepositions or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun (such as 'every soul').
10.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being

11.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
11.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

12.meaning: 'It earned / acquired, gained' — said of deeds and their consequences; the root means to gain or acquire something, especially the moral 'earnings' of one's actions.
12.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it.' The past tense presents the action as completed.
12.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

13.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
13.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

14.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

15.meaning: They are wronged / treated unjustly — to suffer ẓulm, the placing of something out of its right place: injustice, oppression, being deprived of one's due. The passive form names being on the receiving end of wrongdoing.
15.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine plural. The yu- prefix (with the internal vowelling) marks the third person and the passive 'are being …', and the -ūna ending makes it 'they' (masculine plural) as the ones undergoing the action: 'they are wronged'. The -na is the indicative marker.

1.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.

2.meaning: O Allah — a vocative address to Allah. It is the divine name Allah with an added ending standing in place of the call-word 'O', so the whole word means 'O Allah' — an invocation calling directly upon Allah.
2.grammar: The proper name Allah used in direct address (vocative), with the suffixed -umma serving the function of the vocative 'O' that normally precedes a called noun. The word is fixed in this form for calling upon Allah ('O Allah').

3.meaning: Owner, master, sovereign — one who possesses full authority and control over something and disposes of it as he wills. Mālik denotes the rightful possessor and ruler, the one in whose hand a thing truly belongs.
3.grammar: An active participle ('one who owns / master'). The final -a ending here marks the accusative case, which is also the ending given to a called noun in a vocative phrase (the one being addressed). It signals the word as a direct object or as the addressee, rather than a subject.

4.meaning: The dominion, kingship, sovereign power — al-mulk is rule and possession on the grandest scale: the authority of a king, the realm ruled, and the very power to command and dispose. It denotes sovereignty itself.
4.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, typically marking it as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… OF the dominion') or as governed by a preceding preposition.

5.meaning: You give / You grant / You bring — to bestow or hand over something, and also to bring or bring forth. The (form IV) verb conveys the act of granting or conferring something upon someone.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb (causative form IV) addressed to a single masculine 'you'. The tu- prefix marks the second-person singular subject. The final long -ī reflects the weak last root letter ('you give / you grant'); it is the form this defective verb takes in the present.

6.meaning: 'The kingship / sovereignty / dominion' — royal authority and the power to rule and dispose of a realm; the office and possession of a king.
6.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb — the thing given, granted, or acted upon.

7.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
7.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

8.meaning: You will / You wish — to will, want, or choose that something be. Mashīʾa (the noun from this root) is sovereign volition; the verb names the act of willing or desiring a thing into being.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb addressed to a single masculine 'you'. The ta- prefix marks the second-person singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, the normal mood for a plain statement of fact ('you will / you wish').
8.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing, volition

9.meaning: And You strip away / pluck out / take away — to remove something by pulling it out, to wrest or take away what was attached or held. The verb conveys a forceful drawing-out or dispossession.
9.grammar: Present-tense verb addressed to a single masculine 'you', with the prefixed 'and' (wa-). The ta- prefix marks the second-person singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, used for a plain factual statement ('and you take away').
9.root: ن-ز-ع (n-z-ʿ) — pulling out, removing, wresting away

10.meaning: 'The kingship / sovereignty / dominion' — royal authority and the power to rule and dispose of a realm; the office and possession of a king.
10.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb — the thing given, granted, or acted upon.

11.meaning: A compound meaning 'than one who / than whoever' — combining the preposition of comparison 'than' with the relative pronoun 'who', used to compare a person against others.
11.grammar: The preposition 'min' (here 'than', used after elatives) followed by the indeclinable relative 'man' ('who'). The final nūn of 'min' undergoes regressive assimilation into the following mīm of 'man', producing a doubled mīm; the resulting shadda sits on the mīm of 'man'. Both words are indeclinable particles and take no case ending.

12.meaning: You will / You wish — to will, want, or choose that something be. Mashīʾa (the noun from this root) is sovereign volition; the verb names the act of willing or desiring a thing into being.
12.grammar: Present-tense verb addressed to a single masculine 'you'. The ta- prefix marks the second-person singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, the normal mood for a plain statement of fact ('you will / you wish').

13.meaning: And You give might / honor / strengthen — to make someone mighty, honored, and held dear, raising them to a position of strength and esteem. The (form IV) verb means to confer ʿizza — dignity and invincible might.
13.grammar: Present-tense verb (causative form IV) addressed to a single masculine 'you', with the prefixed 'and' (wa-). The tu- prefix marks the second-person singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending for a plain statement of fact ('and you honor / make mighty').

14.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
14.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
14.root: — (pronoun)

15.meaning: You will / You wish — to will, want, or choose that something be. Mashīʾa (the noun from this root) is sovereign volition; the verb names the act of willing or desiring a thing into being.
15.grammar: Present-tense verb addressed to a single masculine 'you'. The ta- prefix marks the second-person singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, the normal mood for a plain statement of fact ('you will / you wish').

16.meaning: And You abase / humble / bring low — to render someone lowly, weak and disgraced, the opposite of honoring. The (form IV) verb means to cast another into dhull — humiliation and subjection.
16.grammar: Present-tense verb (causative form IV) addressed to a single masculine 'you', with the prefixed 'and' (wa-). The tu- prefix marks the second-person singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending for a plain statement of fact ('and you abase / bring low').

17.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
17.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

18.meaning: You will / You wish — to will, want, or choose that something be. Mashīʾa (the noun from this root) is sovereign volition; the verb names the act of willing or desiring a thing into being.
18.grammar: Present-tense verb addressed to a single masculine 'you'. The ta- prefix marks the second-person singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, the normal mood for a plain statement of fact ('you will / you wish').
18.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing, volition

19.meaning: In Your hand — yad ('hand') joined to the preposition bi- ('in / by') and the possessive 'Your'. Idiomatically it denotes possession, power and control: that something rests entirely in another's authority and disposal.
19.grammar: The noun 'hand' governed by the preposition bi- ('in / by') and carrying the attached possessive -ka ('your', masculine singular). After the preposition the noun is genitive, shown by the -i vowel before the pronoun. The phrase works adverbially: 'in your hand', i.e. in your power.
19.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand, and figuratively power/control

20.meaning: The good / the best / what is beneficial — khayr denotes goodness, benefit, and that which is excellent and desirable; it can also mean wealth or abundance. With the article it points to good as a whole, all that is good.
20.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case, the ending typically given to the subject of a sentence or to the thing being described as existing/located somewhere ('the good [is] …').

21.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
21.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

22.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
22.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

23.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
23.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.
23.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

24.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
24.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
24.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

25.meaning: All-powerful, fully able, ever-capable — possessing complete and effective power to do whatever is willed; one whose ability never falls short.
25.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, abiding quality ('thoroughly able'). The final -un is the indefinite nominative (nunation) — the doubled-n shows no 'the', and the -u base vowel marks the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or a predicate ('… is all-powerful').

1.meaning: You make enter / cause to pass into / merge in — to insert one thing into another, to make something penetrate or be absorbed into it. The (form IV) verb conveys causing a thing to enter or interpenetrate, as one period of time merges into another.

parts.en: make enter / cause to pass in

1.grammar: Present-tense verb (causative form IV) addressed to a single masculine 'you'. The tu- prefix marks the second-person singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, used for a plain factual statement ('you cause to enter / you merge in').

2.meaning: The night — al-layl is the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; the dark portion of the day-night cycle, a time of covering, rest and stillness.
2.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case, the ending typically given to the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or used adverbially for time ('the night').

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The daytime — the bright span of hours when the sun is up, from dawn to sunset; the natural counterpart of night.
4.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the,' with its 'l' assimilated into the following 'n'). The final '-i' is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the day') or as following a preposition or a particle that governs the genitive.

5.meaning: You make (something) slip or merge into (something else) — to insert one thing within another, as daylight is folded into the span of night.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb in form IV (the causative pattern 'afʿala,' 'to make something enter'). The 'tu-' prefix marks a second-person 'you' (singular masculine) subject; the stem 'wlij' carries the three root letters w-l-j, and the long 'ū' heard at the start (tū-lij) arises from the prefix's 'u' vowel meeting the quiescent root-initial wāw — the wāw is a root consonant, not a stem vowel. The final '-u' is the indicative mood, the default form for a plain ongoing or habitual statement. Prefixed with 'wa' ('and').

6.meaning: The daytime — the bright span of hours when the sun is up, from dawn to sunset; the natural counterpart of night.
6.grammar: A definite singular noun ('al-' = 'the,' its 'l' assimilated into the following 'n'). The final '-a' is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or otherwise signals 'as / being' something.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: The night — the dark span of hours after sunset until dawn; the natural counterpart of day.
8.grammar: A definite singular noun ('al-' = 'the,' its 'l' assimilated into the following 'l'). The final '-i' is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the night') or as following a preposition or governing particle.
8.root: ل-ي-ل (l-y-l) — night, darkness

9.meaning: You bring forth, draw out, or produce (something) — to make a thing emerge or come out from its source or container.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb in form IV (the causative 'afʿala,' 'to make something come out'). The 'tu-' prefix marks a second-person 'you' (singular masculine) subject, and the final '-u' is the indicative mood, the plain form for an ongoing or habitual statement. Prefixed with 'wa' ('and').

10.meaning: The living — that which is alive, possessing life and vitality.
10.grammar: A definite noun/adjective ('al-' = 'the'). Because the following letter 'ḥ' is a 'moon letter,' the 'l' of 'al-' is fully pronounced and does NOT assimilate (al-ḥayy). The final '-a' is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

11.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
11.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

12.meaning: The dead — that which is lifeless, having lost or never possessed life.
12.grammar: A definite noun/adjective on the intensive pattern 'fayʿil' ('al-' = 'the,' its 'l' assimilated into the following 'm'). The final '-i' is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the dead') or as following a preposition or governing particle.

13.meaning: You bring forth, draw out, or produce (something) — to make a thing emerge or come out from its source or container.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb in form IV (the causative 'afʿala,' 'to make something come out'). The 'tu-' prefix marks a second-person 'you' (singular masculine) subject, and the final '-u' is the indicative mood, the plain form for an ongoing or habitual statement. Prefixed with 'wa' ('and').

14.meaning: The dead — that which is lifeless, having lost or never possessed life.
14.grammar: A definite noun/adjective on the intensive pattern 'fayʿil' ('al-' = 'the,' its 'l' assimilated into the following 'm'). The final '-a' is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
14.root: م-و-ت (m-w-t) — death, dying

15.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
15.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

16.meaning: The living — that which is alive, possessing life and vitality.
16.grammar: A definite noun/adjective ('al-' = 'the'). Because the following letter 'ḥ' is a 'moon letter,' the 'l' of 'al-' is fully pronounced and does NOT assimilate (al-ḥayy). The final '-i' is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the living') or as following a preposition or governing particle.

17.meaning: You provide for, sustain, or bestow provision upon (someone) — to grant the means of life such as food, wealth, and sustenance.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb in the basic form I. The 'ta-' prefix marks a second-person 'you' (singular masculine) subject, and the final '-u' is the indicative mood, the plain form for an ongoing or habitual statement. Prefixed with 'wa' ('and').

18.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
18.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
18.root: — (pronoun)

19.meaning: You will / You wish — to will, want, or choose that something be. Mashīʾa (the noun from this root) is sovereign volition; the verb names the act of willing or desiring a thing into being.
19.grammar: Present-tense verb addressed to a single masculine 'you'. The ta- prefix marks the second-person singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, the normal mood for a plain statement of fact ('you will / you wish').
19.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing, volition

20.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
20.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
20.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

21.meaning: 'Reckoning / account / measure'. It refers to counting, calculating, or taking account — and by extension a limit or measure derived from counting. Often used of a tally or the act of holding to account.
21.grammar: The '-in' ending (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('a reckoning / any measure') and in the genitive case. The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: To take (something) for oneself, to adopt or seize it deliberately as one's own.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in form VIII (the reflexive 'iftaʿala' pattern, 'to take for oneself'). The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine 'he/it' subject. Its underlying jussive form ends in a vowelless consonant; the final '-i' here is a helping vowel added only to avoid an awkward consonant cluster before the next word, not a case or mood ending.

3.meaning: The believers — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm the truth and give it their security and assent.
3.grammar: A definite noun, the active participle of form IV ('mu'min,' 'one who believes/grants security'). The plural ending '-ūna' marks a masculine human plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or doer ('the believers' as those performing the action).

4.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
4.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

5.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
7.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
7.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

8.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
8.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').
8.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — faith, safety, security

9.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
9.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

10.meaning: He does, makes, or carries out; the doing or performing of an act. A general verb for engaging in or committing some deed.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The ya- prefix marks the singular male subject. The final consonant carries no vowel (the jussive/conditional form), which is the shortened form a present verb takes after conditional or certain other particles, typically giving the sense 'if/whoever does…'.
10.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — doing, making, performing an act

11.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
11.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

12.meaning: Then he/it is not; a negation that denies a present state or quality — 'is not the case', 'is not so'. The base word laysa specifically negates being or existence in the present.
12.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so' or 'then'. The stem laysa is a special negating verb meaning 'is not', used to deny a present state. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it is not').
12.root: ل-ي-س (l-y-s) — negation of being; 'is not' (defective verb)

13.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
13.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

14.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
14.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
16.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
16.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

17.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
17.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

18.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
18.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
18.root: — (particle; no root)

19.meaning: You guard yourselves, you are wary and conscious of Allah — to shield yourself by being mindful and reverently cautious, avoiding what brings harm or displeasure.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb in form VIII (the reflexive 'iftaʿala,' here 'to protect oneself / be God-conscious'), from a weak root so its final letter has dropped away. The 'ta-' prefix plus the '-ū' ending mark a second-person masculine plural 'you (all).' The loss of the final '-na' shows the subjunctive/jussive mood, the form used after certain particles (such as those meaning 'that,' 'not,' or in conditions).
19.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — guarding, shielding, protection

20.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
20.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

21.meaning: A guarding, a self-protective caution — wariness exercised to shield oneself from harm or danger.
21.grammar: A verbal noun naming the act of guarding oneself. The feminine ending '-ah' combined with the final '-an' (nunation) puts it in the accusative case while indefinite ('a precaution'); this often expresses manner or purpose — 'as / by way of (caution).'

22.meaning: And He cautions you, puts you on your guard — to alert someone to a danger and urge them to beware of it.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb in the intensive form II ('faʿʿala,' 'to warn earnestly'). The 'yu-' prefix marks a third-person masculine 'he' subject, and the verb stands in the indicative mood (plain statement). The attached '-kum' is the object pronoun 'you (all)'; its vowel appears here as '-kumu' to ease linking to the next word. Prefixed with 'wa' ('and').

23.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
23.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
23.root: — (proper divine name)

24.meaning: His own self, soul, or very being — the inner person or essence of an individual. The base noun nafs denotes the soul/self, and the attached 'his' makes it reflexive ('himself') or possessive ('his soul').
24.grammar: A noun carrying the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the object of certain particles. The suffix -hu means 'his/him', here making the noun reflexive or possessive.
24.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath of life

25.meaning: And to / and toward; a connector "and" joined with a preposition expressing direction or destination toward which something moves or is referred.
25.grammar: A preposition meaning "to/toward," prefixed with the connector wa- ("and"). Being a preposition, it puts the noun that follows it into the genitive case (the "…toward X" relationship). It has no case ending of its own.

26.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
26.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

27.meaning: Al-maṣīr — the destination, the place or state one finally comes to; the journey's end or ultimate outcome to which things return.
27.grammar: A definite noun of place/result on the pattern mafʿil, with the long ī arising from the weak root letter yāʾ (ص-ي-ر). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or what something ultimately is. The word denotes the final place or state to which one comes.
27.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become, come to, end up at

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
2.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

3.meaning: You hide or conceal (something) — to keep a thing secret and out of sight, especially inward thoughts or feelings.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative form IV ('to hide something'), from a weak root whose final letter has dropped away. The 'tu-' prefix plus the '-ū' ending mark a second-person masculine plural 'you (all).' The loss of the final '-na' shows the subjunctive/jussive mood, the form used after certain particles (such as 'that,' 'if,' or 'not').

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: Your chests/breasts — the bosoms, figuratively the seat of one's inner thoughts, intentions, and feelings (plural of ṣadr, 'chest').
6.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'ṣadr.' The '-i' is the genitive case, here required because the noun carries a possessive pronoun: the attached '-kum' means 'your (all)' and grammatically possesses the noun ('the chests OF you').

7.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
7.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

8.meaning: You reveal it, make it show or appear — to bring something out into the open so it becomes visible or known.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative form IV ('to make something appear'), from a weak root whose final letter has dropped away. The 'tu-' prefix plus the '-ū' ending mark a second-person masculine plural 'you (all),' in the subjunctive/jussive mood (the form used after particles like 'that,' 'if,' or 'not'). The attached '-hu' is the object pronoun 'it / him.'
8.root: ب-د-و (b-d-w) — appearing, becoming visible

9.meaning: He knows it, is aware of it — to have knowledge of a thing, perceiving and understanding its reality.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb in the basic form I. The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine 'he' subject. The vowelless ending on the stem ('-lam' with no following vowel) shows the jussive mood, the clipped form used after certain particles or in conditional/result clauses. The attached '-hu' is the object pronoun 'it / him.'

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
10.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence.
