So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

11.meaning: And He knows — to have knowledge, perceiving and being fully aware of things.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb in the basic form I. The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine 'he' subject, and the final '-u' is the indicative mood, the plain form for an ongoing or habitual statement. Prefixed with 'wa' ('and').

12.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
14.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
14.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

15.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
15.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
16.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

17.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
17.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

18.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
18.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
18.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

19.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
19.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

20.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
20.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

21.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
21.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
21.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

22.meaning: All-powerful, fully able, ever-capable — possessing complete and effective power to do whatever is willed; one whose ability never falls short.
22.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, abiding quality ('thoroughly able'). The final -un is the indefinite nominative (nunation) — the doubled-n shows no 'the', and the -u base vowel marks the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or a predicate ('… is all-powerful').

1.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
1.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

2.meaning: You find, come upon, or discover (something) — to encounter a thing or find it to be in a certain state.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the basic form I (from a root whose first letter 'w' drops out in the present). The 'ta-' prefix marks a second-person 'you' (singular masculine) subject, and the final '-u' is the indicative mood, the plain form for an ongoing or future statement.

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'all, every, each, the whole of.' It expresses totality — when joined to a following noun it means 'every (one)' or 'the entirety of' that thing.
3.grammar: A noun of totality with the final -u ending (nominative). The -u typically marks it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It normally attaches to a following noun to mean 'every / all of' it.

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'soul, self, person, living being.' It denotes the inner self or the whole individual — the seat of life and identity, and by extension a 'person' as a single unit.
4.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a soul'). This form appears after prepositions or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun (such as 'every soul').
4.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being

5.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
5.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

6.meaning: She/it did, made, or worked — completed an action or deed in the past.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb in the basic form I. The suffix '-at' marks a third-person feminine singular subject — 'she' or a grammatically feminine 'it' completed the action. The past tense presents the act as already done and finished.

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: Good / goodness; also 'better' or 'best'. A word for what is good, beneficial, or excellent — and, by its pattern, often 'better than'.
8.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective ('good' or 'better'). The final -in (nunation with -i) marks it as indefinite ('some good / any good') and in the genitive case, typically after a preposition or in a possessive link.
8.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, what is better

9.meaning: Made present, brought forward and set before one — caused to be on hand and produced for viewing or reckoning.
9.grammar: A passive participle of the causative form IV ('made to be present / brought forward'); the 'mu-' prefix forms the participle and its passive sense means the thing is acted upon. The final '-an' (nunation) marks the accusative case while indefinite, often functioning as a descriptive state — '(as something) made present.'

10.meaning: A compound: the connective 'and' joined to the particle mā. The particle mā is highly versatile — it can mean 'what / whatever' (introducing an indirect question or a relative clause, 'that which'), or it can function as a negation ('not'). Context determines which sense applies; the core idea is an open, unspecified 'what(ever)' or a flat denial.
10.grammar: Two indeclinable particles, so there is no case ending to mark. The wa- prefix is the simple connective 'and', linking what follows to what precedes. Mā itself does not change form: it serves either as an interrogative/relative ('what, that which') or as a negating word ('not').

11.meaning: She/it did, made, or worked — completed an action or deed in the past.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the basic form I. The suffix '-at' marks a third-person feminine singular subject — 'she' or a grammatically feminine 'it' completed the action. The past tense presents the act as already done and finished.

12.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
12.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

13.meaning: Evil, harm, badness, or something offensive and grievous — that which is bad in itself or brings injury and distress. As a noun it names an evil thing or an evil deed.
13.grammar: The -in ending (nunation/tanwīn) marks an indefinite noun in the genitive case: 'an evil / of an evil'. The genitive typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive ('… of …'), and the doubled-n sound (tanwīn) signals that the noun is indefinite ('a/some').
13.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʼ) — to be bad, evil, to grieve or distress

14.meaning: It/she wishes, longs for, or would love (for something to happen) — an imperfect verb expressing affection mixed with desire, 'to wish, to want fondly'.
14.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb (Form I). The ta- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it') — or a second-person masculine singular ('you'). The final -u ending marks the indicative mood, the plain factual form used for ongoing or future action ('does / will do'), as opposed to the subjunctive or jussive.
14.root: و-د-د (w-d-d) — love, affection, fond wishing

15.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
15.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

16.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
16.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

17.meaning: A compound meaning 'between it/her' — the spatial-relational word 'between, amidst' with an attached pronoun 'it/her' referring to a feminine or non-human noun. It denotes the interval or space separating two things.
17.grammar: Bayna is an adverb of place ('between') and always ends in -a in this fixed form. The attached -hā is a possessive/object pronoun, third-person feminine singular, 'it/her' — pointing to a grammatically feminine or non-human antecedent. Together: 'between it (and …)'.
17.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinctness, the space between

18.meaning: A compound meaning 'and between it/him' — the connective 'and', plus 'between', plus an attached pronoun 'it/him'. It marks the second party of an interval: '… and between him/it'.
18.grammar: The wa- prefix is the connective 'and'. Bayna ('between') stays in its fixed -a form. The attached -hu is a third-person masculine singular pronoun ('him/it'). The -u vowel on the pronoun is its normal form after a preceding -a. The whole phrase pairs with a preceding 'between it' to mean 'between X and Y'.
18.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinctness, the space between

19.meaning: A span, stretch, or interval — especially of time or distance: a 'reach' or 'term' extending from one point to another. It names a measured gap or duration.
19.grammar: The -an ending (tanwīn) marks an indefinite noun in the accusative case: 'a span'. The accusative commonly marks the direct object of a verb or other complement, and the doubled-n (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness ('a/some span').
19.root: أ-م-د (ʼ-m-d) — a term, limit, or stretch of time/space

20.meaning: Far, distant, remote — describing something at a great remove in space, time, or degree. As an adjective it qualifies a noun as 'far off, far-reaching'.
20.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern (often intensive: 'very far'). The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and accusative — agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun it describes. The accusative is the case of objects and many complements; the tanwīn marks indefiniteness ('a far …').

21.meaning: And He cautions you, puts you on your guard — to alert someone to a danger and urge them to beware of it.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb in the intensive form II ('faʿʿala,' 'to warn earnestly'). The 'yu-' prefix marks a third-person masculine 'he' subject, and the verb stands in the indicative mood (plain statement). The attached '-kum' is the object pronoun 'you (all)'; its vowel appears here as '-kumu' to ease linking to the next word. Prefixed with 'wa' ('and').

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
22.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

23.meaning: His own self, soul, or very being — the inner person or essence of an individual. The base noun nafs denotes the soul/self, and the attached 'his' makes it reflexive ('himself') or possessive ('his soul').
23.grammar: A noun carrying the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the object of certain particles. The suffix -hu means 'his/him', here making the noun reflexive or possessive.
23.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath of life

24.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
24.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
24.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

25.meaning: Most kind, gentle, and compassionate; one who is full of tender pity and gentleness. Raʾūf is an intensive form stressing deep, abundant kindness — a name/attribute of Allah meaning 'the Ever-Gentle, Most Compassionate.'

parts.en: full of kindness / most gentle (the final -un is the nominative ending with tanwīn, marking an indefinite predicate)

25.grammar: An intensive adjective ('one full of …') describing abundant kindness. The final '-un' is the nominative case ending together with tanwīn (the '-n' that marks an indefinite noun): it typically marks the word as a subject or, as here, a predicate/description ('… is most kind'). The intensive pattern stresses depth and constancy of the quality.

26.meaning: With/of the servants (of Allah): 'with' or 'as to' joined to a word for human beings as the worshipping servants and creatures of Allah, wholly belonging to and dependent on Him.
26.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the servants') with the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('with / as to') and article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case ending, which is required after a preposition such as 'bi-'.
26.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, to worship; servitude

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
2.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

3.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
3.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

4.meaning: You (plural) love, are devoted to, or hold dear — an imperfect verb of affection addressed to a group. The underlying sense is loving, cherishing, and being drawn toward someone or something.
4.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb of Form IV (the standard verb 'to love', aḥabba / yuḥibbu, from a doubled root). The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural ('you all') in the indicative mood — the plain factual form for ongoing/future action. Dropping the final -na would signal subjunctive or jussive instead.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: A compound command: 'so/then follow me'. It joins the connective 'so/then' to the plural imperative 'follow!' with an attached object 'me'. 'Follow' here means to walk behind, take as a model, and obey.
6.grammar: Fa- is a connective prefix meaning 'so/then', often drawing a consequence. The verb is a Form VIII imperative (command). The -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all — do it!'), and -nī is the first-person object pronoun 'me'. The -n- before it is the nūn al-wiqāya ('protective nūn'), inserted to shield the verb's ending from the attached 'me' pronoun. So: 'then follow me, all of you'.

7.meaning: He will love you (plural), or 'so that He may love you' — an imperfect verb of affection with 'you all' as its object. It expresses the love/favor that one party shows toward a group.
7.grammar: A Form IV imperfect verb. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The stem shows the jussive mood — the vowel-less, clipped form used in conditional answers and after certain particles, here giving the sense 'he will then love' / 'so that he may love'. The attached -kum is the object 'you (plural)', here voweled -kumu for ease of pronunciation before the next word.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
8.root: — (proper divine name)

9.meaning: A compound: 'and He will forgive' / 'and may He forgive'. It joins 'and' to an imperfect verb meaning to forgive, pardon, and cover over sins — to wipe away guilt and shield the wrongdoer from its consequences.
9.grammar: The wa- prefix is the connective 'and'. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The verb stands in the jussive mood — shown by its clipped, vowel-less ending — typically appearing after certain particles or as the result-clause of a condition ('… he will forgive / that he may forgive').
9.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, shield, and pardon; forgiveness

10.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
10.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

11.meaning: A compound: 'your (plural) sins'. The plural noun dhunūb ('sins, faults, misdeeds') with an attached possessive 'your (all)'. A 'sin' here is a fault or offense that incurs guilt.
11.grammar: Dhunūb is a broken (irregular) plural of dhanb, 'sin'. The -a ending marks the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb ('… your sins' as the thing acted upon). The attached -kum is a possessive pronoun, second-person masculine plural, 'your (of you all)'.

12.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
12.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
12.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

13.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

14.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').
14.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: Obey! — a plural command to comply, submit, and do as one is told. The verb denotes willing, active obedience and yielding to authority.
2.grammar: A Form IV imperative (command) built on the root for obedience. The -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee — 'obey, all of you!'. (The written final alif after the wāw is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.)

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
3.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

4.meaning: A compound: 'and the Messenger'. It joins 'and', the definite article 'the', and the noun rasūl — one who is sent, an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver a message.
4.grammar: The wa- prefix is 'and'; al- is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates in sound to the following 'r', hence r-rasūl). The noun is on the faʿūl pattern meaning 'one sent'. The final -a ending marks the accusative case — commonly the direct object of a verb ('… the Messenger' as the one being acted upon).
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching a message or envoy

5.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
5.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

6.meaning: 'They turned away / they turned their backs / they turned aside'. It conveys turning oneself away from something, often implying rejection or withdrawal.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine plural: the ending '-aw' means 'they (did) …'. The Form V pattern (with the 'ta-' prefix and doubled middle letter) gives a reflexive sense — turning oneself away. It states a completed act.
6.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near/turn toward; in this form, to turn away

7.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
7.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
8.root: — (proper name)

9.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

10.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
10.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

11.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
11.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
11.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

3.meaning: He selected, chose, or singled out as preferred — to elect and favor someone, giving them a chosen standing above others.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he did it'). The Form VIII pattern conveys carefully selecting or picking out the best for oneself. The final long -ā reflects the verb's weak (root-final) shape.
3.root: ص-ف-و (ṣ-f-w) — purity, clearness; to select the choicest

4.meaning: 'Adam' — the proper name of the first human being and first prophet.
4.grammar: A proper name that is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) — it takes a restricted set of endings. Its final -a here does double duty: it marks the accusative case (e.g., as a direct object) and, because the name is a diptote, it stands in place of the usual nominative -u while also blocking the tanwīn (-n) that fully inflected nouns would take.

5.meaning: A compound: 'and Nūḥ' — the connective 'and' joined to the proper name Nūḥ (the Prophet Noah).
5.grammar: The wa- prefix is the connective 'and'. The -an ending marks the accusative case, typically the direct object of a verb. Although a proper name, Nūḥ takes regular tanwīn (-an) because it is short and fully declinable, rather than the restricted (diptote) endings of many foreign names.

6.meaning: A compound: 'and the family / line of'. It joins 'and' to the noun āl, meaning a person's household, kin, family, or followers — those belonging to someone. It is normally followed by the name of the person whose family is meant.
6.grammar: The wa- prefix is the connective 'and'. The final -a ending marks the accusative case (the direct object). Āl is an incomplete noun by sense — it leans on a following noun in the genitive to specify whose 'family/house' is intended ('the house of …').
6.root: أ-ه-ل (ʼ-h-l) — household, kin, family; āl is generally held to be a contraction of ahl

7.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (the Prophet Abraham).
7.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -a ending here serves for both accusative and genitive because the name is a diptote — a class of nouns that refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a for these two cases. So this one -a covers 'Ibrāhīm' whether as an object or as 'of Ibrāhīm'.

8.meaning: A compound: 'and the family / house of'. The connective 'and' joined to āl — a person's household, kin, or followers — typically followed by the name of the one whose family is meant.
8.grammar: The wa- prefix is the connective 'and'. The -a ending marks the accusative case (the direct object). Āl needs a following genitive noun to complete its meaning, naming whose 'family/house' is intended ('the house of …').
8.root: أ-ه-ل (ʼ-h-l) — household, kin, family; āl is generally held to be a contraction of ahl

9.meaning: The proper name ʿImrān — a personal/family name (the lineage of ʿImrān).
9.grammar: A proper name treated as a diptote — it refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a ending for both the accusative and the genitive. So this -a marks it as an object, or, after a possessive word, as 'of ʿImrān'.

10.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
10.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
10.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

11.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
11.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
11.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: Offspring, progeny, descendants — the children and seed of a person, a line of descent. It is a collective noun covering one's posterity.
1.grammar: A collective/feminine noun ending in the rounded tā' marbūṭa. When the case ending is voiced, the tā' marbūṭa is pronounced as 't', so the ending sounds '-tan': the -t- of the feminine marker plus -an (tanwīn-fatḥ). The -an marks it indefinite and accusative — 'a progeny / offspring' as a direct object or complement; the doubled-n (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness ('a/some').
1.root: ذ-ر-ر (dh-r-r) — to scatter/multiply; hence scattered seed, progeny

2.meaning: A compound: 'some of it/them' / 'a part of it'. The noun baʿḍ ('a part, portion, some') with an attached pronoun 'it/them' (feminine). It singles out a subset from a larger whole.
2.grammar: Baʿḍ means 'a portion/some'. The -u ending marks the nominative case — typically the subject of a sentence or a word that something is predicated about. The attached -hā is a third-person feminine singular possessive ('of it/them'), referring to a feminine or non-human whole. Paired with another baʿḍ, it commonly yields 'some of them … from others'.
2.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part or portion of something

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
4.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
4.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

5.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
5.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
5.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

6.meaning: All-Hearing / ever-hearing — one who hears completely and perfectly, missing nothing of what is uttered or whispered; an intensive form stressing the fullness of the quality. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
6.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a constant, perfect quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is all-hearing").

7.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
7.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: She said / she spoke — the past-tense verb 'to say', third-person feminine. The root sense is uttering speech, declaring, or stating.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing completed action. The -at ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she did'). The final -i here is an added helping vowel (the feminine ending is normally just -at, voweled to -ati only to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting hamza).

3.meaning: A woman; also specifically 'the wife of' someone. As the feminine counterpart of 'man', imra'a denotes an adult female, and when linked to a following name it means 'the wife of …'.
3.grammar: A feminine noun. The -t- is the feminine ending shown in its 'construct' form (the form used when the noun is bound to a following possessor), and the -u marks the nominative case — typically the subject of a sentence. In construct it leans on a following genitive noun, giving 'the woman/wife of …'.
3.root: م-ر-أ (m-r-ʼ) — relating to a human person; feminine: woman

4.meaning: The proper name ʿImrān — a personal/family name (the lineage of ʿImrān).
4.grammar: A proper name treated as a diptote — it refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a ending for both the accusative and the genitive. So this -a marks it as an object, or, after a possessive word, as 'of ʿImrān'.

5.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
5.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

6.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
6.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

7.meaning: I vowed, I pledged, I dedicated — the past-tense verb 'to make a vow', committing oneself (or dedicating something) to Allah by a solemn promise.
7.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing completed action. The -tu ending marks a first-person singular subject — 'I (did it)'. The verb conveys binding oneself by a vow or consecrating something to Allah.
7.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to vow, pledge, dedicate; also to warn

8.meaning: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
8.grammar: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.
8.root: — (particle + pronoun, no triliteral root)

9.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: My belly or womb — the inner cavity of the body, and by extension the womb in which a child is carried; with the attached pronoun it means specifically 'my belly/womb'.
11.grammar: A noun carrying the possessive ending -ī ('my'). The noun sits in the genitive case (the -i vowel before the pronoun), the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to another word as its possession.
11.root: ب-ط-ن (b-ṭ-n) — belly, that which is inner or hidden

12.meaning: Set free and devoted — a person or thing liberated from ordinary claims so as to be wholly dedicated to a single purpose, especially consecrated to the service of Allah.
12.grammar: A passive participle ('one who is freed/dedicated') of an intensive verb pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, the form typically used for the object of a verb or to describe the state in which something is.

13.meaning: So accept! — a command to receive something graciously and approvingly, addressed to a single male; the verb conveys welcoming and granting favourable acceptance.
13.grammar: A connecting particle fa- ('so/then') joined to a command verb addressed to one male ('you, accept!'). The bare, vowel-less ending is the typical form of a singular masculine imperative, expressing a direct request or appeal.
13.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to accept, receive, turn toward

14.meaning: From me; indicating origin, belonging, or association with the speaker — 'coming from me' or 'of my side'.
14.grammar: The preposition min ('from/of') with the attached pronoun -ī ('me'). An extra n is inserted (giving the doubled 'nn') to join the preposition smoothly to the pronoun. The -ī is the first-person singular pronoun 'me/my'.
14.root: — (particle/preposition; no root)

15.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
15.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

16.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
16.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

17.meaning: "the All-Hearing" — one who hears, perceiving all sounds completely and constantly; used as a divine name it denotes the One whose hearing is perfect and all-encompassing.
17.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, which conveys a deep, enduring quality ('ever-hearing,' not merely 'hearing once'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

18.meaning: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, perfect, and all-encompassing; an intensive form stressing that knowing is an essential, constant attribute.
18.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that stresses depth and permanence of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.
18.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: She laid it/her down — she delivered or gave birth; the verb's core sense is to put down or set down, and of a pregnancy it means to deliver the child. With the suffix it means 'she delivered her/it'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -at ending marks a single female doer ('she did'), and the attached -hā is the object ('her/it'), so together: 'she put/delivered her'.
2.root: و-ض-ع (w-ḍ-ʿ) — to place, put down, set down; to give birth

3.meaning: She said — a completed act of speaking or saying, attributed to a single female.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -at ending that marks a single female doer ('she said'). The plain past form presents the action as a completed whole.

4.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
4.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

5.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
5.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

6.meaning: I laid it/her down — I delivered or gave birth to her; the core sense is to put down, and of a pregnancy to deliver. With the endings it means 'I delivered her/it'.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -tu ending marks the speaker as doer ('I did'), and the attached -hā is the object ('her/it'), giving 'I put/delivered her'.
6.root: و-ض-ع (w-ḍ-ʿ) — to place, put down, set down; to give birth

7.meaning: A female — a female being, whether human or animal; the counterpart of 'male'.
7.grammar: A singular noun denoting a female. It ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case, so its grammatical role is shown by context rather than by a final vowel.

8.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
8.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
8.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

9.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
9.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
10.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

11.meaning: She laid down / delivered — she gave birth; the verb's root sense is to put down or set down, and of a pregnancy it means to deliver the child (here without an attached object).
11.grammar: A past-tense verb whose -at ending marks a single female doer ('she did/delivered'). The action is presented as completed.
11.root: و-ض-ع (w-ḍ-ʿ) — to place, put down, set down; to give birth

12.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not.' It denies that something is currently the case, functioning to negate a statement in the present, and it inflects for person like a verb.
12.grammar: A hollow negating verb fixed in form for the third-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'); the -a ending belongs to its frozen past-tense shape. Though past in form, it negates in the present. It introduces a subject and a predicate, denying the link between them. The prefix wa means 'and'.

13.meaning: The male — a male being, human or animal; the counterpart of 'female', here made definite by 'the'.
13.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'the' and the -u ending. The -u marks the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject doing or being something, or simply named.

14.meaning: Like the female — resembling or comparable to a female; 'as a female is'.
14.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the definite noun 'the female'. After ka- the noun stands in the genitive (the case governed by such particles); this noun's fixed long -ā ending does not visibly change.
14.root: ا-ن-ث (ʾ-n-th) — femaleness, the female

15.meaning: And indeed I — a connector 'and' joined to an emphatic particle that strongly affirms what follows ('truly, indeed'), with 'I' attached as its subject.
15.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the emphatic particle inna, which lends strong certainty to the statement it opens. The attached -ī ('me/I') is its grammatical subject; inna places the noun or pronoun after it in the accusative.

16.meaning: I named her/it — I gave her a name; the verb means to assign or pronounce a name for someone.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb of the intensive pattern (to name). The -tu ending marks the speaker as doer ('I did'), and the attached -hā is the object ('her/it'): 'I named her'.

17.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
17.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

18.meaning: And indeed I — a connector 'and' joined to an emphatic particle that strongly affirms what follows ('truly, indeed'), with 'I' attached as its subject.
18.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the emphatic particle inna, which lends strong certainty to the statement it opens. The attached -ī ('me/I') is its grammatical subject; inna places the noun or pronoun after it in the accusative.

19.meaning: I seek protection for her/it — I place her under safe-keeping and seek refuge on her behalf; the verb means to take or seek shelter from harm.
19.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The u- prefix marks the speaker as doer ('I'), and the -u ending is the plain (indicative) form used for a simple statement of fact. The attached -hā is the object ('her/it'): 'I seek refuge for her'.
19.root: ع-و-ذ (ʿ-w-dh) — to seek refuge, take shelter, protection

20.meaning: With You / in You — the preposition 'with/by/in' joined to the pronoun 'You' (addressing a single person), expressing reliance upon or recourse to that person.
20.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/in/by') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', addressing one male). Pronouns following a preposition take this object form.

21.meaning: And her offspring — 'and' joined to the word for one's progeny or descendants, with 'her' attached: her children and those who come from her.
21.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') with a noun meaning 'offspring' carrying the possessive -hā ('her'). The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or governed by certain particles.
21.root: ذ-ر-ر / ذ-ر-و (dh-r-r / dh-r-w) — to scatter, multiply; hence progeny, descendants

22.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
22.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

23.meaning: The Shayṭān — Satan, the devil: a rebellious, evil being who tempts and misleads; the term suggests one who is far removed from goodness and burning in defiance.
23.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the Satan / the devil'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
23.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote (from good/mercy); a devil

24.meaning: The accursed / driven away — one cast out and pelted, banished from mercy; a fixed epithet describing something or someone expelled and rejected.
24.grammar: An intensive adjective of the 'fixed quality' pattern (one who is stoned/driven off). With the article 'the' and the -i ending it is in the genitive case — the form used after a preposition or when describing a preceding genitive noun.
24.root: ر-ج-م (r-j-m) — to stone, pelt, drive away; to curse

1.meaning: So He accepted her/it — 'so/then' joined to a past verb of gracious acceptance, with 'her' as object: He received her with favour and approval.
1.grammar: The connector fa- ('so/then') with a past-tense verb of the intensive pattern (to accept graciously). The bare verb stem with no doer-suffix indicates a single male/'he' did it; the attached -hā is the object ('her/it').
1.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to accept, receive, turn toward

2.meaning: Her Lord — the word rabb means a master, owner and sustainer who nurtures, governs and provides; used of Allah it is the Lord who creates, owns and cares for all. With the suffix: 'her Lord'.
2.grammar: The noun rabb with the possessive -hā ('her'). The -u vowel before the pronoun is the nominative ending, the form a noun takes when it is the subject — the one doing or being something.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship and ownership

3.meaning: With acceptance — 'with' joined to a noun meaning a receiving or a favourable acceptance; the manner in which something is graciously received.
3.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/by') with a noun meaning 'acceptance'. The -in ending is the indefinite genitive — the case a noun takes after a preposition, with the final -n ('nunation') marking it as indefinite ('an acceptance').
3.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to accept, receive, turn toward

4.meaning: Good — fine, fair, beautiful and pleasing; that which is comely and excellent in quality.
4.grammar: A descriptive adjective ('good/fair'). The -in ending is the indefinite genitive, matching an indefinite genitive noun it describes — the -n ('nunation') marks indefiniteness ('a good …').
4.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, excellent

5.meaning: And He caused her/it to grow — 'and' joined to a past verb meaning to make (a plant or child) grow and flourish, with 'her' as object: He nurtured her into wholesome growth.
5.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') with a past-tense causative verb ('to make grow'). The bare stem with no doer-suffix indicates a single male/'he'; the attached -hā is the object ('her/it').
5.root: ن-ب-ت (n-b-t) — to grow, sprout, vegetate (of plants and growth)

6.meaning: A growing — the act or manner of growth and flourishing; used to reinforce a verb of growing, conveying 'a fine, full growing'.
6.grammar: A verbal noun ('growing/growth'). The indefinite accusative -an ending is the form often used for a noun that echoes and emphasises its own verb, expressing the way or extent of the action.
6.root: ن-ب-ت (n-b-t) — to grow, sprout, vegetate (of plants and growth)

7.meaning: Good, fine, beautiful, excellent — pleasing and praiseworthy in quality. It describes something done well or possessing goodness and beauty.
7.grammar: An adjective ('good'). The -an ending is accusative with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite). As an adjective it agrees with and describes a noun; the accusative case matches a noun in that same case.

8.meaning: And He took charge of her/it — 'and' joined to a past verb meaning to take responsibility for, guarantee and care for someone, with 'her' as object: He undertook her guardianship.

parts.en: he took charge of, made responsible for

8.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') with a past-tense verb of the intensive pattern (to take into one's charge / make responsible). The bare stem with no doer-suffix indicates a single male/'he'; the attached -hā is the object ('her/it').
8.root: ك-ف-ل (k-f-l) — to be responsible for, guarantee, take into one's care; guardianship

9.meaning: Zakariyyā — the proper name of the Prophet Zachariah; a personal name and so without a derived meaning.
9.grammar: A proper name (of a person). It ends in a fixed long -ā and does not change its ending for grammatical case; its role is understood from context.

10.meaning: 'whenever / every time' — a compound expressing that something recurs each and every time a condition is met.
10.grammar: A compound of kull ('every', in the accusative -a used adverbially) and mā ('what / the time that'). Together it works as a conditional time-word, 'each time that …', linking a repeated condition to its repeated result.

11.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he entered' or 'he went in' — to pass into an enclosed place, a house, a state, or among a group.
11.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he entered'. The final -a vowel is the standard ending of this verb pattern and signals a completed action by a single male subject.

12.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
12.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

13.meaning: Zakariyyā — the proper name of the Prophet Zachariah; a personal name and so without a derived meaning.
13.grammar: A proper name (of a person). It ends in a fixed long -ā and does not change its ending for grammatical case; its role is understood from context.

14.meaning: A prayer niche, sanctuary, or private chamber — an inner place set apart for worship, devotion, or retreat; the front recess of a place of prayer.
14.grammar: A definite noun ('the prayer chamber') marked by the prefix al- ('the'). The final -a vowel is accusative, which typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon, e.g. the place entered) or the goal of motion.
14.root: ح-ر-ب (ḥ-r-b) — war, fighting, combat; the noun miḥrāb derives from it as a 'place of struggle / combat'

15.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he found' — to come upon, discover, or encounter something, whether by searching or unexpectedly.
15.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he found'. The final -a is the standard ending marking a completed action by a single male subject.

16.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with her' or 'in her presence' — indicating nearness, possession, or being at someone's side; 'ʿinda' denotes proximity or 'at the place of'.

parts.en: with / at / in the presence of

16.grammar: An adverb of place, ʿinda ('with / at / near'), carrying its built-in accusative -a ending, joined to the attached pronoun -hā ('her'). Together they mean 'in her presence' or 'at her place'.
16.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — being near, at hand, in one's presence

17.meaning: 'provision,' 'sustenance,' 'a means of livelihood' — that which is bestowed to sustain and benefit, such as food and resources. 'Rizq' is whatever Allah grants a creature to live on, material or otherwise.
17.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case with indefiniteness — frequently the role of a stated purpose or explanatory complement ('as provision'), telling for what reason or in what capacity something is given.

18.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
18.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
18.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

19.meaning: A call meaning 'O Maryam' (Mary) — the vocative particle yā ('O') used to address or summon, attached to the proper name Maryam.
19.grammar: A direct address: the particle yā ('O') is used to call out to someone, followed by the name Maryam. The final -u ending is the standard form a singular name takes when being called.
19.root: — (proper name)

20.meaning: A particle/adverb meaning 'in whatever manner,' 'from wherever,' or 'whenever' — it asks or denotes the how, where, or when of an action in an open-ended way.
20.grammar: An invariable interrogative/conditional adverb; it has no case ending and never changes form. It introduces the manner, place, or time of an action in a general, open sense ('in what way / from where / when').

21.meaning: A phrase meaning 'for you' or 'to you' (addressed to a single female) — the preposition li- ('for/to') joined to the pronoun for 'you'.
21.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to'), joined to the attached pronoun -ki ('you'). The lam regularly takes the vowel -a (fatḥa) before any attached pronoun other than the first-person 'me', so la- + -ki is the standard paradigm form. The -ki ending specifically marks a single female addressee, so the whole means 'for you (a woman)'.

22.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
22.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

23.meaning: She said — a completed act of speaking or saying, attributed to a single female.
23.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -at ending that marks a single female doer ('she said'). The plain past form presents the action as a completed whole.
23.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

24.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
24.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

25.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
25.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

26.meaning: 'In the presence of / from with / from the side of' — a noun of place and source meaning nearness or 'with,' used for what is in someone's keeping, possession, or vicinity, and figuratively what proceeds from them.
26.grammar: An adverbial noun meaning 'at / with / in the presence of,' here in the genitive case (the -i ending), as happens when it follows a preposition or links to a following noun ('the presence OF …'). It typically expresses 'from the side of' or 'in the keeping of' someone.
26.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — being at, near, or with; presence and proximity

27.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
27.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

28.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
28.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

29.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
29.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
29.root: — (proper name)

30.meaning: 'He provides / grants sustenance'. It denotes the act of providing the means of life — food, wealth, and every blessing — bestowed by a giver upon recipients. Present tense, third person masculine singular.
30.grammar: The 'ya-' prefix marks a present/ongoing action by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final '-u' is the indicative ending, used for plain statements of fact about an ongoing or habitual action.
30.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, to sustain, provision

31.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
31.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

32.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
32.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
32.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

33.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
33.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
33.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

34.meaning: 'Reckoning / account / measure'. It refers to counting, calculating, or taking account — and by extension a limit or measure derived from counting. Often used of a tally or the act of holding to account.
34.grammar: The '-in' ending (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('a reckoning / any measure') and in the genitive case. The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

1.meaning: An adverb meaning 'there' or 'at that point' — pointing to a distant place, and by extension to a particular moment or set of circumstances ('right then and there').
1.grammar: A demonstrative adverb of place built from hunā ('there') plus the suffix -lika that signals farness, giving 'over there / yonder'. It is a fixed (indeclinable) word with no changing case ending, and can point to a time or situation as well as a place.

2.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he called upon' or 'he prayed / invoked' — to appeal to someone, to summon, or to make supplication.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he called / invoked'. This root ends in a weak letter, so the final root letter appears as the long -ā vowel; it marks a completed action by a single male subject.

3.meaning: Zakariyyā — the proper name of the Prophet Zachariah; a personal name and so without a derived meaning.
3.grammar: A proper name (of a person). It ends in a fixed long -ā and does not change its ending for grammatical case; its role is understood from context.

4.meaning: The noun 'Lord' joined to a 'his' pronoun — 'his Lord'. Rabb conveys the Master and Sustainer who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; far richer than 'lord' alone.
4.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -a ending is accusative, the case used when the noun is an object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case; -hu means it belongs to 'him'.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

5.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
5.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

6.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
6.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

7.meaning: A command meaning 'grant!' or 'bestow!' — a request to give or confer something as a gift, typically addressed to Allah in supplication.
7.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a single person: 'grant!'. The verb's weak first root letter drops in the command form, leaving the short, vowel-less ending — the standard shape of a direct request to one addressee.
7.root: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — giving freely, bestowing a gift

8.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
8.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: From Yourself; from Your presence. The base word ladun means 'the presence of', 'the side of', or 'directly from' — pointing to something issuing straight from a source. Here it is preceded by the preposition min ('from'), whose final n assimilates into the following l so that the l is doubled. With the attached pronoun the whole conveys 'from Your own presence', stressing that what is given comes directly from the giver.

parts.en: from (preposition; its n merges into the following l)
presence / nearness / 'from with' (doubled l from the merged n)

10.grammar: An adverb of place/source ('at, by, in the presence of') joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'your/you' for a single masculine addressee, together conveying 'from Your presence'. The initial l is written with a shadda (doubled): this gemination results from the preceding preposition min, whose final n assimilates into the l. The word implies immediacy of source — something coming directly from the one referred to.
10.root: — (an adverbial particle of place; no triliteral verbal root)

11.meaning: Offspring, progeny, descendants — the children and seed of a person, a line of descent. It is a collective noun covering one's posterity.
11.grammar: A collective/feminine noun ending in the rounded tā' marbūṭa. When the case ending is voiced, the tā' marbūṭa is pronounced as 't', so the ending sounds '-tan': the -t- of the feminine marker plus -an (tanwīn-fatḥ). The -an marks it indefinite and accusative — 'a progeny / offspring' as a direct object or complement; the doubled-n (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness ('a/some').
11.root: ذ-ر-ر (dh-r-r) — to scatter/multiply; hence scattered seed, progeny

12.meaning: An adjective meaning 'good', 'pure', or 'wholesome' (describing a feminine noun) — that which is fine, sound, agreeable, and untainted, whether in substance, character, or speech.
12.grammar: A feminine singular adjective ('good / pure'). The final -tan ending combines the feminine marker with 'tanwīn' (the -n sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a …') in the accusative case, which typically marks it as a direct object or describes such a noun.

13.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
13.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

14.meaning: An intensive descriptive noun meaning 'All-Hearing' or 'ever-hearing' — one who hears fully, constantly, and perfectly; as a divine attribute, the One who hears every sound and supplication.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying constant, abundant hearing. The final -u vowel is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate that describes the subject ('… is all-hearing').
14.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

15.meaning: A noun meaning 'the calling', 'the supplication', or 'the prayer of request' — the act of calling upon Allah, appealing, or invoking.
15.grammar: A definite verbal noun ('the supplication'), marked by the prefix al- ('the'). The final -i vowel is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF supplication') or follows a preposition.

1.meaning: A past-tense verb with attached object meaning 'then she called him' — fa- ('then/so') joined to 'she called out to / summoned him'. The verb implies calling from a distance or with a raised voice.
1.grammar: The connector fa- ('then / so') + a past-tense verb in the third-person feminine singular ('she called'), shown by the -t ending that marks a single female subject, + the attached object pronoun -hu ('him'). The verb pattern (nādā) conveys calling out aloud.

2.meaning: The angels; spiritual beings created by Allah who serve and obey Him and carry out His commands.
2.grammar: A collective plural noun ('the angels') made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for the doer of an action.
