27.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The u- prefix marks the doer as 'I' in a causative (form-IV) verb, 'I make (something) live'. The verb ends in a long -ī because its final root letter is a weak (y) letter; this is the indicative form, presenting the act as a real, ongoing or habitual one.
27.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — to live; life

28.meaning: 'The dead' — those who have died or are without life; the lifeless, as a group.
28.grammar: A definite plural noun/adjective ('the dead'). It is of a plural pattern that ends in a fixed long -ā, so its ending does not change with grammatical position; it refers collectively to those who are dead.

29.meaning: 'By the leave of / with the permission of' — formed from 'with/by' plus 'permission, leave, sanction'. It conveys that something happens by someone's authorization or enabling will.
29.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition 'with/by'. The noun 'idhn' means 'permission, leave, sanction'. After the preposition it takes the genitive -i ending, the form used following a preposition and typically linking on to a following noun ('the permission OF …').
29.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; also listening/ear

30.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
30.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

31.meaning: And I inform you / tell you — to give weighty news or important tidings to a group; an ongoing or repeated act of informing.
31.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The u- prefix marks the doer as 'I' in an intensive (form-II) verb, 'I inform / give news'. The -kum suffix is the object 'you (all)'. The verb is indicative, presenting the informing as a real, ongoing or habitual act.
31.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings, weighty report; to inform

32.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
32.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

33.meaning: You eat — to consume food; addressed to a group, describing an ongoing or habitual action.
33.grammar: The ta- prefix plus the -ūna ending mark the subject as 'you (masculine plural)'. The full -ūna ending (with its final nūn intact) is the indicative mood, presenting the eating as a real, ongoing or habitual fact rather than something negated or made conditional.

34.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
34.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

35.meaning: You store up / lay in store — to set aside and keep provisions for later; addressed to a group, describing an ongoing or habitual action.
35.grammar: The ta- prefix plus the -ūna ending mark the subject as 'you (masculine plural)'. This is a form-VIII verb (the doubled dd- reflects an assimilated infix), giving a sense of doing the action for oneself ('storing away for yourselves'). The full -ūna ending is the indicative mood, presenting the storing as a real, ongoing or habitual fact.
35.root: ذ-خ-ر (dh-kh-r) — to store, hoard, save up provisions

36.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
36.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

37.meaning: Your houses — dwellings or homes belonging to a group of people.
37.grammar: The plural noun 'houses' in construct (possessive) with the attached pronoun -kum, 'your (all)'. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive case, which fits because the word follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun and is being possessed ('… of your houses / in your houses').
37.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — house, dwelling; to spend the night

38.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
38.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

39.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
39.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

40.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
40.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

41.meaning: Surely a sign, a token, or a clear indication; a marker that points to a deeper truth and serves as evidence or a lesson.
41.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphasizer, adding force like 'surely' or 'indeed'. The stem is a feminine singular noun. The -an ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a sign') and accusative, the case used for objects and, characteristically, for the thing affirmed after certain emphatic constructions.
41.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, token; a verse of revelation

42.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
42.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

43.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
43.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

44.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
44.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
44.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

45.meaning: 'Believers / faithful ones' — the plural of muʾmin, one who has faith and trust in Allah and grants assent to the truth.

parts.en: believers (form IV participle, oblique masculine sound plural)

45.grammar: An active participle ('one who believes') from the form IV pattern, here a masculine sound plural. The single suffix -īna is the oblique (accusative/genitive) form of the masculine plural — used for a direct object or after a preposition — as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject. Its nūn is part of the one ending and is not a separable morpheme.
45.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust; hence faith and belief

1.meaning: And confirming / verifying — one who attests that something earlier is true and bears it out; the active doer of 'confirming'.
1.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) from an intensive (form-II) verb, meaning 'one who confirms / attests the truth of'. The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative, which here typically marks a circumstantial state ('coming as a confirmer / while confirming') or the object of a verb.
1.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truth, sincerity; to be truthful, to confirm

2.meaning: To / for that which — a preposition 'to, for' joined to a relative word meaning 'what' or 'that which'.
2.grammar: A combination of the preposition li- ('to, for') with the relative pronoun mā ('that which'). Together they introduce something toward or for which an action is directed; mā itself does not change for case.

3.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
3.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
3.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

4.meaning: My two hands — the pair of hands belonging to the speaker; idiomatically 'what is between my hands' can mean what lies before/ahead of me.
4.grammar: The dual noun 'two hands' joined to the first-person pronoun 'my'. The dual's ending merges with the pronoun -ī to give -ayya. This dual form is in the oblique (accusative/genitive) case — the form used when the word is an object or follows a preposition — rather than the nominative.

5.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
5.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

6.meaning: The Torah — the revealed scripture given to the Prophet Moses (Mūsā).
6.grammar: The al- prefix means 'the' (its 'l' is pronounced as a doubled 't' merging into the following letter). The final -i is the genitive case, fitting a word that follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun ('… of the Torah'). Because it carries 'the', it takes a single -i (not tanwīn).

7.meaning: And so that I may make lawful / permit — to declare something allowed and release it from prohibition; expressed as a purpose ('in order that I make lawful').
7.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The li- prefix means 'so that / in order to' and puts the verb into the subjunctive, marked by the final -a: this signals purpose or intention ('in order that I make lawful') rather than a plain factual statement. The u- prefix marks the doer as 'I' in a causative (form-IV) verb.
7.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to be lawful/permitted; to untie, release

8.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

9.meaning: a part of / some of / a portion of — a noun denoting a piece or fraction of a larger whole (in the accusative form).
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'part' or 'some'. The final -a ending is accusative, marking it as a direct object or, with a measure of time, an adverbial span. It is normally followed by a noun in the genitive ('part of …').
9.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, a portion, some

10.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

11.meaning: It was forbidden / made unlawful — a completed act, by an unnamed doer, of declaring something prohibited.
11.grammar: A past-tense passive verb from an intensive (form-II) stem: the inner vowel pattern 'ḥu-rri-' shows it is passive, 'was forbidden', with the doer left unstated. The final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('it / he'), so it reads 'it was made unlawful'.
11.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, prohibit; sacredness, what is inviolable

12.meaning: A combination meaning 'upon you' or 'over you all' (addressed to a group of males or a mixed group). It frequently carries the sense of an obligation or duty resting on the addressees, or of something coming down 'upon' them.
12.grammar: Built on the preposition ʿalā ('upon, over, against'), which shifts to the form ʿalay- when a pronoun is attached. The ending -kum is the attached object pronoun for a group ('you all', masculine/mixed plural). The whole conveys 'upon you (people)'.

13.meaning: I have come to you — a completed act of arriving or bringing oneself, directed toward a group of addressees.
13.grammar: A past-tense (completed) verb. The -tu ending means 'I' did the action; the -kum suffix is the object 'you (all)'. So the form conveys 'I came / have come to you-plural', presenting the arrival as already accomplished.

14.meaning: With a sign — by means of an indicative token, miracle, or evidentiary proof that points to a truth.
14.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with / by means of' and always pulls the following noun into the genitive. The final -in (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive: 'with a sign', the ending required after this preposition and marking the noun as indefinite ('a', not 'the').
14.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token; a verse of scripture

15.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
15.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

16.meaning: 'Your Lord' (Lord of a group) — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer who owns, governs, and gradually brings to fullness those He addresses.
16.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Master') carries an -i vowel before the attached pronoun, reflecting a genitive/possessive link. The ending -kum is the possessive pronoun for a group ('your', masculine/mixed plural), so together: 'the Lord belonging to you all'.
16.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

17.meaning: A two-part word: a connecting/result particle 'fa' ('so, then, therefore') joined to a command 'be mindful, guard yourselves, hold in reverent awe.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself from harm or wrongdoing through God-conscious vigilance, keeping a careful, reverent guard.
17.grammar: A result particle 'fa-' attached to an imperative (command) verb, 2nd person masculine plural. The -ū ending directs the command at a group: 'you all, guard yourselves / be mindful.' The 'fa-' frames the command as following from something just stated ('so then...').
17.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
18.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
18.root: — (proper name)

19.meaning: 'And obey me' — a command directed at a group to comply with, submit to, and follow the speaker.
19.grammar: wa- is the connector 'and'. The stem is a command (imperative) verb addressed to a plural group; the -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressee ('you all do it'). The final -ni is the 'nūn al-wiqāya' (protective nūn) plus the object pronoun 'me', giving 'obey me'.
19.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, to comply willingly

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

3.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
3.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

4.meaning: 'And your Lord' (Lord of a group) — joining the speaker's Lord to that of the addressees: the one Master and Sustainer of both.
4.grammar: wa- is 'and'. The noun rabb shows an -u vowel, the nominative case typically marking the subject or predicate of a sentence ('… IS the Lord'). The ending -kum is the possessive pronoun for a group ('your', masculine/mixed plural).
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

5.meaning: 'So worship Him' — a directive to a group to serve, devote themselves to, and humbly submit in worship to Him.
5.grammar: fa- is a connector meaning 'so' or 'then', often drawing a consequence. The stem is a command (imperative) verb; the -ū ending addresses a masculine/mixed plural ('you all do it'). The final -hu is the object pronoun 'him/it', so the whole means 'so worship Him'.
5.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve, to devote oneself

6.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
6.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

7.meaning: 'A path / a road / a way' — a clear traveled route; used figuratively for a way of life or course of conduct.
7.grammar: The noun ṣirāṭ ('path'). The ending -un (nunation with -u) marks it as indefinite ('a path') and in the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate ('… IS a path').
7.root: ص-ر-ط (ṣ-r-ṭ) — a way, road, or path

8.meaning: 'Straight / upright / direct' — describing something perfectly even and undeviating, leading directly to its goal without crookedness.
8.grammar: An active participle of the form mustafʿil (here mustaqīm, 'one that is standing straight / upright'), built from the Form X verb istafʿala (here istaqāma, 'to stand straight, be upright'). It functions as an adjective. The ending -un marks it as indefinite and nominative, the case that typically matches a described subject or predicate ('a … one that is straight').
8.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to be upright/straight

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: 'He sensed / perceived / became directly aware of' — to grasp something through the senses or by keen intuition.
2.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb on the 'afʿala' pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he …'). The fixed -a ending is characteristic of this past-tense 'he' form. The pattern adds a sense of bringing about or attaining the perception.
2.root: ح-س-س (ḥ-s-s) — sense perception, to feel or perceive

3.meaning: 'ʿĪsā' — the proper name of the prophet Jesus, son of Mary (peace be upon him).
3.grammar: A proper name. It is grammatically 'invariable' — its final long -ā does not change for case, so it keeps the same form whether subject, object, or possessor.

4.meaning: 'From them / among them' (a group of males or a mixed group) — indicating origin, source, or partitive 'some of them'.
4.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among'). The attached pronoun -hum ('them', masculine/mixed plural) takes a helping vowel -u (becoming -humu) for ease of pronunciation before a following word. The whole means 'from/among them'.

5.meaning: 'Disbelief / rejection' — the act of refusing faith, denying the truth, and being ungrateful toward Allah and His signs; the opposite of belief.
5.grammar: al- is the definite article 'the'. The noun kufr ('disbelief') carries an -a ending, the accusative case, which typically marks the direct object of a verb ('… perceived/found THE disbelief').
5.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover up, to reject faith, to be ungrateful

6.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
6.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

7.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
7.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

8.meaning: 'My helpers / my supporters' — those who come to one's aid and lend strong assistance, claimed as belonging to the speaker.
8.grammar: anṣār is a plural noun ('helpers'). The attached -ī means 'my'. Before this 'my' pronoun the noun's case-vowel merges into the long -ī, so a single -ī is heard: 'my helpers'.
8.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to give victory

9.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
9.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
11.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

12.meaning: 'The disciples' — devoted, sincere followers and close supporters; specifically the term used for the loyal companions of the prophet ʿĪsā (Jesus).
12.grammar: al- is 'the'. The noun ḥawāriyy ('disciple') takes the sound masculine plural ending -ūna, which both makes it plural ('disciples') and marks the nominative case, typically signaling the subject of a sentence.
12.root: ح-و-ر (ḥ-w-r) — whiteness/purity; to return; sincere devotion

13.meaning: 'We' — the standalone pronoun for a speaker including others (or a single speaker of majesty). It stands alone to name or emphasize the subject 'we'.
13.grammar: A detached (standalone) personal pronoun, first-person plural, 'we'. Such independent pronouns are used to state or emphasize the subject, often highlighting 'we' as the ones who do or are something.

14.meaning: 'Helpers / supporters (of)' — those who give aid and strong assistance, standing in support of someone or something.
14.grammar: anṣār is a plural noun ('helpers'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate of a sentence and also begins a possessive construction ('the helpers OF …').
14.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to give victory

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.

17.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
17.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
17.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

18.meaning: 'And bear witness / and testify' — a command to one addressee to observe, affirm, and give testimony to something.
18.grammar: wa- is 'and'. The stem is a command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person; the bare ending with no added vowel or suffix marks the masculine singular addressee ('you bear witness'). The opening vowel a/i is a helping vowel for pronunciation.
18.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, to testify, to be present

19.meaning: A particle-cluster meaning '(testifying/affirming) that we …'. It introduces and emphasizes a statement, asserting firmly that 'we' are the subject of what follows.

parts.en: with / by / in (here introducing the content)

19.grammar: bi- is a versatile preposition ('with, by, in'); joined to anna it introduces the content of a statement or testimony. anna is an emphatic 'that' which strongly asserts the clause it opens. The attached pronoun -nā means 'we'; in writing its nūn merges with the doubled nūn of anna, but the suffix is still nā. After anna it serves as that clause's subject: 'that we …'.

20.meaning: 'Ones who submit / those who surrender themselves to Allah' — the plural of the active participle 'muslim,' i.e. one who willingly submits and devotes himself in obedience to Allah.
20.grammar: A masculine plural active participle (a doer-noun). The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case, the form used when the word stands as the subject or as the predicate naming who/what the subject is.

1.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

1.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
1.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

2.meaning: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.

3.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
3.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

4.meaning: 'You sent down / You revealed' — to cause something to descend from a higher place to a lower one; used especially of Allah sending down revelation, addressed to a single 'You'.
4.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb on the 'afʿala' pattern, which carries a causative sense ('to make come down'). The ending -ta marks the second-person masculine singular doer ('you' — one male) who completed the act: 'You sent down'.
4.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, to come/send down

5.meaning: 'And we followed / and we follow' — to go after, pursue, and conform to someone or something, taking it as a guide or example.
5.grammar: wa- is 'and'. The stem is a completed-action (past-tense) verb on the 'iftaʿala' pattern, which adds a sense of doing something for oneself or diligently ('to follow closely, to adopt as a guide'). The ending -nā marks 'we' as the doer: 'and we followed'.
5.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, to come after, to pursue

6.meaning: The messenger, envoy, or emissary: one who is sent with a message; in the Qur'an typically a prophet sent by Allah bearing revelation to a people.
6.grammar: A noun on the form faʿūl (an intensive/agent pattern, 'one sent'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('… the messenger') or the subject of certain particles. The 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 'r' (a 'sun letter'), pronounced ar-rasūl.

7.meaning: 'So write us / so record us / so enroll us' — a plea that the speakers be registered or inscribed (e.g., among a named group).
7.grammar: fa- is a connector 'so/then', often drawing a consequence. The stem is a command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person ('you write/record'), the bare unsuffixed form marking the singular addressee. The final -nā is the object pronoun 'us': 'so record us'.
7.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write, to inscribe, to ordain/record

8.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
8.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

9.meaning: 'The witnesses / those who testify' — people who observe and bear testimony, affirming the truth of something.
9.grammar: al- is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'sh', heard as ash-shā…). The active participle shāhid ('one who witnesses') takes the sound masculine plural ending -īna, which makes it plural and marks the accusative/genitive case — typically the object of a verb, or the object of a preposition, or part of a possessive phrase.
9.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, to testify, to be present

1.meaning: 'And they schemed / and they plotted' — to devise a hidden plan or stratagem against someone, working covertly toward an end.
1.grammar: wa- is 'and'. The stem is a completed-action (past-tense) verb; the ending -ū marks a masculine/mixed plural doer ('they', three or more): 'and they schemed'. (The written final alif after -ū is silent.)
1.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — to scheme, to plot, to devise a stratagem

2.meaning: 'And He planned / and He devised' — to put in place a counter-design or arrangement; when used of Allah it denotes a wise, just, and overpowering plan that outmatches the schemes of others.
2.grammar: wa- is 'and'. The stem is a completed-action (past-tense) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he …'). The fixed -a ending is characteristic of this past-tense 'he' form: 'and He planned'.
2.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — to scheme, to plot, to devise a stratagem

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
4.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
4.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

5.meaning: 'Best / the best (of)' — superior to all others in goodness, excellence, or worth; the finest in its class.
5.grammar: khayr functions as a comparative/superlative noun ('better / best'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate of a sentence and also opens a possessive phrase ('the best OF …').
5.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or best

6.meaning: Those who scheme and plot — people who lay secret, cunning plans. In Arabic, makr is covert contriving; said of human beings it carries a sense of treacherous plotting, while when ascribed to Allah it means His perfect, just outmaneuvering of such schemes. This is the active participle in the plural: 'the schemers / the plotters.'
6.grammar: An active participle (the doer of an act) made plural. The al- prefix means 'the.' The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative or genitive state — that is, the form used when the word is an object of a verb or governed by a preposition, rather than the subject.
6.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — to scheme, plot, devise a cunning plan

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
2.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: A direct address: 'O Isa (Jesus).' It combines the vocative particle 'O' with the proper name Isa, the prophet known in English as Jesus, son of Mary.
4.grammar: The particle yā is used to call out to or address someone directly ('O …!'). Isa is a proper name; its ending does not change for case because it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) foreign name.

5.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
5.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

6.meaning: 'The One who takes you fully' — the active participle of a verb meaning to take something completely and in full. It is commonly used of receiving a soul at death or of taking a person wholly to oneself. With an attached 'you,' it means 'the One who will take you / receive you in full.'

parts.en: one who takes in full / receives completely

6.grammar: An active participle (the one performing the act) from a verb meaning 'to take in full.' The attached -ka is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'you' (one male). The participle's own final long vowel -ī has absorbed the case ending before the attached pronoun.
6.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to fulfill, complete, take/pay in full

7.meaning: 'And the One who raises you' — joined by 'and' to a preceding word. It is the active participle of a verb meaning to lift up or elevate, with an attached 'you': 'the One who raises / lifts you up.'
7.grammar: The prefix wa means 'and.' The core is an active participle (the one doing the act, 'raiser/elevator'). Its -u ending is the nominative case, the form used for a subject or a predicate. The attached -ka means 'you' (one male).

8.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
8.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'
8.root: — (preposition)

9.meaning: 'And the One who purifies you' — joined by 'and.' It is the active participle of an intensive verb meaning to cleanse or purify thoroughly, with an attached 'you': 'the One who purifies / cleanses you.'
9.grammar: The prefix wa means 'and.' The core is an active participle from an intensive verb form (the doubled middle root letter marks this pattern), denoting the one who thoroughly purifies. Its -u ending is the nominative case (subject/predicate form). The attached -ka means 'you' (one male).
9.root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r) — to be pure, clean; (intensive) to purify, cleanse

10.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
10.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

11.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
11.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

12.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
12.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

13.meaning: 'And the One who makes / places' — joined by 'and.' It is the active participle of a verb meaning to make, render, appoint, or place something into a state: 'the One who makes / appoints.'
13.grammar: The prefix wa means 'and.' The core is an active participle (the one performing the act) meaning 'maker / appointer.' Its -u ending is the nominative case, the form for a subject or predicate.
13.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, place, appoint

14.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
14.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

15.meaning: 'They followed you' — a completed past action. From a verb meaning to follow, pursue, or adhere to. The form shows a group ('they') performing the act on a 'you.'
15.grammar: A past-tense verb in Form VIII (the iftaʿala pattern, here with the t of the pattern assimilated into the first root letter, giving a doubled tt). This form typically adds a reflexive or 'take up / adopt the action' nuance to the basic root, here yielding 'to follow.' The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males). The attached -ka is the object 'you' (one male). Together: 'they followed you.'
15.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

16.meaning: 'Above / over / on top of.' An adverb of place meaning the higher position relative to something else; it can also mean 'superior to' or 'beyond.'
16.grammar: An adverb of place that is normally attached to a following noun ('above …'). Its fixed -a ending is the form such place-words take when they govern the noun that follows them.
16.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above, surpass, exceed

17.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
17.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

18.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
18.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
18.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

19.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
19.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

20.meaning: 'Day' — a span of time. It denotes a day or a definite point/period of time; it links to a following word to specify which day (e.g., 'the day of …').
20.grammar: A masculine noun. Its final -i vowel is the genitive case: it typically appears after a preposition or when the word is linked to a following noun in an 'of …' relationship (as in 'the day OF …').

21.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
21.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

22.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
22.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

23.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
23.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'
23.root: — (preposition)

24.meaning: 'Your return / your place of returning.' A noun naming either the act of returning or the destination to which one comes back, with an attached 'your' addressed to a group: 'your (pl.) return.'

parts.en: return / place or time of returning

24.grammar: A noun of place/time (a 'where/when' noun) built from the verb 'to return.' Its -u ending is the nominative case, used for a subject or predicate. The attached -kum means 'your,' addressed to a group of people.
24.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, go back, come back

25.meaning: 'So I judge / then I decide' — preceded by 'so/then.' From a verb meaning to judge, rule, or decide authoritatively between parties. The form expresses a first-person 'I' acting in the present or future.
25.grammar: The prefix fa means 'so' or 'then,' linking to what precedes. The verb is present/future tense; the a- prefix marks the subject as 'I.' Its -u ending shows the ordinary (indicative) present-tense form, used for a plain statement.
25.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, rule, govern

26.meaning: Between you / among you; the space or relation linking the members of a group.
26.grammar: An adverb of place ('between/among') with an attached pronoun. The fixed -a ending is characteristic of such place-words; the ending -kum means 'you' for a group, so the whole means 'among you all'.
26.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation/interval; the space between two things

27.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
27.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

28.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
28.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
28.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

29.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
29.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

30.meaning: 'You (all) differ / disagree' — from a verb meaning to differ, dispute, or hold conflicting views. The form addresses a group: 'you all differ from one another.'
30.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in a pattern meaning 'to differ among one another.' The ta- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the subject as 'you all' (a group). The -na at the end signals the ordinary (indicative) present form used for a plain statement.
30.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, differ, be at variance

1.meaning: 'Then as for …' A connective opening that introduces and singles out a topic for comment, often paired later with a response. The fa- means 'then/so,' and 'ammā' sets up 'as for (such-and-such)…' to highlight one case among others.
1.grammar: A connector fa- ('then, so') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā introduces a subject for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that gives the comment about it. Neither part takes case endings.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: 'So I punish them / then I will punish them' — preceded by 'so/then.' From an intensive verb meaning to torment or chastise, with an attached 'them.' The form is first-person 'I' acting upon a group.
4.grammar: The prefix fa means 'so' or 'then.' The verb is present/future in an intensive pattern (marked by the doubled middle root letter); the u- prefix marks the subject as 'I.' Its -u ending is the ordinary (indicative) present form for a plain statement. The attached -hum means 'them' (a group).

5.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
5.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

6.meaning: 'Severe / intense / harsh.' An adjective describing something strong, forceful, and hard to bear.
6.grammar: An adjective in an intensive pattern ('very strong/severe'). The -an ending marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the form used when it describes a noun that is itself indefinite and accusative.
6.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, severe

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
8.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
8.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

9.meaning: And the Hereafter / and the next life: 'and' joined to 'the latter (abode)' — the life and final, lasting world that comes after this present one. From a root meaning 'last/later', it is the counterpart to this world (al-dunyā).
9.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the latter / the Hereafter') with conjunction 'wa-' ('and') and article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case ending, the case used after prepositions or to link one noun to another ('… of …').
9.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after; the end

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

11.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
11.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

12.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
12.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

13.meaning: Helpers / supporters: those who give aid, support, and victory to another, standing by them against an adversary; the plural of 'helper'.
13.grammar: A masculine plural active participle — a 'doer' word meaning 'ones who help'. The sound plural ending -īna marks more than two; this -īna form (rather than -ūna) is the case used for objects of verbs and after prepositions or in possession (the accusative/genitive).
13.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to give victory/support

1.meaning: 'And as for …' A connective that introduces and sets apart a new topic for separate comment, usually anticipating a matching response clause. The 'and' joins it on; 'ammā' means 'as for (such-and-such)…'
1.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā singles out a topic for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that supplies the comment. Neither part takes case endings.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
4.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

5.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
5.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
5.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

6.meaning: 'So He pays them in full / then He gives them their due completely' — preceded by 'so/then.' From an intensive verb meaning to render in full, with an attached 'them.' It conveys giving someone the whole of what is owed, without shortfall.
6.grammar: The prefix fa means 'so' or 'then.' The verb is present/future in an intensive pattern (the doubled middle root letter); the ya- prefix marks the subject as 'he.' Because the stem ends in a long vowel (-ī), the indicative is shown by that retained vowel. The attached -him means 'them' (a group).
6.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to fulfill, complete, pay/give in full

7.meaning: 'Their rewards / their wages.' A noun naming recompense — the reward, wage, or compensation earned for deeds — with an attached 'their': 'their rewards.'
7.grammar: A plural noun meaning 'rewards/wages.' The -a ending is the accusative case, the form used when the word is the object of a verb (e.g., the thing given). The attached -hum means 'their,' referring to a group.

8.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
8.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
8.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

9.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

10.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
10.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

11.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
11.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
1.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

2.meaning: 'We recite it / We relate it' — from a verb meaning to recite, read aloud, or convey a narrative, with an attached 'it.' The form expresses 'we' performing the act upon a single thing.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The na- prefix marks the subject as 'we.' The stem ends in a long vowel (-ū) carrying the verb's form. The attached -hu means 'it' or 'him' (the thing recited).
2.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read out, follow in narration

3.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
3.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

4.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
4.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

5.meaning: 'The signs / the verses' — the plural of 'sign,' referring to clear indicators, proofs, miracles, or the verses of revelation that point to truth.
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the signs'), made definite by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The sound feminine plural takes the -i ending when it is an object of a verb or linked after a preposition or possessor — that is, when it is grammatically governed rather than serving as the subject.

6.meaning: 'And the Reminder' — joined by 'and.' The noun dhikr means a reminder, remembrance, or mention; it commonly denotes a revealed admonition that calls the mind and heart back to Allah and the truth.

parts.en: and / by (also used to introduce an oath)

6.grammar: The prefix wa means 'and'; it can also introduce an oath ('by …'). The al- means 'the.' The final -i vowel is the genitive case, which appears after a preposition or oath-particle, or when the word is linked to a following noun in an 'of …' relationship.
6.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

7.meaning: 'The Wise.' An adjective describing one possessing ḥikma — sound, perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right and fitting place. As a divine attribute it denotes flawless wisdom in all decree and command.

parts.en: wise / full of wisdom (in the genitive, '-i')

7.grammar: An adjective in an intensive pattern ('deeply/perfectly wise'). The al- means 'the.' The final -i vowel is the genitive case — the form used after a preposition, or when describing a noun that is itself genitive, or linking in an 'of …' relationship.
7.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to be wise, judge soundly, put things in their right place

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Likeness / example / parable.' The noun mathal denotes a comparison, similitude, or illustrative case put forward to make something understood by analogy.
2.grammar: A masculine noun. Its final -a vowel is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being presented/described.
2.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to be like, resemble; likeness, example

3.meaning: 'ʿĪsā' — the proper name of the prophet Jesus, son of Mary (peace be upon him).
3.grammar: A proper name. It is grammatically 'invariable' — its final long -ā does not change for case, so it keeps the same form whether subject, object, or possessor.

4.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
4.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: An expression meaning 'like the likeness of' or 'as the example of.' It joins the comparison word 'ka' (like, as) to the noun for a likeness/parable, setting up a comparison: 'comparable to the case of…'
6.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like, as') prefixed to a noun. Because ka- functions like a preposition, the noun takes the -i genitive ending, the case used after prepositions and to link 'the likeness OF …' to a following noun.

7.meaning: 'Adam' — the proper name of the first human being and first prophet.
7.grammar: A proper name that is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) — it takes a restricted set of endings. Its final -a here does double duty: it marks the accusative case (e.g., as a direct object) and, because the name is a diptote, it stands in place of the usual nominative -u while also blocking the tanwīn (-n) that fully inflected nouns would take.

8.meaning: 'He created him / He created it' — a completed past act. From a verb meaning to create, originate, or bring into being from nothing, with an attached 'him/it.'
8.grammar: A past-tense verb. With no added subject ending, the base form means 'he' performed the act. The final -a is the past-tense third-person masculine ending. The attached -hu is the object 'him' or 'it.'
8.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, bring into being

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: 'Dust / earth / soil.' The noun turāb denotes dust or dry earth — the fine soil of the ground.
10.grammar: A masculine noun. The -in ending marks it as indefinite ('dust / some dust') and in the genitive case — the form used after a preposition (e.g., 'from …') or when linked to a preceding noun.

11.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
11.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

12.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
12.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

13.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
13.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

14.meaning: The command 'Be!' — an order to come into existence, the creative imperative by which a thing is summoned into being.
14.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one person: 'Be!' It is the shortened command form of the verb 'to be/become,' with the bare, vowel-less ending typical of a singular order.
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into existence

15.meaning: 'And it comes to be / and it is' — the act of existence following upon a command, expressing that something duly comes into being.
15.grammar: The connector 'fa-' ('so/and then') joined to a present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('it is/becomes'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking an ordinary, unconditioned present or future statement; the doer 'it/he' is built into the verb.
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into existence

1.meaning: The truth — that which is real, established, and right; what genuinely corresponds to reality, and so also what is rightfully due. A weighty term spanning truth, reality, and rightful claim.
1.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word standing on its own as the topic. The doubled q (shadda) is part of the root.
1.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, right, to be established

2.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
2.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

3.meaning: The Lord belonging to a single male 'you' — Rabb is the Master, Owner, and Sustainer who creates, nurtures, and brings to maturity; here 'your Lord'.
3.grammar: The noun rabb (Lord, Sustainer) with the attached pronoun -ka, 'your' for one male. The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, the case that typically links a word to a following possessor or follows a preposition (here showing the possession 'of you'). The doubled b (shadda) belongs to the root.

4.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
4.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

5.meaning: A short (jussive) form of the verb 'to be / to become', meaning 'be' or 'does not become / is not'. It expresses being, existing, or coming to be in a clipped form that typically follows a particle such as a negator or a command.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person masculine singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, the form used after negative particles ('did not / was not') or as a command or prohibition.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

6.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
6.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: 'The doubters / those who fall into doubt' — people characterized by harbouring uncertainty, wavering, or contesting the truth.
7.grammar: An active participle (form VIII, 'one who doubts') made definite by al- ('the'). The -ina ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative or genitive case — the form used for the object of a verb or after a preposition. It names a class of people by their action: 'the ones who doubt'.

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
1.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

2.meaning: 'He argued/disputed with you' or '(if anyone) disputes with you' — to contend, wrangle, or press an argument against someone, with a directly attached 'you'.
2.grammar: A past-tense (form III) verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he'), the long a giving it the sense of mutual or directed contention ('to argue with'). The attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you' (masculine singular), the one being disputed with.

3.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
3.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
5.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
5.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: It came to you / reached you — a completed arrival of something reaching a person (one male).
7.grammar: A past-tense verb, 'he/it came', whose final -a vowel is the inherent third-person masculine singular inflection built into the verb form itself (not a separate piece). The attached pronoun -ka ('you', one male) is the object reached — 'it came to you'.

8.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
8.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

9.meaning: The knowledge; sure and certain knowing, established information and understanding (with the definite article).
