9.grammar: A definite verbal noun: al- means 'the'. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship. It denotes knowledge as a settled, certain thing.

10.meaning: Then say! / so say!: a command to one person to speak or utter, joined to what precedes by 'then/so'.
10.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male, 'say!' The prefixed 'fa-' means 'then' or 'so', linking the command to something before it as a consequence or sequel. The bare, vowel-less ending is normal for this imperative.

11.meaning: 'Come! / Come now!' — a call summoning people to approach or come forward, often used to invite a group toward a course of action.
11.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group, masculine plural ('you all'). The -aw ending carries the plural 'you' addressees; the silent alif is a spelling convention written after this plural ending. It is an invitation to approach.

12.meaning: 'Let us call / we call (upon)' — a short form of the verb 'to call, summon, or invoke', expressing a 'we' action of calling out to or summoning.
12.grammar: Present-tense verb with the na- prefix meaning 'we'. The clipped ending (the final weak letter dropped, leaving -u on the stem) is the jussive/apocopated mood — the form used after a command particle ('let us…') or a conditional. It conveys 'we summon / let us call'.

13.meaning: 'Our sons / our children' — male offspring (and by extension children), with an attached 'our'.
13.grammar: A plural noun 'sons' carrying the -a (accusative) case ending, the form used for the object of a verb. The attached -na is the possessive pronoun 'our'. It is the broken (irregular) plural of 'son'.

14.meaning: 'And your sons / and your children' — male offspring (and by extension children), joined by 'and' and possessed by 'you (all)'.
14.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the plural noun 'sons' with the -a (accusative) ending used for a verb's object. The attached -kum is the possessive pronoun 'your' addressed to a group (masculine plural).
14.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — son, building, offspring

15.meaning: 'And our women / and our womenfolk' — adult females (women, or the women of one's household), joined by 'and' and possessed by 'us'.
15.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the noun 'women' with the -a (accusative) ending used for a verb's object. The attached -na is the possessive pronoun 'our'. 'Women' is a plural with no singular from the same stem (its singular is supplied by another word).

16.meaning: 'And your women / and your womenfolk' — adult females (women, or the women of one's household), joined by 'and' and possessed by 'you (all)'.
16.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the noun 'women' with the -a (accusative) ending used for a verb's object. The attached -kum is the possessive pronoun 'your' addressed to a group (masculine plural).

17.meaning: 'And ourselves / and our own selves' — a word denoting the self, soul, or very person; in the plural with 'our' it means 'our own selves'.
17.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the plural noun 'selves/souls' with the -a (accusative) ending used for a verb's object. The attached -na is the possessive pronoun 'our'. It is the broken (irregular) plural of nafs ('self, soul').

18.meaning: 'And yourselves / and your own selves' — a word denoting the self, soul, or very person; in the plural with 'your' it means 'your own selves'.
18.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the plural noun 'selves/souls' with the -a (accusative) ending used for a verb's object. The attached -kum is the possessive pronoun 'your' addressed to a group (masculine plural).
18.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person, breath

19.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
19.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

20.meaning: 'Let us pray earnestly / humbly implore' — to beseech Allah fervently and sincerely, pouring out earnest supplication. A short form expressing a 'we' action.
20.grammar: Present-tense (form VIII) verb with the na- prefix meaning 'we'. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, here giving an exhortation ('let us…'). It denotes fervent, humble supplication.

21.meaning: 'So/then let us place / appoint / make' — a short form of the verb 'to make, put, place, or render', prefixed with 'so/then' and expressing a 'we' action.
21.grammar: The prefix fa- ('so/then', marking sequence or result), then the na- prefix meaning 'we', on a present-tense verb. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, fitting an exhortation or consequence ('so let us place…'). It means to set, put, or render something.

22.meaning: 'The curse / condemnation' — a divine curse: being cast out and removed from mercy and blessing.
22.grammar: A singular noun 'curse' made definite by the article al- ('the'), whose lam assimilates into the word-initial lam of laʿnat (shown by the doubled lam with shadda). The -a ending is accusative, the form used for the object of a verb. Because the noun already carries the definite article, it is not in a construct (iḍafa) relationship; the feminine -t (taʾ) simply remains open before the case ending.

23.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
23.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

24.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
24.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
24.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

25.meaning: 'The liars / those who lie' — people characterized by speaking falsehood and denying the truth.
25.grammar: An active participle ('one who lies') made definite by al- ('the'). The -ina ending marks a sound masculine plural; written this way it serves the accusative or genitive case, and here it is genitive — the form used after a preposition or as the second (possessed) term of an 'of' relationship. It names a class of people by their trait: 'the ones who lie'.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
2.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

3.meaning: 'Surely it / indeed it (is)' — an emphatic 'it/he', combining a particle of emphasis ('surely, indeed') with the standalone pronoun 'he/it'.
3.grammar: The emphatic prefix la- ('truly, surely'), attached to the detached pronoun huwa ('he/it', third-person masculine singular). Together they strongly affirm the subject: 'it is most certainly…'.

4.meaning: 'The account / narrative / story' — a true narration of events recounted in sequence; the telling of what happened.
4.grammar: A noun made definite by al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative — the case used when the word is the subject of a sentence or stands as the thing being identified ('it is the account'). It denotes a recounting or relating of events.
4.root: ق-ص-ص (q-ṣ-ṣ) — recounting, relating, following a trail

5.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
5.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
5.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

6.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
6.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: 'A god / a deity' — any object of worship; the general word for a deity (as opposed to the proper name Allah).
8.grammar: A singular indefinite noun 'a god'. The -in ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a/any') and in the genitive case — the form used after a preposition or in an 'of' relationship. It denotes a deity in general.
8.root: ا-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
10.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

11.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
11.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
12.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

13.meaning: 'Surely it / indeed it (is)' — an emphatic 'it/he', combining a particle of emphasis ('surely, indeed') with the standalone pronoun 'he/it'.
13.grammar: The emphatic prefix la- ('truly, surely'), attached to the detached pronoun huwa ('he/it', third-person masculine singular). Together they strongly affirm the subject: 'it is most certainly…'.

14.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
14.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.
14.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, honour, invincibility

15.meaning: The All-Wise — one possessing perfect wisdom, who puts everything in its right place and acts with flawless judgment; can also carry the sense of one who decrees and decides soundly.
15.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) stressing the depth and constancy of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a describing predicate.
15.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, to be wise

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
1.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

2.meaning: 'They turned away / they turned their backs / they turned aside'. It conveys turning oneself away from something, often implying rejection or withdrawal.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine plural: the ending '-aw' means 'they (did) …'. The Form V pattern (with the 'ta-' prefix and doubled middle letter) gives a reflexive sense — turning oneself away. It states a completed act.
2.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near/turn toward; in this form, to turn away

3.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
3.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

5.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
5.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

6.meaning: 'Of/with the corrupters / those who spread corruption' — people who cause ruin, disorder, and moral decay, opposed to setting things right.
6.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/of', here often reinforcing a statement), then the definite al- ('the') on an active participle (form IV, 'one who corrupts'). The -ina ending is a sound masculine plural in the genitive case, required after the preposition. It names a class by their action: 'those who spread corruption'.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'O people of… / O folk of…' — a vocative call ('O!') addressed to the 'people' or 'folk' belonging to something (such as the people of a household, place, or scripture).
2.grammar: The vocative particle ya ('O') used to address or call out, plus the noun 'people/folk'. The -a ending is accusative, which is the case a called-upon noun takes when it is attached to a following word ('O people OF …'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with something.
2.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, those belonging to

3.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
3.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

4.meaning: 'Come! / Come now!' — a call summoning people to approach or come forward, often used to invite a group toward a course of action.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group, masculine plural ('you all'). The -aw ending carries the plural 'you' addressees; the silent alif is a spelling convention written after this plural ending. It is an invitation to approach.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
5.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

6.meaning: 'A word / statement / utterance' — a single meaningful unit of speech: a word, saying, or pronouncement.
6.grammar: A singular feminine indefinite noun 'a word'. The -in ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a/some') and in the genitive case — used after a preposition or in an 'of' relationship. It denotes an utterance or saying.

7.meaning: 'Fair / equitable / common' — even-handed and just; something equal, level, or held in common between parties.
7.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective meaning 'equity, fairness, an even thing'. The -in ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the genitive case — used after a preposition or to describe a preceding genitive noun ('a word that is fair'). It conveys evenness and impartiality.

8.meaning: 'Between us' — the spatial or relational word for 'between/among', with 'us' attached: the space, relation, or matter standing between ourselves.
8.grammar: An adverb of place 'between', fixed in the -a form, with the attached pronoun -na ('us'). Together they mean 'between us / among us', marking a relation linking two or more parties.
8.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

9.meaning: 'And between you' — the word for 'between/among' joined by 'and', with 'you (all)' attached: the space, relation, or matter standing between you.
9.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the adverb of place 'between' (fixed in the -a form), with the attached pronoun -kum ('you', masculine plural). Together they mean 'and between you (all)', marking a relation involving the addressees.
9.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

10.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
10.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

11.meaning: A first-person plural verb meaning 'we worship/serve' — to direct devotion, submission, and obedient service toward a deity, the act of ʿibāda (worship).
11.grammar: Present-tense verb in the 'we' form: the na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The final -a ending is the subjunctive mood, which the verb takes after certain particles (such as 'that', 'so that', 'in order to', or a negating 'not'), giving a sense of an intended, hoped-for, or negated action rather than a plain statement of fact.

12.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
12.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
13.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

14.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

15.meaning: A first-person plural verb meaning 'we associate (something) as a partner' — specifically to set up partners or equals alongside Allah, the act of shirk, the gravest opposite of pure monotheism.
15.grammar: Present-tense verb in the 'we' form: the nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'), the vowel -u- reflecting the verb's stem pattern. The stem itself (Form IV, 'to associate partners with') is built into the verb's shape rather than added by the prefix. The final -a ending is the subjunctive mood, used after particles like 'that' or 'so that', or after a negation — conveying an intended or negated action rather than a simple factual statement.
15.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, take as partner

16.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
16.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

17.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
17.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

18.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
18.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

19.meaning: A third-person masculine singular verb meaning 'he takes/adopts' — to take something for oneself, to seize or adopt it, often in the sense of taking something as a possession or for a particular purpose.
19.grammar: Present-tense verb in the 'he' form: the ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The final -a ending is the subjunctive mood, taken after particles such as 'that' or 'so that', or after a negation — signalling an intended, purposed, or negated action rather than a plain fact.
19.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp

20.meaning: A noun-plus-pronoun meaning 'some of us' or 'a part of us' — baʿḍ denotes a portion, part, or some members of a larger whole, here joined to 'us'.
20.grammar: A noun ('a part, some') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us/our') making it 'some of us'. The -u ending on the noun is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject or doer of a sentence (the one performing the action).

21.meaning: Some, a part, or one of a group — 'another' when paired with 'one'. It singles out an unspecified portion or member set against the rest.

parts.en: some / a part / one (of a group)

21.grammar: A noun meaning 'a part / some'. The -an ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case used for a direct object. Paired with baʿḍ ('another'), it builds the sense 'one another / each other'.
21.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, a portion, some of a whole

22.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'lords' or 'masters' — those who own, command, sustain, and are obeyed; the plural of rabb. Used of beings wrongly set up as objects of obedience and devotion.
22.grammar: A plural noun. The final -an ending (written with the extra alif) is the indefinite accusative: the 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('lords', not 'the lords'), and the accusative case typically marks a direct object of a verb or the second object of verbs like 'to take (X as Y)'.
22.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, own, master; lordship

23.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
23.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

24.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
24.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
24.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

25.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
25.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

26.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
26.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

27.meaning: 'They turned away / they turned their backs / they turned aside'. It conveys turning oneself away from something, often implying rejection or withdrawal.
27.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine plural: the ending '-aw' means 'they (did) …'. The Form V pattern (with the 'ta-' prefix and doubled middle letter) gives a reflexive sense — turning oneself away. It states a completed act.
27.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near/turn toward; in this form, to turn away

28.meaning: A command meaning 'then say / so say' — an order directed to a group to utter or declare something aloud, prefaced by 'then/so' linking it to what precedes.
28.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group, prefixed by fa- ('then, so, and so'). The stem qūl- ('say') is followed by the -ū ending that marks a masculine plural addressee — 'you all, do this'. As a command it directs the listeners to perform the act of speaking.

29.meaning: A command meaning 'bear witness / testify' — an order to a group to witness, attest, or testify to something, to affirm it as true with full awareness.
29.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group. The opening hamza/'i' is a helping vowel to make the command pronounceable; the stem is ish'had- ('bear witness'). The -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all'), directing the group to perform the act of bearing witness.
29.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

30.meaning: A particle-cluster meaning '(testifying/affirming) that we …'. It introduces and emphasizes a statement, asserting firmly that 'we' are the subject of what follows.

parts.en: with / by / in (here introducing the content)

30.grammar: bi- is a versatile preposition ('with, by, in'); joined to anna it introduces the content of a statement or testimony. anna is an emphatic 'that' which strongly asserts the clause it opens. The attached pronoun -nā means 'we'; in writing its nūn merges with the doubled nūn of anna, but the suffix is still nā. After anna it serves as that clause's subject: 'that we …'.

31.meaning: 'Ones who submit / those who surrender themselves to Allah' — the plural of the active participle 'muslim,' i.e. one who willingly submits and devotes himself in obedience to Allah.
31.grammar: A masculine plural active participle (a doer-noun). The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case, the form used when the word stands as the subject or as the predicate naming who/what the subject is.

1.meaning: 'O people of… / O folk of…' — a vocative call ('O!') addressed to the 'people' or 'folk' belonging to something (such as the people of a household, place, or scripture).
1.grammar: The vocative particle ya ('O') used to address or call out, plus the noun 'people/folk'. The -a ending is accusative, which is the case a called-upon noun takes when it is attached to a following word ('O people OF …'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with something.
1.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, those belonging to

2.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
2.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

3.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'why? / for what reason?' — a question asking the cause or purpose of something. It is formed from the preposition 'for/about' fused with the question-word 'what'.
3.grammar: A question particle built from li- ('for, about') joined to mā ('what'); when these combine, the long vowel of 'what' is shortened to give li-ma ('for what?, why?'). It opens a question seeking a reason or motive.

4.meaning: A second-person plural verb meaning 'you argue / dispute' — to wrangle, debate, or contend with one another using arguments and proofs, the act of ḥijāj (disputation).
4.grammar: Present-tense verb of mutual action (the long ā in the pattern signals doing something back-and-forth with another). The stem ends at the doubled jīm (ḥājj-), and the tu-…-ūna frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The full -ūna ending is the indicative mood, used for a plain statement or genuine question about something actually happening.
4.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — to argue, present a proof, dispute

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (the Prophet Abraham).
6.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -a ending here serves for both accusative and genitive because the name is a diptote — a class of nouns that refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a for these two cases. So this one -a covers 'Ibrāhīm' whether as an object or as 'of Ibrāhīm'.

7.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

8.meaning: A passive verb meaning 'it (feminine) was sent down / revealed' — to be caused to descend; used of revelation and of things sent down from on high.
8.grammar: A past-tense passive verb ('was sent down') from a causative pattern (to make something descend). The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject — the thing sent down is grammatically feminine. The final vowel appears here as -i (rather than silent -t) as a helping vowel that eases pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting alif.
8.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (causative) to send down

9.meaning: A proper noun: the Torah (al-Tawrāt) — the scripture revealed to Moses (Mūsā).
9.grammar: A definite proper noun carrying the prefix al- ('the'); its 'l' sound assimilates into the following 't'. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence (e.g. the thing that 'was sent down').

10.meaning: A proper noun meaning 'and the Gospel' (al-Injīl) — the scripture revealed to Jesus (ʿĪsā), joined by 'and'.
10.grammar: A definite proper noun: wa- ('and') links it to a preceding word, and al- ('the') makes it definite. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence (the thing that 'was sent down').

11.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
11.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

12.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
12.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

13.meaning: 'After him / it' — 'baʿd' denotes what comes afterward in time or sequence, here joined to 'him/it'.
13.grammar: A time-noun 'baʿd' (afterness) with an attached pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. The '-i' vowel on 'baʿd' is its case ending, set by 'baʿd's' own position in the sentence (commonly governed by a preceding preposition), not by the suffix; the attached '-hi' is the possessor ('him/it'), and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive. The pronoun's 'i'-vowel (-hi rather than -hu) follows because it comes after a genitive '-i'.

14.meaning: 'Then will you not…?' — a rhetorical opener combining 'then/so,' a question, and a negation, used to prompt reflection ('do you then not…?').
14.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb: the question marker 'a-' ('?'), the connector 'fa-' ('then/so'), and the negator 'lā' ('not'). Together they form a rhetorical question expecting agreement — 'will you then not…?' It has no case or tense ending of its own.

15.meaning: 'You understand / use reason' — to comprehend, think, and grasp matters with the intellect; to apply sound reasoning.
15.grammar: The prefix 'ta-' marks a 2nd-person present-tense verb, and the '-ūna' ending makes the subject a masculine-inclusive plural 'you all.' The '-ūna' is the indicative marker, signalling a plain factual or ongoing statement.
15.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to reason, understand, be intelligent

1.meaning: An attention-drawing phrase meaning 'here you are! / lo, you are these' — a particle of alerting ('here, behold') fused to the pronoun 'you (plural)', used to call attention to the addressees and their situation.
1.grammar: Built from the alerting particle hā ('here!, behold!') prefixed to the standalone pronoun antum ('you', masculine plural). The pronoun antum is the form used for the subject/topic — 'you all'. Together they draw attention: 'Here you are, you are the ones who…'.

2.meaning: 'These' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things that are near ('these ones, these here').
2.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'these,' used for near things or people (of either gender). It is built on a fixed base, but its final vowel reflects case: the -i here is the genitive form (hāʾulāʾi), required because it falls in a genitive position governed by the preceding preposition. This contrasts with the nominative form hāʾulāʾu — so the -i is a genuine case marker, not merely a connecting vowel.

3.meaning: A second-person plural past verb meaning 'you argued / disputed' — you contended with one another by way of argument and proof (the act of ḥijāj).
3.grammar: A past-tense verb of mutual action (the long ā signals doing something back-and-forth with another party). The suffix -tum marks a second-person masculine plural subject who did the action — 'you all argued'.
3.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — to argue, present a proof, dispute

4.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
4.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

5.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

6.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
6.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'knowledge' — sure, established knowing; awareness of facts based on evidence, the opposite of ignorance or guesswork.
7.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative: the 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('some knowledge', not 'the knowledge'), and the nominative case typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing whose existence is being affirmed.

8.meaning: 'Then why? / so for what reason?' — a compound asking the reason for something, combining 'then/so' with the interrogative 'why / for what.'
8.grammar: A question word, not a verb. It joins 'fa-' ('then/so') with the preposition 'li-' ('for') and the interrogative 'mā' ('what') — which loses its long vowel when a preposition is attached, giving 'lima' ('for what / why'). The whole expression asks for a reason.

9.meaning: A second-person plural verb meaning 'you argue / dispute' — to wrangle, debate, or contend with one another using arguments and proofs, the act of ḥijāj (disputation).
9.grammar: Present-tense verb of mutual action (the long ā in the pattern signals doing something back-and-forth with another). The stem ends at the doubled jīm (ḥājj-), and the tu-…-ūna frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The full -ūna ending is the indicative mood, used for a plain statement or genuine question about something actually happening.
9.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — to argue, present a proof, dispute

10.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
10.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

11.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
11.grammar: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.

12.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
12.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

13.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
13.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

14.meaning: A noun meaning 'knowledge' — sure, established knowing; awareness of facts based on evidence, the opposite of ignorance or guesswork.
14.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative: the 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('some knowledge', not 'the knowledge'), and the nominative case typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing whose existence is being affirmed.
14.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge

15.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
15.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
15.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

16.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
16.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
16.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

17.meaning: And you / while you (all) — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), often introducing an accompanying circumstance ('while you …').
17.grammar: The conjunction wa- joined to the detached subject pronoun 'you all' (masculine). This standalone pronoun stands as a subject or for emphasis; it has a fixed form and does not change for case. With wa- it can mark a simultaneous state ('and you / while you').

18.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
18.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

19.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
19.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.
19.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, knowledge

1.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
1.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: A proper noun: Abraham (Ibrāhīm), the patriarch and prophet, exalted as an upright monotheist and 'friend of Allah'.
3.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence. Because it is a foreign proper name, it is 'diptote' — it does not take the indefinite 'n' sound (tanwīn) that ordinary nouns would.

4.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'a Jew, a Jewish person' — one belonging to the Jewish community or faith (Yahūdī).
4.grammar: A noun of belonging formed with the -iyy ending (which means 'belonging to, characterized by'). The final -an (written with the extra alif) is the indefinite accusative: the 'n' sound marks it as indefinite ('a Jew'), and the accusative case typically marks a direct object or, after verbs of 'being/becoming', the description of the subject.
4.root: ه-و-د (h-w-d) — relating to the Jewish people/faith

5.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
5.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

6.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'a Christian' — one belonging to the Christian community or faith (Naṣrānī).
6.grammar: A noun of belonging formed with the -iyy ending ('belonging to, characterized by'). The final -an (written with the extra alif) is the indefinite accusative: the 'n' sound marks it as indefinite ('a Christian'), and the accusative case typically marks a direct object or the description that follows verbs of 'being/becoming'.
6.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid (associated with the Christians, an-Naṣārā)

7.meaning: 'but / however' — a particle that introduces a contrast or correction, setting what follows against what was just said. The opening 'wa-' connects it ('and').
7.grammar: A contrasting particle ('but, however') that signals a turn against the preceding idea. It does not change endings on words; it simply introduces a corrective or opposing clause. The 'wa-' prefix links it to what came before.

8.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

8.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

9.meaning: 'Upright in faith, naturally inclined to pure monotheism' — one who turns away from all false worship toward sincere devotion to the one Allah; a term for steadfast, primordial monotheistic faith.
9.grammar: A singular indefinite noun/adjective (an intensive 'faʿīl' pattern). The -an ending is accusative plus nunation: it marks indefiniteness ('a/an') and the accusative case, the form used for an object, a descriptive term, or a circumstantial state ('… as one upright in faith').
9.root: ح-ن-ف (ḥ-n-f) — to incline away (from error) toward pure monotheism

10.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'one who submits, a Muslim' — someone who surrenders themselves wholly to Allah in willing obedience; the active doer of islām (submission).
10.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun, with the mu- prefix marking 'one who does X') from a verb meaning 'to submit/surrender oneself'. The final -an (written with the extra alif) is the indefinite accusative: the 'n' sound marks it as indefinite ('a Muslim'), and the accusative case typically marks a direct object or the description following verbs of 'being/becoming'.
10.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — to be safe/whole; (this pattern) to submit, surrender

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

12.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

12.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

13.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
13.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

14.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
14.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.
14.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, partner

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: A comparative meaning 'more entitled, nearer, more deserving' — having a closer claim or greater right to something; the most fitting or worthiest.
2.grammar: A comparative/superlative form on the pattern 'more/most ___' (the same shape as 'greater', 'nearer'). It is built from a root meaning closeness and is typically followed by 'to/with' to name what one has a stronger claim upon. Its ending does not change for case (it is fixed), as is normal for words ending in this long -ā.
2.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near, be an ally/guardian; closeness

3.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
3.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
3.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

4.meaning: A proper noun with a preposition meaning 'with/to Abraham' — the patriarch-prophet Ibrāhīm, governed by the preposition 'with, in respect of'.
4.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by, in respect of') attached to the proper name Abraham. After a preposition a noun takes the genitive case; for an ordinary noun this would show as -i, but because 'Abraham' is a foreign proper name (diptote) its genitive is marked with -a instead, and it takes no 'n' sound (tanwīn).

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'surely those who / indeed they who' — an emphatic 'truly/indeed' joined to the relative word 'those who', which introduces a description of a group of people.
5.grammar: The emphatic prefix la- ('surely, truly') attached to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), masculine plural — used to point to a group and then describe them by what follows. The relative pronoun has a fixed ending and does not change for case. (When la- joins it, the initial 'a' of the pronoun is dropped in writing.)

6.meaning: A past verb plus object meaning 'they followed him' — to follow, go after, adhere to, and conform to someone, taking them as a guide or example (the act of ittibāʿ).
6.grammar: A past-tense verb in an intensive 'self-involving' pattern (to take up following for oneself); the stem is ittabaʿ-. The -ū suffix marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they did it'), and the attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him/it'. So: 'they followed him'.
6.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

7.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and this (one)' — the pointing word 'this' (for something near, masculine/neutral) joined to 'and'.
7.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to the demonstrative hādhā ('this'), used to point to something near at hand (masculine singular). A demonstrative like this has a fixed ending and does not change for grammatical case; it can stand as a subject or be linked to a following noun ('this ___').

8.meaning: The Prophet — a person to whom Allah sends revelation and a divinely guided message for humankind. The word denotes one who conveys tidings from Allah, or (on another derivation) one of high and exalted rank.
8.grammar: A definite singular noun marked by the prefixed 'al-' ('the'). The doubling (shadda) on the nūn is not part of the base word: it results from the 'l' of 'al-' assimilating into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), so 'al-nabiyy' is pronounced 'an-nabiyy'. The base noun is نَبِيّ (nabiyy). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or the one being described.
8.root: Two derivations are held by grammarians: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings, weighty information (one who brings tidings); or ن-ب-و (n-b-w) — to be high or elevated (one of exalted rank), favoured by those who note the doubled yāʾ pointing to an original wāw.

9.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
9.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
10.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

11.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
11.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
11.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

12.meaning: A protector, guardian, ally, and intimate helper; one who is close and takes charge of another's affairs, supporting and safeguarding them.
12.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that is being described ("… is the protector"). The pattern denotes one who possesses the quality intensely.
12.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, alliance, guardianship, taking charge of another

13.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
13.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

1.meaning: She wished, longed for, or fondly desired something. The verb conveys an inner yearning or affectionate wish that something be so.
1.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The '-at' ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject — 'she' did the action, or an action done by a grammatically feminine noun.

2.meaning: A group, party, or faction — a distinct band or section of people, often a smaller portion of a larger body.
2.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a group', not 'the group') and in the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence.
2.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, circle; a portion that moves about

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

4.meaning: People of / folk of / those belonging to — the family, followers, or possessors of something (as in 'people of the Book'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with a thing.
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/folk of'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('people OF …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.
4.root: ء-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, people belonging to

5.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
5.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

6.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

7.meaning: They cause (you) to go astray — they lead away from the right path into error or misguidance. The verb describes actively making someone lose their way.
7.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the causative pattern (to 'make' someone stray). The '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the attached '-kum' is the object 'you (all)'.
7.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

8.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
8.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

9.meaning: They cause to go astray — they lead others away from the right path into error. The verb describes actively misguiding people.
9.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the causative pattern (to 'make' someone stray). The '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') and signals the verb is in its full (indicative) form, used for ongoing or factual statements.
9.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

10.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
10.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

11.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
11.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

12.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
12.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'they perceive / they are aware / they sense.' The root denotes fine, immediate awareness — noticing or feeling something, often subconsciously. It frequently appears in the negative, expressing that people fail to realize something.

parts.en: perceive / sense / be aware (Form I stem)

13.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, Form I (imperfect stem yashʿuru, with -u- after the second root letter), third-person masculine plural. The prefix 'ya-' and ending -ūna give 'they (masc.) do / are doing,' the -ūna marking the indicative — an ongoing or habitual state of awareness (or, when negated, the lack of it).
13.root: ش-ع-ر (sh-ʿ-r) — to perceive, sense, be finely aware

1.meaning: 'O people of… / O folk of…' — a vocative call ('O!') addressed to the 'people' or 'folk' belonging to something (such as the people of a household, place, or scripture).
1.grammar: The vocative particle ya ('O') used to address or call out, plus the noun 'people/folk'. The -a ending is accusative, which is the case a called-upon noun takes when it is attached to a following word ('O people OF …'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with something.
1.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, those belonging to

2.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
2.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

3.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'why? / for what reason?' — a question asking the cause or purpose of something. It is formed from the preposition 'for/about' fused with the question-word 'what'.
3.grammar: A question particle built from li- ('for, about') joined to mā ('what'); when these combine, the long vowel of 'what' is shortened to give li-ma ('for what?, why?'). It opens a question seeking a reason or motive.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'you disbelieve', 'you reject faith', or 'you are ungrateful' — to refuse to believe, to deny the truth, or to be ungrateful, addressed to a group.
4.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks the second person ('you') and the -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural subject in the indicative mood (ongoing or habitual action). The root joins the ideas of denying faith and being ungrateful — covering over a truth or a blessing.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to disbelieve, deny, be ungrateful, cover over

5.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
5.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
5.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: And you / while you (all) — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), often introducing an accompanying circumstance ('while you …').
7.grammar: The conjunction wa- joined to the detached subject pronoun 'you all' (masculine). This standalone pronoun stands as a subject or for emphasis; it has a fixed form and does not change for case. With wa- it can mark a simultaneous state ('and you / while you').

8.meaning: You bear witness, you testify — to witness with your own eyes and then affirm or attest to it. The verb joins seeing/being present with giving testimony.
8.grammar: Present/future-tense verb addressed to a group ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks second person 'you'; the -ūna ending marks masculine-plural subjects and the indicative mood (a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action), as opposed to a command or a subjunctive/jussive that drops the final -na.
8.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, be present, testify

1.meaning: 'O people of… / O folk of…' — a vocative call ('O!') addressed to the 'people' or 'folk' belonging to something (such as the people of a household, place, or scripture).
1.grammar: The vocative particle ya ('O') used to address or call out, plus the noun 'people/folk'. The -a ending is accusative, which is the case a called-upon noun takes when it is attached to a following word ('O people OF …'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with something.
1.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, those belonging to

2.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
2.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

3.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'why? / for what reason?' — a question asking the cause or purpose of something. It is formed from the preposition 'for/about' fused with the question-word 'what'.
3.grammar: A question particle built from li- ('for, about') joined to mā ('what'); when these combine, the long vowel of 'what' is shortened to give li-ma ('for what?, why?'). It opens a question seeking a reason or motive.

4.meaning: You (plural) mix up, confound, or obscure — to blend one thing with another so that truth and falsehood become indistinguishable, or to dress something in a disguise.
4.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and the full ending signals the indicative form used for factual or habitual action.
4.root: ل-ب-س (l-b-s) — to clothe, cover; to confuse, obscure

5.meaning: The truth — that which is real, right, and established; reality, the just due, the genuine as opposed to the false.
5.grammar: A definite noun with 'the'. The -a ending is the accusative, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the truth').
5.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is established and real

6.meaning: With / by falsehood — 'the false, the vain, the baseless' joined to a preposition and 'the'.
6.grammar: The preposition bi- joined to the definite noun 'the falsehood' (an active participle meaning 'that which is null/vain'). The -i ending is the genitive, required because the noun follows the preposition.
6.root: ب-ط-ل (b-ṭ-l) — to be void, false, vain, of no effect

7.meaning: And you (plural) conceal, hide, or suppress — to keep something secret and withhold it from others, especially knowledge or truth.
7.grammar: A present/future-tense verb joined by the prefix 'wa-' ('and'). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and the full ending signals the indicative form used for factual or ongoing action.

8.meaning: The truth — that which is real, right, and established; reality, the just due, the genuine as opposed to the false.
8.grammar: A definite noun with 'the'. The -a ending is the accusative, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the truth').
8.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is established and real

9.meaning: And you / while you (all) — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), often introducing an accompanying circumstance ('while you …').
9.grammar: The conjunction wa- joined to the detached subject pronoun 'you all' (masculine). This standalone pronoun stands as a subject or for emphasis; it has a fixed form and does not change for case. With wa- it can mark a simultaneous state ('and you / while you').

10.meaning: You know / you are aware; to possess knowledge or recognition of something (a group).
10.grammar: A Form I present-tense verb. The ta-…-ūna frame means 'you all (do)' for a group, with the final -na marking the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact (you know / you are aware).

1.meaning: And she said / and a (feminine) group said — introducing speech that was spoken or declared.
1.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb joined by 'wa-' ('and'). The '-at' ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject — 'she' said, or an action attributed to a grammatically feminine noun.

2.meaning: A group, party, or faction — a distinct band or section of people, often a smaller portion of a larger body.
2.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a group', not 'the group') and in the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence.
2.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, circle; a portion that moves about

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

4.meaning: People of / folk of / those belonging to — the family, followers, or possessors of something (as in 'people of the Book'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with a thing.
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/folk of'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('people OF …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.
4.root: ء-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, people belonging to

5.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
5.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

6.meaning: 'Believe!' — a command to a group: have faith, trust, and affirm. Built on the verb meaning to attain security and to believe, it calls people to embrace faith.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the verb meaning 'to believe / to have faith'. The -ū ending directs the command to a second-person masculine plural audience, 'you all — believe!'.

7.meaning: A combination meaning 'with/for the one that' or 'in exchange for that which'. It fuses the preposition bi- (with, by, in exchange for) onto the masculine singular relative pronoun alladhī ('the one who/that'), introducing a clause that further identifies the referred-to thing.

parts.en: the one who/that (masc. sing. relative pronoun)

7.grammar: bi- is a preposition that always governs a genitive; alladhī is an indeclinable masculine singular relative pronoun whose form does not change for case. It points to a single masculine entity and requires a following clause to complete its sense ('the one that …').

8.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
8.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
8.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

9.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
9.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
9.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

10.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
10.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
11.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

12.meaning: Face — literally the front of the head; figuratively the foremost part, the outset, or the direction one turns toward.
12.grammar: A singular noun. The '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or signals an adverbial sense such as time or manner.
12.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, front, direction one turns to

13.meaning: The daytime — the bright span of hours when the sun is up, from dawn to sunset; the natural counterpart of night.
13.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the,' with its 'l' assimilated into the following 'n'). The final '-i' is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the day') or as following a preposition or a particle that governs the genitive.
