The tu- prefix marks both the present tense and the passive voice ('is being …-ed'), so the doer is unnamed and the focus is on what undergoes the action. The stem -tlā keeps the second root consonant (t) and ends in a long ā written with ى, the shape a weak-final (defective) root takes when no further ending is attached.
4.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

5.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
5.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

6.meaning: "signs / verses / tokens" — the plural of āya, a 'sign' or evident token that points to something beyond itself; it also denotes a verse of revelation, each one a sign.
6.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks sound feminine plural). The final -u is the nominative case, the form taken as the subject of a sentence or the leading term of a possessive chain ('the signs OF …').

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: And in/among you (plural) — placing something within a group of people or in their midst.
8.grammar: A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in/among', which is followed by the attached pronoun -kum meaning 'you' for a group (masculine plural). After a preposition this pronoun stands in the genitive (object) position, so the whole phrase means 'and in/among you all'.
8.root: — (particle/preposition)

9.meaning: His Messenger — one who is sent to deliver a message, here belonging to 'Him'.
9.grammar: A noun 'messenger' carrying the -u (nominative) ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or the thing being identified ('… is the one who …'). The attached pronoun -hu means 'his', linking the messenger to a male owner ('His messenger').

10.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
10.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

11.meaning: He holds fast, grips firmly, takes secure hold of something for protection or support.

parts.en: hold firmly, cling for protection (form VIII stem)

11.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he holds firmly'). The ya- prefix marks 'he' as the doer (the doubling sometimes seen in the script is a recitation mark, not a true consonant doubling). The bare final consonant with no added vowel (jussive form) is the shape the verb takes after conditional or commanding particles, often giving the sense 'whoever holds firm…'. The pattern (form VIII) adds a reflexive, self-involving nuance: to take firm hold for one's own protection.
11.root: ع-ص-م (ʿ-ṣ-m) — to protect, hold fast, preserve

12.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
12.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
12.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

13.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
13.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

14.meaning: He has been guided — shown and led to the right way by someone else.

parts.en: weak-root ending of a 3rd-person masc. sing. past verb

14.grammar: A past-tense passive verb, third person masculine singular ('he was guided'). The internal vowel shape (ḍamma then kasra, the hu-…-i- pattern) marks the passive: the action is received, not done, so the guide is unnamed and the person is the one led. The subject 'he' is carried by a zero ending (no added suffix); the final -ya is the vowelled form of the weak final root letter, not a person marker.
14.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
15.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

16.meaning: 'A path / road / way'. It denotes a clear, open road that one travels — often used figuratively for a course of life or conduct.
16.grammar: The '-in' ending (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('a path / some way') and in the genitive case. The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

17.meaning: Straight, upright, undeviating — a path or course that runs true without bending or wandering.

parts.en: being/standing straight (form X stem of q-w-m)

17.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word) describing something as 'straight/upright', built on form X of the root, whose verb (istaqāma) simply means 'to be or become straight'. The musta- prefix marks the one possessing that quality, and the stem -qīm comes from the root with its weak middle letter appearing as ī. The -in ending is both indefinite ('a …') and genitive, the case used after a preposition or when the word follows and describes another noun ('… of a straight …').
17.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: Be mindful and wary of — guard yourselves by placing a protective barrier between yourselves and harm or wrongdoing. This is the verb of taqwā: God-conscious caution that shields one from what is forbidden.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group ('you all'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you.' Built on a reflexive pattern (Form VIII), it conveys 'protect yourselves / be on guard.'

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: Due right, just measure, rightful claim; that which is true and rightly owed — here used to mean 'as is truly its due'.
6.grammar: A noun meaning 'truth, right, due'. The final -a (accusative) often marks the object of a verb, and in a possessive phrase like this it commonly conveys the sense 'with the full right/due OF …', i.e. as something deserves to be done.
6.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is due and real

7.meaning: The reverent fear and dutiful mindfulness owed to Him — a guarding awareness that one keeps toward Allah, attached here to 'Him'.
7.grammar: A noun for the proper, God-fearing reverence due to someone. It is the first term of a possessive (iḍāfa) construction, and that construction is what puts it in the genitive, shown by the -i on its final letter; the following pronoun -hi ('his / of Him') is the possessor. So the phrase means 'the reverent fear due to Him'. The pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows an i-vowel.
7.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield (the root behind taqwā)

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: You will surely die / you shall most certainly die — the verb 'to die' addressed to a group ('you all'), carrying heavy emphasis that the dying will inevitably happen.
9.grammar: A present/future verb, second-person masculine plural, with the heavy emphatic ending. Without emphasis the form would be tamūtūna ('you all die'): the 'ta-' prefix marks the 'you' subject and the long -ūna marks the masculine plural. Before the doubled emphatic -nna, that plural -ūna loses its nūn and its vowel shortens, leaving only the residual damma (-u) shown here — so the -u is the remnant of the plural suffix, not part of the bare stem. The -nna ending stresses that the action will most certainly occur and fixes the verb's mood.

10.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
10.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

11.meaning: And you / while you (all) — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), often introducing an accompanying circumstance ('while you …').
11.grammar: The conjunction wa- joined to the detached subject pronoun 'you all' (masculine). This standalone pronoun stands as a subject or for emphasis; it has a fixed form and does not change for case. With wa- it can mark a simultaneous state ('and you / while you').

12.meaning: Ones who submit / are submitted — those in a state of willing surrender and peace toward Allah (the people described by the word 'Muslim'). Plural, referring to people.
12.grammar: An active participle (a 'one-who-does' word) in the sound masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks the plural in its subject form — the form used when the word is the doer or the thing being described (as a predicate); the parallel object/'of' form would be -īna.
12.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — peace, safety, wholeness; to submit

1.meaning: And hold fast! — a command to a group to grip firmly and cling for protection and security.

parts.en: hold firmly, cling for protection (form VIII command stem)
you all (do it!) — plural command ending

1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group: 'and hold firmly, all of you!'. The -ū ending marks a plural masculine command ('you all do it'). The verb is form VIII, which adds a reflexive sense — to take firm hold for one's own protection. The word begins with a helping (elidable) alif that lets its consonant cluster be pronounced; after the connector 'and' that helping vowel drops out in speech.
1.root: ع-ص-م (ʿ-ṣ-m) — to protect, hold fast, preserve

2.meaning: By/with the rope or cord — a cord viewed as something to grasp, by extension a bond, covenant, or lifeline of connection.
2.grammar: The preposition 'with/by/to' attached to the noun 'rope'. Any noun after this preposition takes the -i (genitive) ending, which is why it appears here; the genitive also sets it up to be linked to a following noun ('the rope OF …'). The word can mean a literal cord or, figuratively, a binding tie or covenant.

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

5.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
5.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

6.meaning: They split into factions, broke apart, became scattered and divided.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine plural ('they became divided'). The -ū ending marks 'they' as the doers. The pattern (form V, with the ta- prefix and a doubled middle root letter) is reflexive/resultative of the simpler 'to divide': the action falls back on the doers themselves, so they ended up split apart into separate groups.

7.meaning: A command to a group meaning 'and remember / and call to mind / and mention.' The root spans both calling something to memory and uttering it aloud.
7.grammar: The connector 'wa' (and) plus a command (imperative) verb 'remember/mention.' The ending -ū addresses a masculine plural group ('you all remember!').
7.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

8.meaning: A favor, blessing, or grace bestowed; the bounty and kindness shown by a giver, especially the abundant gifts of Allah.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun ('favor'). The final tā' is pronounced (rather than as silent -h) because the word is in a construct chain, joining to a following noun ('the favor of …'); the -a ending here marks the accusative case, typical of a direct object.
8.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — favor, blessing, comfort, grace

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
10.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
11.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

12.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
12.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

13.meaning: Enemies — those locked in hostility or opposition; the plural of 'enemy'.
13.grammar: A plural noun 'enemies' with the -an ending, which marks it as indefinite ('enemies') and in the accusative case. The accusative is the case used for the direct object of a verb or, very commonly, for a word that states what someone became or how they ended up ('became enemies').

14.meaning: Then He joined together, united and reconciled — bringing things into harmony and close bonding, especially hearts.
14.grammar: The connector 'then/so' attached to a past-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('then He united'). In Arabic the 'he' subject of a past verb is shown by a zero ending (no added suffix); the final -a is simply the vowel on the last root letter. The doubled middle root (form II) makes the verb causative and intensive: to actively bring separate things together into harmony.
14.root: أ-ل-ف (ʾ-l-f) — to join, unite, become familiar/intimate

15.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
15.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
15.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

16.meaning: Your hearts — the inner seat of feeling, intention, and understanding, belonging to a group of people.
16.grammar: A plural noun 'hearts' carrying the -i (genitive) ending because it is the first term of a possessive (iḍāfa) construction with the following pronoun -kum ('your', for a group). This noun-plus-pronoun pairing expresses possession: 'the hearts OF you all' = 'your hearts'. In Arabic the heart is understood as the center of both emotion and thought.
16.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, change

17.meaning: Then you (plural) became, came to be, ended up in a new state — originally 'to enter the morning', widely used to mean simply 'to become'.
17.grammar: The connector 'then/so' attached to a past-tense verb with the ending -tum, which marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers of a completed action. This verb belongs to the family of 'becoming' verbs: it reports a change of state and normally introduces a description of what the people became.
17.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning, daybreak; to come to be

18.meaning: By His favor, grace, or blessing — a bestowed kindness or benefit, here attributed to 'Him'.
18.grammar: The preposition 'by/with' attached to the noun 'favor/blessing'. The noun takes the -i (genitive) ending here both because it follows the preposition and because it is the first term of a possessive construction with the pronoun that follows. The attached pronoun -hi means 'his' ('His favor'); it appears as -hi rather than -hu because it follows an i-vowel. Together: 'by His grace'.
18.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — blessing, favor, comfort, grace

19.meaning: Brothers — kin or close companions bound in brotherhood; the plural of 'brother', often used for spiritual or fraternal closeness rather than only blood relation.
19.grammar: A plural noun 'brothers' with the -an ending, marking it as indefinite and accusative. The accusative is the case used for a direct object or, commonly, to state what people became or how they turned out ('became brothers'). This particular plural carries the warm sense of brotherhood and fellowship.
19.root: أ-خ-و (ʾ-kh-w) — brother, brotherhood

20.meaning: And you (plural) were — reporting a past state or ongoing condition of a group of people.
20.grammar: The connector 'and' attached to the past tense of the verb 'to be'. The ending -tum marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the subject. This verb sets up a description of a state in the past ('you all were …'), and it typically introduces the condition or situation that followed.
20.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come into being

21.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
21.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

22.meaning: The edge, brink, or rim of something — the very lip of a drop or hollow, the point right before falling in.
22.grammar: A noun meaning 'edge/brink'. It ends in a fixed long ā and does not change its shape for case, so the ending carries no separate case marker. It commonly stands in front of another noun to mean 'the edge OF …', evoking the narrow margin at the very lip of something.

23.meaning: A pit, hollow, or dug-out hole in the ground.
23.grammar: A noun 'pit/hole' with the -in ending, marking it as indefinite ('a pit') and genitive. The genitive is the case a noun takes when it follows and is possessed by another noun ('the edge OF a pit') or comes after a preposition. The root sense is of something hollowed out by digging.
23.root: ح-ف-ر (ḥ-f-r) — to dig, hollow out; a pit

24.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
24.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

25.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
25.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

26.meaning: Then He rescued you (plural), saved and pulled you out from danger or destruction.
26.grammar: The connector 'then/so' attached to a past-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('then He rescued'). The 'he' subject is shown by a zero ending; the -a before the pronoun is the vowel on the last root letter, not a separate person marker. The attached pronoun -kum ('you all') is the object — the ones rescued. The pattern (form IV) is causative: to bring about someone's deliverance, to pull them to safety.

27.meaning: From it / from her — marking the starting point or source out of which something comes, referring to a feminine or grammatically-feminine thing.
27.grammar: The preposition 'from/out of' attached to the pronoun -hā ('it/her'), which refers back to a feminine or grammatically-feminine noun. After a preposition this pronoun stands in the genitive (object) position, giving the sense 'from it' — the source or point of departure of an action.
27.root: — (particle/preposition)

28.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
28.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
28.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

29.meaning: He makes clear / He explains; to set something forth plainly so that its meaning is evident.
29.grammar: A Form II present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain, ongoing statement of fact (he makes clear / he is making clear).
29.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness, making evident

30.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
30.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

31.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
31.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

32.meaning: 'His signs / His verses.' The plural of a word meaning a sign, token, or mark that points to a greater reality — also used for the verses of revelation — here joined to 'his'.
32.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form this plural takes when it follows a preposition or is linked as the object of a possessor; the -hi ('his') marks ownership: 'his signs'.
32.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark; a verse of revelation

33.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

33.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

34.meaning: 'You (plural) are/become guided' — to be led on the right path, to find and follow correct direction. The verb conveys accepting guidance and being set straight, not merely knowing the way but walking it.
34.grammar: A present-tense verb (form VIII) addressed to a group. The ta- prefix marks second person ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural in the indicative mood — the ordinary, factual mood used when a verb is not negated or subordinated by a particle that would clip its ending. So it means 'you (all) are guided / become rightly guided.'
34.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, to lead rightly

1.meaning: And let there be — a directive that something should come into existence or be brought about.
1.grammar: The connector 'and' plus the particle of command 'let', joined to the present-tense verb 'to be' in the third person feminine singular ('let it/she be'). The 'let' particle turns the statement into an indirect command — a wish or instruction that something exist — and pulls the verb into its bare jussive form, ending in a plain consonant with no added vowel.
1.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come into being

2.meaning: 'From you / among you (plural)' — indicating a part taken out of, or belonging to, a group of people being addressed.
2.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun -kum ('you all,' masculine plural). Together they express partition or origin: a part drawn 'from / among' the addressed group.

3.meaning: 'A community / a nation, a people' — a body of people bound together as a single group, often by shared faith, way, or era.
3.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -un ending is nominative plus nunation: the -n sound signals 'a/an' (indefinite), and the -u marks the nominative case, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being named.
3.root: ء-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — to head toward; a community, way, model

4.meaning: They call, invite, summon, or appeal — calling others toward something, or calling upon someone.

parts.en: call, invite, summon (stem with weak root letter as long ū)

4.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, third person masculine plural ('they call/invite'). The ya- prefix together with the -na ending marks 'they' (a group) as the doers of an ongoing or repeated action (the doubling sometimes shown in the script is a recitation mark, not a true consonant doubling). The stem's final long ū is the weak root letter (w) appearing as a vowel. The verb can mean to invite people toward something or to call upon someone in supplication.
4.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invite, summon, supplicate

5.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
5.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

6.meaning: The good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a quality or as desirable things.
6.grammar: The definite article 'the' attached to the noun 'good/goodness', which carries the -i (genitive) ending. Here the genitive is governed by a preceding preposition meaning 'toward', so the phrase reads 'toward the good'. The word covers both moral goodness and beneficial things in general.
6.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, to choose what is best

7.meaning: And they command, order, or bid — expressing the act of instructing others to do something, often with the sense of urging good conduct.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb. The wa- prefix means 'and'. The base ya- prefix marks third person ('he/they'), and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the present/ongoing tense: 'they command'. This ending signals an unfinished or habitual action by a group of males.

8.meaning: 'In a fitting / honourable / customary way' — bi- ('with/in') joined to al-ma'rūf, literally 'that which is known and recognised', i.e. what is right, decent, and approved by sound custom and morality.

parts.en: what is right / recognised as good

8.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition 'with / in'. The l- is 'the'. The stem is a passive participle meaning 'that which is known/recognised (as good)'. The final -i is the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition like bi-.
8.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognise; hence what is recognised as good

9.meaning: And they forbid, prohibit, or restrain — the act of holding others back from something, the natural counterpart to commanding.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb. The wa- prefix means 'and'. The ya- prefix marks third person ('he/they'). The root ends in a weak letter (-y), which surfaces as a wāw within the stem (yanhaw-); the masculine plural present subject is then marked by the ending -na ('they'), in the present/ongoing tense: 'they forbid'.

10.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
10.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

11.meaning: That which is rejected, disapproved, and recognized as wrong — what sound nature and revelation deem objectionable; 'the wrong' or 'the reprehensible'.
11.grammar: A noun (originally a passive participle, 'that which is denied/rejected') with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.

12.meaning: 'And those' — the connective 'and' joined to the demonstrative 'those'. It both links to what precedes and points out a group ('and it is those who…').
12.grammar: A connecting particle wa ('and') prefixed to a plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. The wa simply joins what follows to what came before. The demonstrative is fixed in form (no case endings), and its -ka element marks distance; it may refer to people of either gender.

13.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
13.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

14.meaning: 'The successful / the ones who flourish' — those who attain what they seek and are saved from what they fear. The underlying sense is of prospering, thriving, and winning through to lasting wellbeing and salvation, not merely worldly success.
14.grammar: A definite active participle (Form IV) in the masculine plural: 'the ones who succeed/prosper'. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate identifying who someone is.
14.root: ف-ل-ح (f-l-ḥ) — to prosper, succeed, thrive

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: You (plural) are / you happen to be. A form of the 'hollow' verb kāna ('to be'), which links a subject to a state or description, or expresses simply being or existing.
2.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The dropping of the usual final -na (so takūnū rather than takūnūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form expected after conditional or subordinating particles.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

3.meaning: Like those who — a comparison particle joined to a relative pronoun, meaning 'similar to the ones who…' and pointing to a group defined by what follows.
3.grammar: A compound of the preposition ka- ('like, as'), expressing resemblance, and the masculine plural relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). The relative pronoun is fixed in form and introduces a description; it does not change for case.

4.meaning: They split apart, became divided, scattered into factions — to break into separate groups, losing unity.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in a reflexive pattern (tafaʿʿala) conveying becoming divided among themselves. The -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') and the past/completed tense: 'they became divided'. The final silent alif is a spelling convention after this plural ending.

5.meaning: And they differed, disagreed, or fell into dispute — to hold conflicting views and diverge from one another.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in the mutual pattern (iftaʿala), conveying disagreement among parties. The wa- prefix means 'and'. The -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') and the past/completed tense: 'they differed'. The final silent alif follows the spelling rule for this plural ending.
5.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to differ, succeed, come after

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
7.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
7.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: It came to them / he came to them: a completed act of arriving or coming, with the recipients ('them') built into the word.

parts.en: final vowel of the past-tense base (he/it)

9.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it … '), expressing a completed action. In this form the 'he/it' subject carries no added suffix — the -a is simply the final vowel resting on the last root letter of the base, not a person marker. The attached -hum(u) is the object pronoun 'them'; its vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before a following word.

10.meaning: The clear proofs / evident signs — plainly manifest, self-evident pieces of evidence that make the truth unmistakable.

parts.en: clear proofs / evident signs (the final -u is the nominative case ending, marking the subject)

10.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun (with 'al-' = 'the') meaning 'clear proofs.' The plural ending 'āt' marks a feminine plural, and the final -u is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the noun as the subject/doer of a sentence ('… the clear proofs came to you'). The pattern 'bayyina' denotes something that makes things plainly evident.
10.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness; to make plain or evident

11.meaning: 'And those' — the connective 'and' joined to the demonstrative 'those'. It both links to what precedes and points out a group ('and it is those who…').
11.grammar: A connecting particle wa ('and') prefixed to a plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. The wa simply joins what follows to what came before. The demonstrative is fixed in form (no case endings), and its -ka element marks distance; it may refer to people of either gender.

12.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
12.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

13.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
13.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

14.meaning: Great, immense, mighty — vast in magnitude or importance. Describes something tremendous, whether in size, weight, or gravity.
14.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern, conveying a strong, established quality. The '-un' ending marks it nominative and indefinite; as an adjective it typically agrees with and describes an indefinite noun ('a great …').
14.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, immense

1.meaning: Day — a span of time; frequently used to denote a momentous appointed Day, especially the Day of Resurrection and Judgment.
1.grammar: A noun ending in the accusative vowel -a. On a time-word like this the accusative commonly works adverbially to mean 'on the day (when…)' or 'on a day', setting the time-frame for an action.

2.meaning: It turns white, becomes bright or radiant — the whitening of something, often used of faces lit up with joy and honor.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the color/transformation form (Form IX, ifʿalla, 'to become white'; past base اِبۡيَضَّ). The present tense of a third-person feminine singular subject takes the shape tafʿallu (تَبۡيَضُّ), where the ta- prefix marks the feminine singular subject ('it/she'). The final -u marks the plain present indicative — an ongoing or future state: 'it turns white'.

3.meaning: Faces — the plural of 'face'; by extension, persons themselves, or the direction and aspect a thing presents.
3.grammar: A plural noun. The final -un (nominative with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('faces, some faces') and as the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence.

4.meaning: And it turns black, becomes dark — the blackening of something, often used of faces overcome by grief, shame, or sorrow.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb in the color/transformation form (Form IX, ifʿalla, 'to become black'; past base اِسۡوَدَّ). The wa- prefix means 'and'. The present tense of a third-person feminine singular subject takes the shape tafʿallu (تَسۡوَدُّ), where the ta- prefix marks the feminine singular subject ('it/she'). The final -u marks the plain present indicative — an ongoing or future state: 'it turns black'.

5.meaning: Faces — the plural of 'face'; by extension, persons themselves, or the direction and aspect a thing presents.
5.grammar: A plural noun. The final -un (nominative with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('faces, some faces') and as the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence.

6.meaning: 'Then as for …' A connective opening that introduces and singles out a topic for comment, often paired later with a response. The fa- means 'then/so,' and 'ammā' sets up 'as for (such-and-such)…' to highlight one case among others.
6.grammar: A connector fa- ('then, so') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā introduces a subject for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that gives the comment about it. Neither part takes case endings.

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: It turned black, became dark — the completed blackening of something, especially of a face overtaken by gloom or disgrace.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb in the color form (Form IX, ifʿalla, 'to become black'). The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject ('she/it') in the past/completed tense: 'it turned black'.
8.root: س-و-د (s-w-d) — blackness, darkness

9.meaning: Their faces — the plural 'faces' joined to a possessive 'their', i.e. the faces belonging to a group of people.
9.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u before the suffix is the nominative ending, marking the word as a subject or topic. The suffix -hum means 'their' (referring to a group of males or a mixed group): 'their faces'.

10.meaning: Did you disbelieve? — a pointed question put to a group, asking whether they rejected faith or denied the truth.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb opened by the question particle a- ('did…?'). The -tum ending marks a 'you' (masculine plural) subject in the past/completed tense, so the whole is a reproachful question: 'Did you (all) disbelieve?'.
10.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to disbelieve, deny, be ungrateful

11.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
11.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
11.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

12.meaning: Your faith / your believing — the inward belief and trust of a group of people. It joins the noun 'faith' (īmān) to an attached pronoun 'your (plural)'.
12.grammar: The noun īmān ('faith') carries the genitive -i ending and then the possessive pronoun -kum ('your', plural). The genitive shows the noun is governed by a preposition or joined to a preceding word; -kum makes it 'your faith' (belonging to a group).
12.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to believe

13.meaning: So taste! — a command to a group to 'taste' or experience something, often used figuratively of undergoing a consequence or punishment.
13.grammar: A command (imperative). The fa- prefix means 'so' or 'then', linking it to what precedes. The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural addressee ('you all'): 'so taste!'. The final silent alif is a spelling convention after this plural ending.

14.meaning: The punishment, chastisement, or torment — a penalty inflicted as retribution, especially the painful suffering of divine reckoning.
14.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the punishment'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb or the subject/predicate after certain particles.
14.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment; the inflicting of pain

15.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
15.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

16.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
16.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

17.meaning: A verb meaning 'you disbelieve', 'you reject faith', or 'you are ungrateful' — to refuse to believe, to deny the truth, or to be ungrateful, addressed to a group.
17.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks the second person ('you') and the -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural subject in the indicative mood (ongoing or habitual action). The root joins the ideas of denying faith and being ungrateful — covering over a truth or a blessing.
17.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to disbelieve, deny, be ungrateful, cover over

1.meaning: 'And as for …' A connective that introduces and sets apart a new topic for separate comment, usually anticipating a matching response clause. The 'and' joins it on; 'ammā' means 'as for (such-and-such)…'
1.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā singles out a topic for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that supplies the comment. Neither part takes case endings.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: It turned white, became bright — the completed whitening of something, especially of a face lit up with joy and honor.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the color form (Form IX, ifʿalla, 'to become white'). The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject ('she/it') in the past/completed tense: 'it turned white'.

4.meaning: Their faces — the plural 'faces' joined to a possessive 'their', i.e. the faces belonging to a group of people.
4.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u before the suffix is the nominative ending, marking the word as a subject or topic. The suffix -hum means 'their' (referring to a group of males or a mixed group): 'their faces'.

5.meaning: So in / then within — a connective 'so/then' joined to the preposition 'in', placing something inside or within what follows.
5.grammar: A compound of the connective fa- ('so, then'), which links a result to what precedes, and the preposition fī ('in, within'). A preposition like fī puts the noun that follows into the genitive case ('… in …').

6.meaning: Mercy — compassion, tenderness, and active kindness shown to another; sparing, relenting, and treating with gentleness.
6.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('the mercy OF …') or comes after a preposition. The feminine -t sound surfaces when the word connects to what follows.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
8.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

9.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
9.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

10.meaning: 'Ones who abide / remain forever; everlasting dwellers.' The plural of an active participle describing those who stay, persist, and endure in a state or place without end — abiding permanently.
10.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when such a group is the subject of a sentence or is being described as being in that state.
10.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — to remain forever, endure, be everlasting

1.meaning: That; a demonstrative used to point to something distant or already mentioned. It singles out a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing, roughly 'that one over there.'
1.grammar: A feminine singular demonstrative pronoun pointing to something far off. The -ka element signals remoteness ('that yonder' rather than 'this near'). Being a demonstrative, it does not take case endings; its form is fixed.

2.meaning: "signs / verses / tokens" — the plural of āya, a 'sign' or evident token that points to something beyond itself; it also denotes a verse of revelation, each one a sign.
2.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks sound feminine plural). The final -u is the nominative case, the form taken as the subject of a sentence or the leading term of a possessive chain ('the signs OF …').

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: "We recite it / We relate it" — built on the verb meaning to recite aloud, to read out, to convey a text in sequence; with the object pronoun it means 'we recite them/it'.
4.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'we' form. The na- prefix marks first-person plural ('we'). The attached -hā is the object 'it/them' (referring to a feminine or non-human-plural noun).
4.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read out, follow

5.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

6.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
6.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
6.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

7.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
8.root: — (proper divine name)

9.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
9.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
9.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

10.meaning: Wrongdoing, injustice, oppression — placing something where it does not belong; acting unjustly, whether against others, oneself, or the truth.
10.grammar: A noun. The final -an (accusative with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite and often as the object of a verb, or works adverbially ('wrongfully, unjustly'), describing the manner in which something is done.
10.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress, do injustice

11.meaning: A phrase: 'for the worlds / for all peoples' — 'li-' meaning 'for/to', and 'al-ʿālamīn' meaning all created realms, all nations and beings, the whole of existence.
11.grammar: A definite plural noun preceded by 'li-' ('for'). The '-īn' ending is the masculine sound plural in its genitive/accusative form — here genitive because it follows the preposition 'li-'. The genitive 'plural of -īn' marks 'the … s' as the object of 'for'.
11.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; (ʿālam) a world/realm known to its Maker

1.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and to Allah (belongs)' — expressing ownership or rightful belonging to Allah; the lām conveys possession or entitlement.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the prepositional phrase 'lillāhi'. This phrase is the preposition 'li-' ('to/for', here showing possession) prefixed to the name 'Allah'; when 'li-' attaches, the connecting hamza and the first lām of the definite article are elided in writing, leaving a single written lām for the preposition followed by the doubled (shadda-bearing) lām of the name. 'Allah' takes the -i (genitive) ending required after a preposition.

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

5.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
5.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
7.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

8.meaning: And to / and toward; a connector "and" joined with a preposition expressing direction or destination toward which something moves or is referred.
8.grammar: A preposition meaning "to/toward," prefixed with the connector wa- ("and"). Being a preposition, it puts the noun that follows it into the genitive case (the "…toward X" relationship). It has no case ending of its own.

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: It is returned / brought back; a present-tense passive action of being sent or referred back to a source or destination.
10.grammar: A present/ongoing verb in the passive voice, so the action is done to the subject ("is returned/brought back"). The tu- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular (or non-human plural) subject ("it/they"). The final -u ending signals the indicative mood, used for stating an action.

11.meaning: The matters, affairs, or things; the plural of "affair/matter," denoting all the various businesses, situations, or commands taken together.
11.grammar: A definite plural noun with prefixed al- ("the"), the plural of the word for "matter/affair." The -u ending is nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as the doer/topic of an action.

1.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
1.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
1.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

2.meaning: The word for 'best / better / greatest good' — the superior or most excellent of things; also simply 'good, benefit'. The form shown is the construct (linking) form ready to attach to a following noun ('the best of …').
2.grammar: A noun used both for 'good/benefit' and, in comparisons, 'better/best'. The final -a marks the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb or after certain particles. It often begins a construct chain meaning 'the best of …'.
2.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, what is good; choosing the better

3.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
3.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.

4.meaning: It was brought forth, produced, or raised up — the act of being made to come out or be put forward, done to it by another.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice (causative pattern), so the subject is acted upon: 'it was brought forth/raised up' rather than doing the action itself. The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject ('she/it') in the past/completed tense.
4.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, bring forth, emerge

5.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
5.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

6.meaning: You command, order, or enjoin — addressing a group, the act of instructing others to do something, often to urge what is good.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks it as masculine plural and as the plain present indicative — an ongoing or habitual action: 'you (all) command'.

7.meaning: 'In a fitting / honourable / customary way' — bi- ('with/in') joined to al-ma'rūf, literally 'that which is known and recognised', i.e. what is right, decent, and approved by sound custom and morality.

parts.en: what is right / recognised as good

7.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition 'with / in'. The l- is 'the'. The stem is a passive participle meaning 'that which is known/recognised (as good)'. The final -i is the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition like bi-.
7.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognise; hence what is recognised as good

8.meaning: And you forbid, prohibit, or restrain — addressing a group, the act of holding others back from something, the counterpart to commanding.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb. The wa- prefix means 'and'. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'). The root ends in a weak letter (-y), which surfaces as a wāw within the stem (tanhaw-); the masculine plural present subject is then marked by the ending -na, in the present/ongoing tense: 'you (all) forbid'.
8.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to forbid, prohibit, restrain

9.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
9.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

10.meaning: That which is rejected, disapproved, and recognized as wrong — what sound nature and revelation deem objectionable; 'the wrong' or 'the reprehensible'.
10.grammar: A noun (originally a passive participle, 'that which is denied/rejected') with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.

11.meaning: And you believe, have faith, trust securely — addressing a group, the inward assent of faith and trustful affirmation.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative/intensive pattern (Form IV, āmana, 'to believe, have faith'). The wa- prefix means 'and'. The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks it as masculine plural and as the plain present indicative — an ongoing state: 'you (all) believe'.

12.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
12.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
12.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

13.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
13.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

14.meaning: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.
14.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust, faith

15.meaning: A people or community defined by belonging — most literally a household or family, and by extension the folk or people associated with a thing, place, or way (as in 'the people of the Scripture/Book'). It denotes those who belong to or are at home with something.
15.grammar: A singular noun (used collectively). The final -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject or 'doer' of a sentence, or a thing being named or described.

16.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
16.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

17.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic 'surely/certainly' joined to the verb 'was/became.' The verb is the past tense of 'to be,' which in Arabic also conveys 'used to be' or describes a settled state of existence; the attached particle stresses and affirms that statement.
17.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphatic particle adding 'truly, certainly.' The stem kāna is a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'); the final -a is the standard past-tense vowel for that form. It often pairs with a following word to mean 'X would have been / used to be.'
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

18.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
18.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.
18.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, beneficial, choice, excellence

19.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
19.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

20.meaning: 'From them / among them' (a group of males or a mixed group) — indicating origin, source, or partitive 'some of them'.
20.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among'). The attached pronoun -hum ('them', masculine/mixed plural) takes a helping vowel -u (becoming -humu) for ease of pronunciation before a following word. The whole means 'from/among them'.

21.meaning: The believers — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm the truth and give it their security and assent.
21.grammar: A definite noun, the active participle of form IV ('mu'min,' 'one who believes/grants security'). The plural ending '-ūna' marks a masculine human plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or doer ('the believers' as those performing the action).

22.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and most of them' (or 'but most of them'). It joins the comparative noun 'more/most' — used to mean 'the greater part, the majority' — to a pronoun referring to a group of people.
22.grammar: wa- is a joining particle ('and/but'). akthar is a comparative/superlative noun ('more, most'). The -u ending is nominative (subject case). The attached -hum(u) is a possessive pronoun, 'their / of them,' for a masculine plural group; its vowel is lengthened to -humu for ease of pronunciation before a following word.

23.meaning: Those who defiantly disobey — the active participle 'fāsiq' (one who breaks away from obedience, transgressing moral and religious limits) in its sound masculine plural, with the definite article.
23.grammar: Definite ('al-') sound masculine plural active participle. The '-ūna' ending is the nominative (subject) form of the masculine plural, used when the word is the doer of an action or the subject of a sentence.
23.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to break away, depart from obedience; to act immorally

1.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
1.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

2.meaning: 'They harm/injure you' — a verb expressing the causing of damage, hurt, or detriment to someone, with 'you' (plural) as the ones affected.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya-…-ū framing marks third-person masculine plural ('they'). The long -ū is the plural subject marker. In the plain indicative this form would end in -na (yaḍurrūna); here the -na is dropped, which marks the verb as non-indicative. The dropped -na from a plural verb is shared by two moods — the subjunctive (manṣūb), triggered by particles such as 'an' ('to'), 'lan' ('will never'), and 'kay' ('so that'), and the jussive (majzūm), triggered by particles such as 'lam' ('did not'), the imperative 'li-', and conditional 'in' ('if') — so the dropped -na alone is shared between them; only the governing particle tells which mood applies. The attached -kum is the object pronoun, 'you (all).'

3.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
3.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

4.meaning: Harm, hurt, or an affliction — something offensive or injurious, ranging from a minor irritation or ailment to anything that causes discomfort or distress.
4.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending (written with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative: it marks 'a harm / some harm' as the object of a verb or as part of a descriptive phrase, with the 'n' sound signalling indefiniteness ('a/an').
4.root: أ-ذ-ي (ʾ-dh-y) — to harm, hurt, injure, cause discomfort

5.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
5.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

6.meaning: 'They fight you' — a verb of mutual combat and warfare, denoting engaging an enemy in battle, with 'you' (plural) as the opponent.
6.grammar: A present/future verb from a pattern (long 'aa' after the first letter) that carries the sense of mutual, reciprocal action (fighting one another). The yu-…-ū framing marks third-person masculine plural ('they'). The long -ū is the plural subject ending. The plain indicative would end in -na (yuqātilūna); its loss here marks the verb as non-indicative. For a plural verb the same dropped -na serves two moods — the jussive (majzūm), triggered by particles such as 'lam' ('did not'), the imperative 'li-', and conditional 'in' ('if'), and the subjunctive (manṣūb), triggered by 'an' / 'lan' / 'kay' — so the form alone does not distinguish them; the governing particle decides. The attached -kum is the object 'you (all).'

7.meaning: 'They turn (something) toward you' — a verb meaning to make something face or turn in a direction, to cause a turning or to put someone in charge; with 'you' (plural) as the one toward whom the turning is directed.
7.grammar: A present/future verb whose doubled middle consonant gives a causative/intensive sense ('to make turn'). The yu-…-ū framing marks third-person masculine plural ('they'). The long -ū is the plural subject ending. The plain indicative would end in -na (yuwallūna); its loss marks the verb as non-indicative. The dropped -na from a plural verb is common to two moods — the jussive (majzūm), triggered by particles such as 'lam,' imperative 'li-,' and conditional 'in,' and the subjunctive (manṣūb), triggered by 'an' / 'lan' / 'kay' — so the bare form does not by itself reveal which; the governing particle does. The attached -kum is the object 'you (all),' lengthened to -kumu before a following word.

8.meaning: 'The backs' — the plural of 'back' (the rear of a person or body), commonly evoking the act of turning one's back, retreating, or fleeing.
8.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a ending is accusative, the case that commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
8.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — back, rear; that which comes behind

9.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
9.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

10.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
10.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

11.meaning: To be helped, aided, or given victory — for support to be granted, especially against an adversary.
11.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, masculine plural 'they.' The yu- prefix is the third-person masculine imperfect marker; the passive sense ('they are being helped,' by an unnamed helper) comes from the internal vowelling rather than from the prefix itself.
