5.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with an attached possessive pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. 'Rabb' carries a doubled (geminated) 'b' — the shaddah — at its core. The '-i' vowel on 'rabb' is its case ending, determined by 'Lord's' own role in the sentence (not by the suffix); the attached '-kum' is the possessor ('your'), addressing a plural 'you', and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive.

6.meaning: 'and a garden' — a lush, walled garden of trees and shade; the term used for the Garden of Paradise. The leading 'wa' joins it ('and …').
6.grammar: An indefinite feminine noun joined by 'wa' ('and'). The ending '-tin' (feminine -t plus tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive, which typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('… of a garden'). The root conveys something covered over and concealed by dense foliage.
6.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal; a garden of dense foliage

7.meaning: 'its breadth / its width' — the expanse or wideness of a thing. The attached pronoun 'its' (feminine) ties the width to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
7.grammar: A masculine noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-hā' ('its', referring to something feminine). The -u on the noun is the nominative ending, which generally marks it as the subject or topic ('its breadth [is …]').

8.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the celestial expanse above, here in the plural ('the heavens'), encompassing all the layers of the sky. The definite article marks them as the known heavens.
8.grammar: A definite feminine sound plural ('the heavens'). The ending '-ātu' carries the -u that marks the nominative, generally signaling the subject or topic of the sentence ('the heavens [are …]').
8.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; the sky/heaven

9.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, and world beneath, as opposed to the heavens. The leading 'wa' joins it ('and …') and the definite article marks it as the known earth.
9.grammar: A definite feminine noun joined by 'wa' ('and'). The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as the subject or topic of a sentence ('and the earth [is …]').

10.meaning: A passive verb: 'it was made ready / it has been prepared, readied, set up in advance.' In the passive, the focus is on the thing prepared, not on who prepared it. The 'prepare' sense comes from the derived (Form IV) verb aʿadda, 'to make ready, equip beforehand.'
10.grammar: A past-tense passive verb, 3rd person feminine singular, from Form IV (aʿadda, 'to prepare/make ready'). The vowel pattern (u-i) marks it as passive ('was prepared' rather than 'prepared'). The final -t ending shows the subject is feminine singular ('she/it was prepared').
10.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — Form I means 'to count, number'; the 'prepare/make ready' sense belongs to the derived Form IV (aʿadda)

11.meaning: For the people of taqwā — the God-conscious, those who are mindful and careful of Allah, guarding themselves against wrongdoing out of awareness of Him. The whole word means 'for/to the God-conscious ones'.

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

11.grammar: An active participle in the sound masculine plural, prefixed by the preposition 'li-' ('for/to') and the definite article 'al-'. The '-īna' ending is the oblique (genitive/accusative) plural form, used after a preposition; it means 'the (several) ones who…'. The base verb form (Form VIII) carries a reflexive sense: those who shield or protect themselves.
11.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield; hence taqwā: God-conscious caution

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: 'They spend/give out': to expend wealth or provision, especially by giving it away in charity and in good causes. The word centers on disbursing what one has rather than hoarding it.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in Form IV (anfaqa, 'to spend, expend'). The imperfect prefix is only yu-; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ف-ق), not part of the prefix. The yu- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural) doing the action now or habitually. The -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, the default 'plain' form used for ongoing or repeated action.
2.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, give out

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: Ease, prosperity, and times of comfort — a state of well-being, plenty, and pleasant circumstances. The word denotes the season of life when things go well.
4.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-', 'the') of an intensive pattern (faʿʿāʾ) suggesting a marked, abundant state of ease. The 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 's' sound (a sun letter), shown by the shadda on the 's'. The final '-i' is the genitive case ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
4.root: س-ر-ر (s-r-r) — to gladden, please; joy and delight

5.meaning: 'And hardship / affliction' — harm, injury, or suffering that touches the body or circumstances (such as illness or loss). Joined by 'and'.
5.grammar: The connector wa ('and') plus a definite feminine noun on the faʿlāʾ pattern, denoting an intense condition (grievous harm or suffering); the article's 'l' is assimilated into the following sun letter 'ḍ'. The final -i is the genitive case, taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive construction.

6.meaning: And those who suppress and swallow down their rage — people who hold back and contain their anger rather than letting it burst out. The verb pictures choking back a feeling and keeping it bottled within.
6.grammar: An active participle in the sound masculine plural, joined by 'wa-' ('and') and made definite by 'al-'. The '-īna' ending is the oblique (genitive/accusative) plural, meaning 'the ones who…'. It describes a habitual doer of the action: those who characteristically restrain their wrath.
6.root: ك-ظ-م (k-ẓ-m) — to suppress, choke back, hold in (especially anger or grief)

7.meaning: Rage, fury — hot, boiling anger; the surge of wrath that wells up inside a person.
7.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-', 'the'). The final '-a' is the accusative case ending, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or follows certain particles.

8.meaning: And those who pardon — people who readily forgive others, overlooking and letting go of wrongs done to them rather than seeking retribution.
8.grammar: An active participle in the sound masculine plural, joined by 'wa-' ('and') and made definite by 'al-'. The '-īna' ending is the oblique (genitive/accusative) plural, meaning 'the ones who…'. It denotes those who habitually pardon and excuse others.
8.root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w) — to pardon, excuse, efface (a fault); also to relieve

9.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
9.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

10.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
10.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
10.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

11.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
11.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
11.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

12.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
12.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

13.meaning: 'The doers of good / those who act with excellence and beauty'. It denotes people who do what is good and do it well — acting righteously, generously, and with sincerity, as if conscious of being watched by Allah.

parts.en: good-doers / those who excel in doing good

13.grammar: A definite plural active participle (the 'doer' form of the verb 'to do good'). The prefixed al- means 'the'. The ending -īna marks a sound masculine plural in the object/oblique state — the form used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition. It refers to male (or mixed) persons characterized by the action.
13.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful; to do well and excellently

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

3.meaning: They did, they committed, they performed — a completed action carried out by a group (masculine 'they').
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The '-ū' ending means the subject is 'they' (a masculine plural group) and that the action is already complete. This very verb (faʿala) is the standard template by which Arabic grammarians name all verb patterns.
3.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, make, act; an action or deed

4.meaning: A gross indecency or shameful, immoral act — conduct that is flagrantly obscene and exceeds the bounds of decency. The word names something whose ugliness is extreme and obvious.
4.grammar: A feminine noun in the indefinite. The '-tan' ending combines the feminine '-t-' with '-an', the accusative-indefinite marker ('an indecency'), which typically signals the direct object of a verb or a non-specific 'a/an'.
4.root: ف-ح-ش (f-ḥ-sh) — to be excessive, foul, indecent; gross immorality

5.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
5.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

6.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
6.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
7.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

8.meaning: They remembered, called to mind, made mention of — a group (masculine 'they') brought something to consciousness or recalled it. The verb often carries the sense of remembering Allah.
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The '-ū' ending marks a 'they' subject (masculine plural) and indicates a completed action. The root sense spans both inward remembrance and outward mention.
8.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, call to mind, mention; remembrance

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
9.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

10.meaning: And then they sought forgiveness — a group asked Allah to pardon and cover over their faults. The 'fa-' adds the sense 'and so / then', linking it as the next step after something.
10.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form X, whose pattern ('istafʿala') typically means 'to seek/ask for' the root's action — here, to seek forgiveness. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'then / and so'. The '-ū' ending marks a 'they' subject (masculine plural) and a completed action.
10.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, forgive, pardon; concealment of sins

11.meaning: For their sins — concerning the wrongs and offenses belonging to them. 'Sins' here are misdeeds that burden a person; the attached pronoun marks them as 'theirs'.
11.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition 'li-' ('for/concerning') and ending in the attached possessive pronoun '-him' ('their', masculine plural). The '-i-' before the pronoun reflects the genitive case, which is required after a preposition and when a noun is possessed.
11.root: ذ-ن-ب (dh-n-b) — to sin, do wrong; a sin or offense

12.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
12.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

13.meaning: He forgives / can forgive — He covers over and pardons faults. Describes an ongoing or characteristic act of forgiving by a single subject ('he').
13.grammar: A present/future-tense (imperfect) verb. The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final '-u' is the indicative ending, signalling a plain, ongoing statement of fact (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive mood).

14.meaning: The sins — wrongs and offenses taken collectively as a known category. The definite article makes it 'the sins' as a whole.
14.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun, with 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'dh' sound (a sun letter), shown by the shadda on the 'dh'. The final '-a' is the accusative case ending, which typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
14.root: ذ-ن-ب (dh-n-b) — to sin, do wrong; a sin or offense

15.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
15.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

16.meaning: Allah — the proper name of the One True God, the sole deity worthy of worship. It is a unique name with no plural and no gender, referring to the Divine Being Himself.
16.grammar: The proper divine name. The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the one who acts or about whom something is said. As the name of the Divine it is always definite and never pluralized.
16.root: — (the divine name; commonly linked to ʾ-l-h, 'to deity / worship')

17.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
17.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

18.meaning: They persist / they keep at it — a group (masculine 'they') stubbornly continues in something, clinging to it without turning away. Often used of doggedly continuing in wrongdoing.
18.grammar: A present/future-tense (imperfect) Form IV verb meaning to persist insistently. The 'yu-' prefix plus the '-ū' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The verb ends in '-ū' without the final 'n', a form used after certain particles and in commands/negations (the subjunctive/jussive moods) rather than a plain statement.
18.root: ص-ر-ر (ṣ-r-r) — to insist, persist, be obstinate; to bind tightly

19.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
19.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

20.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
20.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

21.meaning: They did, they committed, they performed — a completed action carried out by a group (masculine 'they').
21.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The '-ū' ending means the subject is 'they' (a masculine plural group) and that the action is already complete. This very verb (faʿala) is the standard template by which Arabic grammarians name all verb patterns.
21.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, make, act; an action or deed

22.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
22.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

23.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
23.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'
23.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

2.meaning: 'Their recompense / requital / reward' — the return or payment one is given in response to deeds, whether good or bad. Combined here with 'their.'
2.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive -hum ('their,' masculine plural). The -u vowel on 'jazāʾ' is the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being identified in a statement.

3.meaning: Forgiveness — Allah's covering over and pardoning of sins; the act and gift of having one's faults effaced.
3.grammar: A verbal noun of the 'mafʿila' pattern, naming the abstract action of forgiving. The '-tun' ending combines the feminine '-t-' with '-un', the nominative-indefinite marker, which typically marks an indefinite subject ('a forgiveness') — the one acting or being asserted to exist.

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: 'Their Lord / their Sustainer.' The noun 'rabb' — a master who owns, nurtures, sustains, and brings to maturity all under His care — joined to 'their.' It conveys far more than 'lord': the one who creates, provides for, and governs His servants.
5.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun -him ('their,' masculine plural). The -i ending is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to another in an 'of / belonging to' relationship; here it pairs with the attached 'their.'
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship, ownership, care

6.meaning: And gardens — lush, walled gardens of trees and flowing water; the standing image of Paradise. The plural points to many such gardens.
6.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun, joined by 'wa-' ('and'). The '-un' ending is the nominative-indefinite marker ('gardens'), which typically marks an indefinite subject — the one acting or asserted to exist. The base word 'janna' literally means a place so densely planted that its ground is hidden/concealed.
6.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide; hence a garden (whose floor is hidden by foliage)

7.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
8.root: — (preposition)

9.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
9.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').

10.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
10.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.

11.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
11.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.

12.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
12.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

13.meaning: And how excellent is…! — a fixed expression of praise meaning 'and what a wonderful…'. It is used to extol something as the best of its kind.

parts.en: how excellent is! / what a fine…

13.grammar: A frozen verb of praise (a special 'verb of admiration') joined by 'wa-' ('and'). It does not conjugate for tense in the ordinary way; it stands at the head of a phrase to declare that what follows is excellent and praiseworthy. Its fixed '-a' ending is part of this set form.
13.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — goodness, favor, blessing; to be pleasant/excellent

14.meaning: Reward, recompense, wage — the return or compensation given for what one has done; payment for work or deeds.
14.grammar: A noun. The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or, as here without nunation, a noun that is the first term of a possessive phrase ('the reward of …'). It denotes a deserved recompense, whether worldly or in the Hereafter.
14.root: أ-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — to recompense, reward; wages, reward

15.meaning: The doers / the workers — those who act and put things into practice, especially the ones who do righteous deeds. The word names people defined by their working and acting.
15.grammar: An active participle in the sound masculine plural, made definite by 'al-'. The '-īna' ending is the oblique (genitive/accusative) plural, meaning 'the ones who…'; here it typically follows a possessive link ('the reward of the workers'). It denotes habitual doers — those characterized by working and acting.
15.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deed, work

1.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

2.meaning: 'It passed away / went by, came to an end' — said of a community, time, or era that has elapsed and is now gone. The root carries the sense of being emptied out, hence of time or people that have passed.
2.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it,' used here because the noun it refers to is grammatically feminine. The past tense states a completed action.
2.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty/vacant; to pass away, elapse

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: 'before you,' 'prior to you' — an expression of precedence in time or place, here relating that precedence to 'you (plural).' The core word denotes the 'before' side, what comes earlier or in front.
4.grammar: An adverb of time/place ('before') joined to the pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). The '-i' ending is genitive: such words of place/time regularly take this case, especially after a preposition, and the attached pronoun completes the sense as 'before you.'

5.meaning: Established ways, patterns, or precedents — recurring courses of action and fixed practices. It often refers to the consistent ways in which Allah has dealt with earlier peoples; the plural points to several such precedents.
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun (singular 'sunna'). The '-un' ending is the nominative-indefinite marker ('ways / precedents'), which typically marks an indefinite subject — the one acting or asserted to exist. The word denotes a trodden path that has become a settled custom.
5.root: س-ن-ن (s-n-n) — to set a course / lay down a way; a custom, path, precedent

6.meaning: So travel! / then journey! — a command to a group (masculine 'you all') to set out and move across the land. The 'fa-' gives the sense 'so / then', tying the command to what came before.
6.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you all', prefixed by 'fa-' ('so/then'). The '-ū' ending marks the plural addressees being told to act. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter surfaces as the long 'ī' in this form.
6.root: س-ي-ر (s-y-r) — to travel, journey, move along; a journey

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
8.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

9.meaning: So look! / then observe! — a command to a group (masculine 'you all') to look attentively and consider, to take a lesson from what is seen.
9.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you all', prefixed by 'fa-' ('so/then'). The '-ū' ending marks the plural addressees being commanded. The verb means more than mere seeing — it implies attentive looking that leads to reflection.
9.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, observe, consider, reflect

10.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
10.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

11.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

11.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

12.meaning: The outcome, end-result, or final consequence — what a matter or a course of conduct ultimately comes to. It names the end that follows from a beginning.
12.grammar: A feminine noun. The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or, without nunation as here, the first term of a possessive phrase ('the outcome of …'). It denotes that which comes at the heel — the consequence that follows on.
12.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after (at the heel); an end, consequence

13.meaning: The deniers / those who cry lies — people who reject the truth as false and treat the messengers and revelation as lies. The word names them by their habit of calling truth a falsehood.
13.grammar: An active participle of Form II (the doubled, intensive pattern) in the sound masculine plural, made definite by 'al-'. The '-īna' ending is the oblique (genitive/accusative) plural, meaning 'the ones who…'; here it typically follows a possessive link ('the … of the deniers'). The Form II shape conveys persistently and emphatically declaring something a lie.
13.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; to declare false, give the lie to

1.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
1.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

2.meaning: A clear statement or plain exposition that makes something evident and removes ambiguity; clarification by which a matter is set forth openly.
2.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a clarification') and in the nominative case, the case used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described/identified.
2.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct, evident; to make plain

3.meaning: For the people, for mankind, for humankind. The preposition 'for/to' joined to 'the people' as a collective term for human beings.
3.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') prefixed to the noun 'al-nās' ('the people'). The article 'al-' loses its 'a' sound after 'li-' and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's initial n (hence the doubled 'nn'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition.

4.meaning: A connective 'and' plus 'guidance' — 'and guidance': right direction, the showing of the correct way, that which leads one rightly.
4.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'hudā' is a noun meaning 'guidance'; because it ends in a special shortened alif, its indefinite ending appears as -an (written with tanwīn over the preceding letter). This -an is the indefinite marker; on such alif-ending nouns the case is not separately shown, so the word can stand as subject, object, or predicate alike.

5.meaning: An admonition or earnest counsel that touches the heart — a reminder meant to soften, warn, and turn a person toward what is right.
5.grammar: A prefix wa- ('and') joined to a singular feminine noun of instance (the mafʿila pattern, naming a single act or instance of the verb). The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('an admonition') and nominative, the case typically used for a subject or a thing being identified.

6.meaning: 'For the mindful/God-conscious ones' — for those who have taqwa: a reverent, protective awareness of Allah that makes a person guard against wrongdoing and shield themselves from His displeasure. The word names people characterized by this watchful piety.

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

6.grammar: A preposition li- ('for') joined to a definite masculine sound plural active participle. The -ina ending is the plural form used after a preposition or as an object (the oblique/genitive-accusative case) — 'for the … ones'. The participle pattern (muftaʿil) describes those who actively do the action: those who keep themselves guarded.

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: To grow weak, faint, or feeble; to lose strength and resolve.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, second person masculine plural ('you all weaken'). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject. The dropped final nūn (tahinū rather than tahinūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive mood — the form that follows particles of negation, prohibition, or purpose.
2.root: و-ه-ن (w-h-n) — to be weak, feeble, faint

3.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
3.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

4.meaning: To feel grief, sorrow, or sadness; to be saddened and distressed inwardly.
4.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, second person masculine plural ('you all grieve'). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject. The missing final nūn (taḥzanū rather than taḥzanūna) shows the subjunctive/jussive mood — the form used after particles of prohibition, negation, or purpose.

5.meaning: 'And you' — the standalone pronoun for a group being addressed, used to emphasise or single out the persons spoken to.

parts.en: connecting vowel before a following word

5.grammar: A prefix wa- ('and') joined to the detached subject pronoun antum, second person masculine plural ('you all'). The added final -u (giving antumu) is a helping vowel inserted to ease pronunciation when the next word begins with a definite article; it carries no case meaning of its own.

6.meaning: Those who are higher, uppermost, or superior — the ones holding the upper hand and the loftier standing.
6.grammar: A definite plural noun/adjective of the 'afʿal' (elative) pattern meaning 'highest/superior', made definite by al- ('the'). The -awna ending marks a masculine sound plural in the nominative case — the case used for a subject or predicate ('the higher ones').
6.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — height, loftiness, to be high/exalted

7.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
7.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

8.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
8.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

9.meaning: 'Believers / faithful ones' — the plural of muʾmin, one who has faith and trust in Allah and grants assent to the truth.

parts.en: believers (form IV participle, oblique masculine sound plural)

9.grammar: An active participle ('one who believes') from the form IV pattern, here a masculine sound plural. The single suffix -īna is the oblique (accusative/genitive) form of the masculine plural — used for a direct object or after a preposition — as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject. Its nūn is part of the one ending and is not a separable morpheme.
9.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust; hence faith and belief

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: For something to touch, afflict, or come into contact with a group of people — often used of harm, hardship, or injury befalling someone.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third person masculine singular ('it/he touches'), with the attached object pronoun -kum ('you all') as the thing touched. The stem ends in a bare consonant (-msas rather than -massu) showing the jussive mood, the form used after conditional words and particles like 'if' or 'when'.
2.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, make contact, afflict

3.meaning: A wound or sore — physical injury, especially the kind sustained in battle or struggle.
3.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a wound') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence (the thing that does or undergoes the action).

4.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
4.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

5.meaning: Touched, afflicted, or befell — for something (such as harm or hardship) to have made contact with someone.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he/it touched'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for a single masculine subject; the doubled middle consonant (shadda) is part of this root's basic form.
5.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, make contact, afflict

6.meaning: the people / the folk — a body of people, a community or group regarded collectively (here in the accusative form).
6.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative. Since the verb it follows is passive (and so takes no direct object), this accusative is adverbial — marking the circumstance or setting of the action ('before / in front of the people') rather than a thing being acted upon.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to arise; a people standing together

7.meaning: A wound or sore — physical injury, especially the kind sustained in battle or struggle.
7.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a wound') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence (the thing that does or undergoes the action).

8.meaning: 'Its like' / 'the like of it' — something equal or comparable to a previously mentioned thing.
8.grammar: A noun meaning 'like/equal' with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('its/his'). The -u ending before the pronoun is nominative, the case used for a subject or predicate. The pronoun -hu refers back to a previously named masculine thing ('the like OF it').
8.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, comparison

9.meaning: And that; and that one. 'Tilka' is a demonstrative pointing to something distant or notable ('that' / 'those'), prefixed with 'and'. It singles out and draws attention to a thing set apart.
9.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a feminine demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' or 'those'. As a demonstrative it is fixed in form (it does not change for case) and serves to point out and identify something at a distance.

10.meaning: The days — stretches of time; by extension, the unfolding turns and fortunes of time and history.
10.grammar: A definite plural noun, 'the days' (plural of yawm), made definite by al- ('the'). The final -u marks the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.

11.meaning: We turn it about in alternation — to make something pass to and fro between people in turns, so each in turn receives it.
11.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of the III ('mufāʿala') pattern conveying mutual exchange, first person plural ('we'), with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it', referring to a feminine or plural thing). The nu- prefix means 'we'; the -u before the pronoun marks the indicative mood, used for plain ongoing statements.
11.root: د-و-ل (d-w-l) — to alternate, take turns, pass round; cf. 'dawla'

12.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
12.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
12.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

13.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
13.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
13.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

14.meaning: 'So that He may make known/known-by-experience' — to bring something to light and distinguish it through what actually happens, so it becomes manifest and proven (a knowing tied to outcome, not the mere awareness already possessed).
14.grammar: Prefix wa- ('and') + purpose particle li- ('so that') + a present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('He knows/makes evident'). The li- of purpose puts the verb in the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a ending, which is the form used after 'so that / in order to'.
14.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, to know

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
15.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

16.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
16.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

17.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
17.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

18.meaning: And to take, adopt, or choose for oneself — to take something or someone as one's own (e.g. as a helper, ally, or possession).
18.grammar: Prefix wa- ('and') + a present-tense verb of the VIII ('iftaʿala') pattern, third person masculine singular, carrying the reflexive sense 'take for oneself'. The final -a marks the subjunctive mood — the form used after a purpose particle ('so that He may take'), here carried over from a preceding 'so that'.
18.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp

19.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
19.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
19.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

20.meaning: Witnesses — those present who observe and can testify to what they saw; can also carry the sense of those who bear witness. Plural.
20.grammar: A broken plural on the fuʿalāʾ (فُعَلَاء) pattern, which is a diptote: it takes the -a ending for BOTH the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn (the final 'n'). Because of this, the -a alone does not tell you the case — the word could be a direct object (accusative) or governed by a preposition ('of/among', genitive). Only when made definite or put into construct would it take the ordinary -i in the genitive.
20.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, observe, testify, be present

21.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
21.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
21.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

22.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
22.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

23.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
23.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

24.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
24.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.
24.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; wrongdoing, injustice

1.meaning: 'So that He may purify/refine' — to cleanse thoroughly and test so as to remove impurity, sifting out what is flawed and leaving what is pure.
1.grammar: Prefix wa- ('and') + purpose particle li- ('so that') + a present-tense verb of the II ('faʿʿala', intensive/causative) pattern, third person masculine singular. The li- of purpose puts the verb in the subjunctive, shown by the final -a — the form used after 'so that / in order to'.
1.root: م-ح-ص (m-ḥ-ṣ) — to purify, cleanse, sift, refine

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
4.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

5.meaning: And to wipe out, blot away, or gradually erase — to diminish and destroy something little by little until it is gone.
5.grammar: Prefix wa- ('and') + a present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('He wipes out'). The final -a marks the subjunctive mood — the form used after a purpose particle ('so that He may wipe out'), here carried over from a preceding 'so that'.
5.root: م-ح-ق (m-ḥ-q) — to wipe out, efface, annihilate gradually

6.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
6.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
6.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

2.meaning: 'You supposed / reckoned / thought'. It denotes forming an opinion or assumption — to deem something to be the case. Past tense, second person masculine plural ('you all').
2.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all') performing a completed action. The verb conveys reckoning or assuming something to be true.

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: 'You enter / will enter'. It denotes going into a place or state. Present tense, second person masculine plural ('you all'), in a form that follows certain particles.
4.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present-tense action addressed to 'you'. The '-ū' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('you all'). The dropping of the final 'n' (compared with the plain 'tadkhulūna') shows the verb is in a dependent mood, used after particles of negation, intent, or purpose.

5.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — the place of lush, shaded greenery promised as the abode of bliss; literally a garden whose foliage covers the ground.
5.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. 'janna' is a feminine noun (the tā marbūṭa ending). The final -a is accusative, the form typically marking a word as the object of a verb or, with place-nouns, the destination/location toward which an action occurs.

6.meaning: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
6.grammar: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

7.meaning: For Him to make known/known-by-experience — to bring to light and distinguish through what actually occurs (a knowing tied to manifest outcome).
7.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('He knows/makes evident'). The base form is jussive (after a conditional or negating particle), which would normally end in a bare consonant (yaʿlam); the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a consonant cluster.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
8.root: — (proper divine name)

9.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
9.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

10.meaning: They strove and struggled with effort — they exerted themselves and fought hard for a cause, expending strength against difficulty or an opponent.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb of the III ('mufāʿala') pattern, which conveys effortful, sustained, or mutual action ('to strive/struggle against'). The ending -ū marks a third person masculine plural subject ('they all strove'). The silent alif written after the wāw is a spelling convention for this ending.
10.root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d) — to exert effort, strive, struggle; cf. 'jihād'

11.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
11.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
11.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

12.meaning: And for Him to make known/known-by-experience — to bring to light and distinguish through what actually happens.
12.grammar: Prefix wa- ('and') + a present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('He knows/makes evident'). The final -a marks the subjunctive mood — the form used after a purpose particle ('so that He may know'), here carried over from a preceding 'so that'.

13.meaning: 'The patient ones / the steadfast' — those who endure hardship with calm perseverance, restraining themselves and holding firm under trial.
13.grammar: A definite plural noun/participle ('the ones who...') referring to males or a mixed group. The '-īna' ending is the plural form used when the word is an object or follows a preposition (roughly 'the patient ones' as a target of the sentence). The 'al-' prefix means 'the'.
13.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, endure, hold firm

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
2.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

3.meaning: You long for or wish for — to desire and yearn that something come to pass; to cherish a hope or wish.
3.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of the V ('tafaʿʿala') pattern, second person masculine plural ('you all wish'). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -awna ending marks a masculine plural subject in the indicative mood — the form used for plain, ongoing statements.
3.root: م-ن-ي (m-n-y) — to wish, desire, hope for

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'death' — the ending of earthly life, the departure of the soul.
4.grammar: A definite noun, made definite by al- ('the'). The -a ending is the accusative case, most commonly marking the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). So it reads '(the) death' as something received or aimed at.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'before' — denoting that which precedes in time or order.
6.grammar: An adverb/noun of time. The -i ending is genitive, which here arises because it follows a preposition (commonly 'min', 'from'); it characteristically links to a following noun ('before … OF …').
6.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; the front or prior side

7.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
7.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

8.meaning: You meet it, encounter it, or come face to face with it — to come upon something directly.
8.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, second person masculine plural ('you all meet'), with the attached object pronoun -hu ('it/him'). The original plural -ūna ending has lost its final nūn (talqaw rather than talqawna), showing the subjunctive/jussive mood — the form used after particles of purpose, condition, or negation.
8.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, come upon

9.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
9.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

10.meaning: You saw it / you have seen it — for a group to have perceived something with their own eyes, or to have come to realise it.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb, second person masculine plural ('you all saw'), with the attached object pronoun -hu ('it/him'). When an object pronoun is suffixed, the plural subject ending -tum lengthens to -tumū: the wāw here is not silent but spells a pronounced long vowel ū (ra-ay-tu-mū-hu), the linking vowel that joins the plural subject to the following object pronoun.

11.meaning: And you / while you (all) — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), often introducing an accompanying circumstance ('while you …').
11.grammar: The conjunction wa- joined to the detached subject pronoun 'you all' (masculine). This standalone pronoun stands as a subject or for emphasis; it has a fixed form and does not change for case. With wa- it can mark a simultaneous state ('and you / while you').

12.meaning: You look on, gaze, or watch — to direct one's eyes toward something and observe it; can also carry the sense of waiting and watching.
12.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, second person masculine plural ('you all look on'). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the full -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject in the indicative mood — the form used for plain, ongoing statements (the retained final nūn is the sign of this mood).
12.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, gaze, observe, await

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: Muḥammad — a masculine proper name meaning 'the praised one' or 'one worthy of much praise', built on the pattern of intensive/repeated praise.
2.grammar: A proper name of the passive-participle 'mufaʿʿal' (intensive) pattern, meaning 'highly praised'. The final -un (nunation) marks it as nominative — the case used for a subject or for the thing being identified/named.

3.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
3.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

4.meaning: "a messenger" — one who is sent bearing a message; an envoy or apostle, here in the indefinite sense "a messenger."
4.grammar: The -un ending is nominative with nunation: the -u marks it as a subject (the doer/topic), and the final -n signals that it is indefinite ("a messenger," not "the messenger").

5.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

6.meaning: 'It passed away / went by, came to an end' — said of a community, time, or era that has elapsed and is now gone. The root carries the sense of being emptied out, hence of time or people that have passed.
6.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it,' used here because the noun it refers to is grammatically feminine. The past tense states a completed action.
6.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty/vacant; to pass away, elapse

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: A word meaning 'before him' or 'prior to him' — combining a noun denoting that which comes earlier in time or sequence with an attached pronoun referring to a single masculine entity.
8.grammar: A noun of time ('before') carrying the genitive -i ending, with the attached pronoun -hi ('him'). The -hi form of the pronoun (rather than -hu) appears after a genitive -i vowel. Together it expresses 'before him' or 'prior to him'.
8.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to be before, to precede, to face/receive

9.meaning: "the messengers" — the definite plural of rasūl, an envoy or messenger: one sent with a message or mission. With the article it denotes 'the messengers' as a defined group.
9.grammar: A definite broken (internally formed) plural noun. The leading al- is 'the', and its 'l' assimilates into the following r- (heard as rr-). The final -u is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence.

10.meaning: A cluster of particles meaning roughly 'so/then, is it that if…' — opening a question with rebuke or astonishment and introducing a hypothetical condition.
10.grammar: Three particles fused together: the interrogative hamza 'a-' (asking a question, often with reproach or wonder), the connective 'fa-' ('so/then'), and the conditional 'in' ('if'), which introduces a supposition whose consequence follows. None of these takes a case ending; they are functional particles.

11.meaning: 'He died' — the completed act of dying, the departure of life from a being.
11.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the third-person masculine singular: the stem with the -a ending marks a completed action done by 'he'. It reports that the dying has already taken place.

12.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
12.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

13.meaning: 'He was killed / slain' — to have one's life taken by another, expressed in the passive so the focus is on the one killed rather than the killer.
13.grammar: A past-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular. The internal vowel pattern (u after the first letter, i after the second) marks it as passive — 'was killed' — and the final -a marks the completed action attributed to 'he'. The doer is left unnamed.

14.meaning: 'You (plural) turned back / reversed course' — to wheel around and go back the way one came, often implying a relapse or retreat.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb of the reflexive 'in-' pattern (a doer turning / being turned over), with the suffix -tum marking the subject as 'you' plural masculine. It states that the turning-back was completed by the group addressed.
14.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn, overturn; the heart

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
15.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

16.meaning: 'Your (plural) heels' — the backs of the feet; idiomatically tied to turning back, retreating, or abandoning a path one was on.
16.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, 'heels', carrying the genitive -i ending, joined to the possessive pronoun -kum ('your', plural masculine). The genitive ending here links the noun to the attached possessor 'you all'.
16.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — heel; to follow / come after; consequence

17.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
17.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

18.meaning: 'He turns back / reverses' — present-tense turning around or relapsing; can also carry the sense of being overturned.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb of the reflexive 'in-' pattern, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix marks 'he', and the stem means to turn oneself back. The vowelless (sukūn) final consonant marks the jussive (majzūm) mood used after conditional particles, expressing 'he turns back' as a conditional act.
18.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn, overturn; the heart

19.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
19.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

20.meaning: His two heels; the back parts of the feet. The phrase 'to turn on one's heels' idiomatically means to turn back, retreat, or abandon a path one had set out on.
20.grammar: A dual noun ('two heels') with the attached pronoun -hi ('his/its'). The -ay- ending is the dual form used in the accusative/genitive (it would be -ā in the nominative), marking exactly two of something. The pronoun ending -hi (rather than -hu) takes its 'i' vowel to harmonize with the preceding 'y' sound.
20.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — heel, that which comes behind/after

21.meaning: So never / then never — a connector 'so/then' joined to an emphatic particle of negation that denies a future action absolutely: 'will never (at all)'.
21.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', linking to what precedes. 'lan' negates a following present-tense verb and casts it into the future with emphatic force ('will never'); it also puts that verb into the subjunctive, which shows up as a final '-a' on the verb.

22.meaning: 'He harms / injures' — to do damage or hurt to someone or something.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular, with the ya- prefix for 'he'. This is a doubled (geminate) verb: the final -a vowel on the doubled consonant marks the SUBJUNCTIVE (manṣūb) mood used after certain particles, conveying 'that he should harm'. (Note: the jussive of a geminate verb would instead drop this vowel — yaḍurr with sukūn — so the -a here is specifically subjunctive, not jussive.)

23.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
23.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
23.root: — (proper name)

24.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
24.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'
24.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — thing, to will

25.meaning: 'And He will reward / requite' — to repay or recompense someone for what they have done, with future certainty; combined here with 'and' and a particle stressing futurity.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he', from the ya- prefix), prefixed by 'wa-' ('and') and the future marker 'sa-' ('will'). The final long -ī is the verb's weak final letter; the form here functions as a plain future statement, 'and He will requite'.

26.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
26.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

27.meaning: 'The grateful ones / the thankful' — those who recognize and acknowledge benefit and respond with gratitude, as a defined group.
27.grammar: An active participle ('one who is grateful') made definite by 'al-' ('the') and put in the sound masculine plural with the ending -īna.
