9.grammar: A singular adjective. The -an (tanwīn) ending is the indefinite accusative, commonly marking it as the predicate of a 'was/had been' type sentence or the object of a verb — describing someone as 'harsh.'
9.root: ف-ظ-ظ (f-ẓ-ẓ) — harshness, coarseness, roughness of manner

10.meaning: Hard, harsh, rough, or stern — describing something thick, coarse, or unyielding; in the construct form, ready to be linked to what is hard (e.g. 'hard of...').
10.grammar: A singular adjective in the accusative, shown by the final -a (with no tanwīn). The bare -a (rather than -an) signals it is in a construct ('hard of ...'), about to be joined to a following noun that completes the sense, such as 'hard of heart.'

11.meaning: The heart — the inner seat of feeling, understanding, and intention; figuratively the core of a person.
11.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive, which here means the word is the second part of a construct ('... of the heart') or follows a preposition — linking it to a preceding word.
11.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — the heart; turning over, change (the heart as that which turns)

12.meaning: They scattered, dispersed, broke apart, and went off in different directions — a group breaking up and drifting away.
12.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the reflexive Form VII (infaʿala), which gives a sense of something happening to the subject — 'they came apart / scattered.' The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural, 'they.' The prefixed lām (la-) adds emphasis, 'surely/certainly,' typical in the answer to a hypothetical 'if.'
12.root: ف-ض-ض (f-ḍ-ḍ) — to break up, scatter, disperse, separate

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: Around / surrounding / in the vicinity of you (singular) — the area encircling a person.
14.grammar: A noun of place meaning 'the area around,' used adverbially ('around'). Its base genitive ending -i is carried by the attached pronoun -ka ('your'), so the whole means 'around you.' The pronoun -ka here addresses a single male.
14.root: ح-و-ل (ḥ-w-l) — to surround, encircle; turning/change around something

15.meaning: So pardon / overlook / efface — to forgive a fault and wipe it away as though it never was, here as a command 'then pardon!'
15.grammar: A command (imperative) Form I verb addressed to one person, 'pardon!' The final weak letter of the root drops in the command, leaving the short -u sound. The fa- prefix links it to what precedes as a consequence, 'so/then (pardon).'
15.root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w) — to pardon, efface, forgive; to let pass without penalty

16.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
16.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

17.meaning: A command meaning 'and seek forgiveness' — an appeal to Allah to cover, pardon, and protect one from the consequences of sin. The verb conveys actively asking for that pardon, not merely wishing for it.
17.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'do (you) seek forgiveness.' The form built on the ist- pattern conveys 'to ask/seek for' something, so it means 'request forgiveness.' The bare ending with no final vowel marks it as a direct order. The wa- prefix simply links it to what precedes as 'and.'

18.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
18.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

19.meaning: A command meaning 'and consult them' — to seek others' opinion and take mutual counsel with them before deciding, treating their input as worthy of weight.
19.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'do (you) consult.' The verb is of the form that implies mutual, back-and-forth dealing — here, exchanging counsel. The attached -hum is the object 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group). The bare stem ending marks a direct order. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
19.root: ش-و-ر (sh-w-r) — to consult, take counsel, seek advice

20.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
20.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

21.meaning: The matter, affair, command, or decision — either a thing being dealt with or an authoritative order that is issued. The definite article marks it as a specific, known matter.
21.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links it to a preceding noun ('… of the matter') or follows a preposition.
21.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; a matter or affair

22.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
22.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.

23.meaning: Means 'you resolved / made a firm decision' — to settle one's will firmly on a course of action and commit to carrying it out.
23.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ta ending marks the doer as 'you' (a single male) who completed the action: 'you resolved / you determined.' The past tense presents the firm decision as something already taken.
23.root: ع-ز-م (ʿ-z-m) — to resolve, be firmly determined

24.meaning: A command meaning 'then rely / put your trust' — to commit one's affair wholly to Allah, depending on Him for the outcome after doing what one can.
24.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'do (you) rely / put trust.' The verb's doubled pattern carries the sense of wholly committing oneself in reliance. The bare stem ending marks a direct order. The fa- prefix means 'then' or 'so,' signaling that this follows on from something prior.
24.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, rely upon, commit one's affair

25.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
25.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
25.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

26.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
26.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

27.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
27.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

28.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
28.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

29.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
29.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
29.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

30.meaning: Means 'those who rely / the trusting ones' — people whose settled habit is to commit their affairs to Allah and depend on Him.
30.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) made plural for males: 'the ones who rely.' The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the object or prepositional form (as opposed to -ūna, the subject form). The l- prefix means 'the.'
30.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, rely upon, commit one's affair

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: Means 'He helps / gives victory to you' — to aid, support, and grant triumph to someone, especially against an adversary.
2.grammar: A present/future verb. The ya- prefix marks the doer as 'he' (or a singular non-human subject). The attached -kum is the object 'you' (a group), here voweled as -kumu so it can join smoothly to the next word. The shortened stem vowel reflects that the verb stands in a non-indicative position (after a conditional or jussive context).
2.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, support, grant victory

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
4.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

5.meaning: Means 'one who overcomes / a victor' — the party that prevails, defeats, and gains the upper hand over another.
5.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun): 'one who overcomes / prevails.' The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form a noun takes as an object or after certain particles. Used in a construction of 'no … at all,' it can convey 'there is no overcomer.'

6.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

7.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
7.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

8.meaning: Means 'He forsakes / abandons you' — to withhold help and leave someone to fend for themselves, letting them down at a time of need.
8.grammar: A present/future verb. The ya- prefix marks the doer as 'he' (or a singular non-human subject). The attached -kum is the object 'you' (a group). The shortened stem ending shows the verb stands in a non-indicative (conditional/jussive) position rather than as a plain statement.
8.root: خ-ذ-ل (kh-dh-l) — to forsake, abandon, withhold support

9.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
9.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

10.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'this one' or 'the one' — a pointing word ('that/this') used to single out a person or thing. It often combines with the question particle to form 'who is it that…?'
10.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this/that one'). It does not take case endings; the final -ā is part of the fixed word. It functions to point out or identify someone or something.

11.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

12.meaning: Means 'He helps / gives victory to you' — to aid, support, and grant triumph to someone.
12.grammar: A present/future verb. The ya- prefix marks the doer as 'he' (or a singular non-human subject). The -u on the stem (nṣuru) is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement of fact: 'he helps.' The attached -kum is the object 'you' (a group).
12.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, support, grant victory

13.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
13.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

14.meaning: 'After him / it' — 'baʿd' denotes what comes afterward in time or sequence, here joined to 'him/it'.
14.grammar: A time-noun 'baʿd' (afterness) with an attached pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. The '-i' vowel on 'baʿd' is its case ending, set by 'baʿd's' own position in the sentence (commonly governed by a preceding preposition), not by the suffix; the attached '-hi' is the possessor ('him/it'), and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive. The pronoun's 'i'-vowel (-hi rather than -hu) follows because it comes after a genitive '-i'.
14.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, distance

15.meaning: A two-part phrase: the joining word 'and' plus the preposition 'on / upon / incumbent upon,' often used to express an obligation resting on someone.
15.grammar: The connector 'wa' ('and') joined to the preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon'). Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending; a noun governed by 'ʿalā' takes the genitive.

16.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
16.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

17.meaning: An exhortation: 'so let (someone) put their trust' — to place complete reliance and dependence (tawakkul) upon Allah, committing one's affairs to Him.
17.grammar: A third-person command (jussive of command). 'fa-' connects ('so'), the prefixed 'li-' turns the verb into an order ('let him…'), and 'ya-' marks a third-person 'he' subject. The final '-i' is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before the next word, not a case ending.
17.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, rely, commit one's affairs

18.meaning: The believers — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm the truth and give it their security and assent.
18.grammar: A definite noun, the active participle of form IV ('mu'min,' 'one who believes/grants security'). The plural ending '-ūna' marks a masculine human plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or doer ('the believers' as those performing the action).
18.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust, faith

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: To a prophet / for a prophet. The li- is the preposition 'to/for', and 'nabiyy' means a prophet — one chosen and inspired by Allah to convey His guidance to people.
3.grammar: Li- is a preposition ('to/for') and always puts the following noun in the genitive case. The -in ending is genitive with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite: 'a prophet').
3.root: Two derivations are recognized: ن-ب-أ (n-b-') — news, tidings (a prophet as one who conveys news/revelation from Allah); and ن-ب-و (n-b-w) — to be high/elevated (a prophet as one of exalted rank). The latter underlies the unhamzated spelling نَبِيّ.

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: Means 'he acts treacherously / takes unlawfully from spoils' — to misappropriate or secretly withhold something held in trust, classically defrauding shared war-booty.
5.grammar: A present/future verb with the doer 'he' marked by the ya- prefix. The -a ending here marks the subjunctive, the form a verb takes after certain particles (such as 'that' / 'it is not for … to …'), giving the sense 'that he should misappropriate.' The doubled final letter belongs to the root.
5.root: غ-ل-ل (gh-l-l) — to act treacherously, misappropriate trust/spoils

6.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
6.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

7.meaning: Means 'he acts treacherously / misappropriates' — to secretly take or withhold something held in trust, especially from shared spoils.
7.grammar: A present/future verb with the doer 'he' marked by the ya- prefix. The bare ending with no final vowel (and the doubled root letters separated, ghlul) marks the jussive — the form used in conditions, giving the sense 'if/whoever misappropriates.'
7.root: غ-ل-ل (gh-l-l) — to act treacherously, misappropriate trust/spoils

8.meaning: He/it comes, or brings. From the verb 'to come'; with an object it carries the sense of bringing or producing something.
8.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 3rd person masculine. This root ends weakly in a vowel, and the bare form yati (without a final -ī) shows the jussive or apocopated mood, the clipped form used after conditional particles and in answers to conditions.
8.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming, bringing

9.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
9.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

10.meaning: Means 'he acted treacherously / misappropriated' — completed misappropriation or secret withholding of something held in trust.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb with a built-in doer 'he' (a single male): 'he misappropriated.' The past tense presents the act as already done. The doubled final letter belongs to the root.
10.root: غ-ل-ل (gh-l-l) — to act treacherously, misappropriate trust/spoils

11.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
11.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
11.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

12.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
12.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

13.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
13.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

14.meaning: A present/future-tense passive verb meaning 'it is paid in full, repaid completely, given its full due.' The pattern conveys discharging an obligation entirely, leaving nothing owed.
14.grammar: A present-tense passive verb (the tu- prefix with the inner vowel pattern marks 'is being done to'). It is third-person feminine singular: 'she/it is paid in full.' The verb is built on the Form II intensive pattern (doubled middle root), stressing completeness — full and thorough payment. The final long -ā reflects the weak final root letter.
14.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — fulfilling, completing, paying in full, keeping faith with an obligation

15.meaning: A noun meaning 'all, every, each, the whole of.' It expresses totality — when joined to a following noun it means 'every (one)' or 'the entirety of' that thing.
15.grammar: A noun of totality with the final -u ending (nominative). The -u typically marks it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It normally attaches to a following noun to mean 'every / all of' it.

16.meaning: A noun meaning 'soul, self, person, living being.' It denotes the inner self or the whole individual — the seat of life and identity, and by extension a 'person' as a single unit.
16.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a soul'). This form appears after prepositions or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun (such as 'every soul').
16.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being

17.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
17.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

18.meaning: 'It earned / acquired, gained' — said of deeds and their consequences; the root means to gain or acquire something, especially the moral 'earnings' of one's actions.
18.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it.' The past tense presents the action as completed.
18.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

19.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
19.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

20.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
20.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

21.meaning: They are wronged / treated unjustly — to suffer ẓulm, the placing of something out of its right place: injustice, oppression, being deprived of one's due. The passive form names being on the receiving end of wrongdoing.
21.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine plural. The yu- prefix (with the internal vowelling) marks the third person and the passive 'are being …', and the -ūna ending makes it 'they' (masculine plural) as the ones undergoing the action: 'they are wronged'. The -na is the indicative marker.

1.meaning: A compound opener meaning roughly 'Is then he who …?' — it poses a pointed question, often contrasting two parties, with 'man' picking out the person ('the one who').
1.grammar: Three pieces fused together. The opening a- is the question marker ('is …?'). The fa- means 'then / so,' linking to what came before. 'man' is the relative/interrogative 'who / the one who'; its base form ends in a silent consonant but is here given the helping vowel -i (mani) so it joins smoothly to the next word. The whole sets up a rhetorical contrast.

2.meaning: Means 'he followed / pursued' — to go after something and adopt it, walking in its path or seeking it out, whether following a person, a way, or an aim.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with a built-in doer 'he' (a single male): 'he followed.' It is built on the reflexive ift'aʿala pattern (which inserts a -t- after the first root letter); this pattern adds the sense of actively pursuing or making something one's own. Here the first root letter ت merges with that inserted -t-, producing the doubled ت heard at the start (it-ta-) — so the doubling is at the front from this merging, not in the middle root letter. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending.
2.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

3.meaning: Means 'good pleasure / approval' — the state of being well-pleased and contented, especially Allah's pleasure as the highest object of a believer's striving.
3.grammar: A noun naming the abstract idea of being well-pleased. The -a ending marks the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or after certain particles. It frequently stands in a possessive link ('the pleasure OF …').
3.root: ر-ض-و (r-ḍ-w) — to be pleased, content, satisfied

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: Means 'like one who …' — combines 'like / as' with 'the one who,' setting up a comparison to a person defined by what they do.
5.grammar: Two pieces: the prefix ka- means 'like / as' (a comparison particle that puts the following noun in the genitive), and 'man' is the relative pronoun 'who / the one who.' Together: 'like the one who …,' typically contrasting one party with another.

6.meaning: Means 'he returned / came back (bearing something)' — to come back drawing a burden upon oneself; with an unwelcome thing it conveys incurring or bringing it back on oneself.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb with a built-in doer 'he' (a single male): 'he returned / came back laden.' The past tense presents it as completed. It is commonly paired with 'with' (bi-) to mean returning carrying or having earned something.
6.root: ب-و-ء (b-w-ʾ) — to return, come back, settle into / incur

7.meaning: Means 'with wrath / displeasure' — a thing carried or incurred, where 'sakhaṭ' is anger and strong displeasure (here typically Allah's).
7.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with / by means of' and places the following noun in the genitive. The noun's -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n indicating it is indefinite): 'with a wrath / displeasure.' The genitive is the case a noun takes after a preposition like bi-.
7.root: س-خ-ط (s-kh-ṭ) — to be angry, displeased, indignant

8.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
8.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: Means 'and his refuge / abode' — the place to which one ultimately resorts and where one comes to rest or dwell.
10.grammar: A place-noun (a 'place of …' form) meaning 'place of resort / dwelling.' The attached -hu is the possessive 'his / its.' The wa- prefix means 'and.' The -u vowel on the attached pronoun (hu) reflects its base form after a long vowel.
10.root: أ-و-ي (ʾ-w-y) — to take shelter, resort to, give refuge

11.meaning: Hell / Jahannam — the proper name of the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter.
11.grammar: A proper name (the name of Hell), treated as a feminine, non-fully-inflecting noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, marking it as the subject/predicate of a statement ('… is Jahannam'). Because it is a proper name of this type, it does not take the usual final '-n' (tanwīn) of ordinary nouns.

12.meaning: And how evil / wretched (it is)! — wa joined to biʾsa, a fixed verb of blame used to condemn something as bad, the opposite of niʿma ('how excellent'). It expresses strong disapproval.
12.grammar: Conjunction wa- ('and') plus biʾsa, a frozen verb of blame ('how wretched is …') that does not change for tense. It introduces strong condemnation of whatever follows as its subject, the counterpart of niʿma ('how good is …').

13.meaning: Al-maṣīr — the destination, the place or state one finally comes to; the journey's end or ultimate outcome to which things return.
13.grammar: A definite noun of place/result on the pattern mafʿil, with the long ī arising from the weak root letter yāʾ (ص-ي-ر). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or what something ultimately is. The word denotes the final place or state to which one comes.
13.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become, come to, end up at

1.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
1.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

2.meaning: Means 'ranks / degrees / levels' — gradations of standing or rank, one tier above another, like rungs by which things differ in elevation.
2.grammar: A feminine plural noun: 'degrees / ranks.' The -un ending is the nominative with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite): 'degrees / ranks (are…).' The nominative is the case for the subject of a sentence. The long -ā- is the plural-pattern vowel.
2.root: د-ر-ج (d-r-j) — to ascend by steps, gradation, rank

3.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
3.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
5.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
5.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

6.meaning: 'All-Seeing / fully observant' — one who sees clearly and with complete insight; as a divine attribute, the One who perceives all things.
6.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting one who possesses sight to a high degree — 'all-seeing'. The -un ending (tanwīn) is nominative plus indefiniteness, the form used for a subject or for a predicate ('[He] is all-seeing').

7.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
7.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

8.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
8.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
8.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
1.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

2.meaning: Means 'he bestowed a favour / showed grace' — to confer a benefit or kindness upon someone; the same root can also mean to recount a favour reproachfully, but the core sense is granting a gracious gift.

parts.en: he bestowed a favour / showed grace

2.grammar: A past-tense verb with a built-in doer 'he' (a single male): 'he bestowed a favour.' The past tense presents the act of grace as completed. It is commonly followed by 'upon' (ʿalā) to name the one favoured. The doubled final letter belongs to the root.
2.root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n) — to bestow favour/grace; to confer a benefit

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
4.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
4.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

5.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
5.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

7.meaning: 'He raised up / sent forth / dispatched' — a past-tense verb. The root sense is to rouse or set something in motion; of a person it means to send or commission, and of the dead it means to resurrect.
7.grammar: A complete past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he raised/sent'. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for 'he' (a single male doer in completed past action).
7.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — rousing, sending forth, raising up (including resurrection)

8.meaning: "in them / among them" — the preposition 'in/among' joined to the pronoun 'them,' locating something within or amid a group of people.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun, giving 'fīhim.' The preposition 'fī' keeps its long 'ī.' The pronoun '-him' is the third-person masculine plural ('them'); its vowel is 'i' (rather than '-hum') because it follows the high front vowel 'ī' of 'fī'.
8.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

9.meaning: "a messenger / an envoy" — one who is sent bearing a message; 'rasūl' is an emissary commissioned to convey something on behalf of the one who sent him, especially a prophet sent with a divine message.
9.grammar: A masculine noun on the faʿūl pattern, indefinite ('a messenger'). The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the indefinite accusative case, the form used for the direct object of a verb; the written alif carries this ending.
9.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message, messenger

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

11.meaning: Themselves / their own selves — the noun nafs ('self, soul, person, inner being') joined to a pronoun 'their'. Used reflexively it means 'their own selves' and conveys the inmost self, the seat of desires and the person as a whole.
11.grammar: The plural noun anfus ('selves') carries the genitive -i ending followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by a preposition or joined to a preceding word; -him makes it 'their selves'.
11.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

12.meaning: "he recites / he reads aloud / he follows" — to recite or read out (especially scripture), conveying the sense of following the words one after another; 'talā' is to recite, and also to follow closely.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he recites / will recite'). The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he/it' as the doer. The verb is from a root ending in a weak letter, which surfaces as the long 'ū' ('yatlū'); the final long vowel here reflects the indicative (statement) mood. Final '-ā' in the script (alif) is a spelling convention.
12.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud; to follow

13.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
13.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
13.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

14.meaning: 'His signs / His verses.' The plural of a word meaning a sign, token, or mark that points to a greater reality — also used for the verses of revelation — here joined to 'his'.
14.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form this plural takes when it follows a preposition or is linked as the object of a possessor; the -hi ('his') marks ownership: 'his signs'.
14.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark; a verse of revelation

15.meaning: "and he purifies them / cleanses and improves them" — to purify, cleanse, and cause to grow in goodness; 'zakkā' (form II) means to make pure and wholesome, removing what is corrupt and nurturing what is righteous.

parts.en: purify / cleanse and cause to grow

15.grammar: A present-tense form-II verb, third-person masculine singular ('he purifies'), with the object pronoun 'them' attached. The 'yu-' prefix marks 'he/it' for this doubled-letter form-II verb; the long 'ī' before the pronoun is the verb's weak final letter. The pronoun '-him' is third-person masculine plural ('them'), its vowel 'i' following the 'ī' sound.
15.root: ز-ك-و / ز-ك-ي (z-k-w / z-k-y) — purity, growth, increase in goodness

16.meaning: "and he teaches them / instructs them" — to teach, instruct, or impart knowledge; 'ʿallama' (form II) is the intensive/causative of 'to know,' i.e. to cause someone to know, to school them in something.
16.grammar: A present-tense form-II verb, third-person masculine singular ('he teaches'), with the object pronoun 'them' attached. The 'yu-' prefix (with 'u') marks the doubled-middle-letter form-II verb and means 'he/it.' The pronoun is normally '-hum,' but its vowel becomes 'u' ('-humu') to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a vowel-cluster.
16.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing; (form II) to teach

17.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
17.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
17.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

18.meaning: "and the wisdom" — sound judgement and deep understanding that puts things in their right place; 'ḥikma' is wisdom: knowledge joined to right action, insight into the true nature and proper order of things.
18.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the wisdom'); 'wa-' is 'and' and 'al-' is 'the.' The final '-a' is the accusative case ending, the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb or when joined to another accusative noun.
18.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, govern wisely; wisdom, sound judgement

19.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
19.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

20.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
20.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
20.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

21.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
21.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

22.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
22.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
22.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

23.meaning: A two-part expression meaning 'surely in / indeed within'. It joins an emphasis particle ('surely, indeed') with the preposition 'in', stressing that something is firmly located or contained inside.
23.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphatic particle ('surely, indeed') used to strengthen a statement. fī is a preposition ('in/within') and, like all prepositions, governs a following noun, putting it into the genitive case.

24.meaning: Means 'straying / error / being lost' — wandering off the right path, the opposite of guidance, whether literally losing one's way or going astray in belief and conduct.
24.grammar: An abstract noun: 'straying / error.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite) — the case a noun takes after a preposition or in a possessive link, e.g. 'in an error.' The long -ā- belongs to this noun-pattern.
24.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

25.meaning: Means 'clear / plain / making manifest' — something that is evident in itself and also makes other things plain, leaving no ambiguity.
25.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) from a pattern that often carries the sense 'making clear' as well as 'being clear.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite), the form taken after a preposition or when describing a genitive noun — i.e. it agrees with a preceding indefinite noun in the genitive ('a clear …').
25.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct; to make evident

1.meaning: A cluster opening a rhetorical question and joining it disjunctively to what precedes, then introducing a past-time clause: roughly 'Or when…?' / 'Is it that, when…?' The opening hamza poses an interrogative-cum-rebuke (often expecting agreement or expressing reproach); the connective carries the disjunctive 'or' sense; and 'lammā' marks a point in past time meaning 'when' or 'at the moment that'.
1.grammar: A cluster of particles, so it has no case or tense ending. The leading hamza signals a yes/no question, frequently rhetorical. The following connective functions as the disjunctive 'or', linking the question to what came before. 'Lammā' governs a following past-tense clause and points to a definite moment in the past ('when…') rather than the future.

2.meaning: It (feminine) befell, struck, or afflicted you — said of a calamity, blow, or misfortune reaching and hitting its target.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form IV. The '-at' ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it did'). The attached '-kum' is the object pronoun 'you (all)', so the whole means 'it struck you (pl.).' The verb denotes a completed action.
2.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, befall correctly

3.meaning: A calamity, affliction, or misfortune — something distressing that strikes a person, especially trouble that arrives suddenly and from outside one's control.
3.grammar: An active-participle-based feminine noun, here standing as a singular indefinite noun. The final -un (nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a misfortune') and in the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified.
3.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit a target, to strike, to befall (also linked to what is right/apt)

4.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

5.meaning: You (plural) struck, hit, or inflicted (something on someone) — to land a blow or attain a target.
5.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form IV. The '-tum' suffix marks the subject as second-person masculine plural ('you all did'). It describes a completed act of striking or hitting a target.
5.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, befall correctly

6.meaning: Twice the like of it / double its amount — 'two times the equivalent' of some quantity.

parts.en: two likes of / double the equal of

6.grammar: A noun in the dual ('two of a like'). The '-ay' ending is the dual form used in the object/genitive state, meaning 'two equivalents of.' The attached '-hā' is a feminine possessive pronoun ('of it'), so the phrase means 'two times its like.'

7.meaning: 'You (plural) said' — to say, speak, or utter. The verb covers any act of stating or declaring something in words.
7.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix -tum marks the masculine plural 'you (all)' as the doers of a completed action — it signals both the past tense and that the speakers being addressed are a group. (This is a hollow verb: its middle root letter is a wāw, which surfaces as a long ā in the base form qāla but reduces to a short u, giving qul-, before a consonant-initial suffix like -tum.)
7.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

8.meaning: A particle/adverb meaning 'in whatever manner,' 'from wherever,' or 'whenever' — it asks or denotes the how, where, or when of an action in an open-ended way.
8.grammar: An invariable interrogative/conditional adverb; it has no case ending and never changes form. It introduces the manner, place, or time of an action in a general, open sense ('in what way / from where / when').
8.root: — (particle)

9.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
9.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

10.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
10.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

11.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
11.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

12.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
12.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

13.meaning: 'In the presence of / from with / from the side of' — a noun of place and source meaning nearness or 'with,' used for what is in someone's keeping, possession, or vicinity, and figuratively what proceeds from them.
13.grammar: An adverbial noun meaning 'at / with / in the presence of,' here in the genitive case (the -i ending), as happens when it follows a preposition or links to a following noun ('the presence OF …'). It typically expresses 'from the side of' or 'in the keeping of' someone.
13.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — being at, near, or with; presence and proximity

14.meaning: 'Yourselves' — literally 'your own selves/souls.' Anfus is the plural of nafs ('self, soul, person'); with the attached pronoun it expresses the reflexive 'your own selves.'
14.grammar: A plural noun ('selves') with an attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your,' masculine plural). The -i ending is genitive: the noun is governed by a preceding preposition or stands in a possessive ('of …') construction.
14.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self / soul / breath

15.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
15.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
16.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

17.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
17.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

18.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
18.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.
18.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

19.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
19.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
19.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

20.meaning: All-powerful, fully able, ever-capable — possessing complete and effective power to do whatever is willed; one whose ability never falls short.
20.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, abiding quality ('thoroughly able'). The final -un is the indefinite nominative (nunation) — the doubled-n shows no 'the', and the -u base vowel marks the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or a predicate ('… is all-powerful').

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: It struck/befell you (plural). A past-tense verb meaning that something — typically a hardship, calamity, or event — reached, hit, or happened to a group of people. Built on a verb whose core idea is hitting a target or something landing squarely upon someone.
2.grammar: Third-person masculine singular past-tense verb ("it/he struck"), with the attached object pronoun -kum meaning "you all" as the ones struck. It is a Form I hollow verb (its middle root-letter is a weak letter that surfaces as the long ā). No final case-vowel applies; the -a in aṣāba is the verb's own stem vowel.
2.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, strike a target correctly; from this, calamity striking

3.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
3.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
3.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

4.meaning: Met, encountered, came together — a past-tense verb meaning two parties came face to face or clashed/met one another.
4.grammar: A Form VIII third-person masculine singular past-tense verb ("he/it met"), pattern iCtaCaCa. It opens with a connecting (prosthetic) hamza — silent when joined to a preceding word — followed by the first root letter (l), then the Form VIII infix -t-, which often gives a mutual or reflexive sense (here, two sides meeting each other). The final -ā is the verb's own weak ending (a defective root ending in a long vowel), not a case marker.
4.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, come upon

5.meaning: The two gatherings / the two hosts — the dual of "a gathering, assembly, or massed body," meaning specifically two such groups or armies (a "gathering" being a collected mass of people).
5.grammar: A definite noun in the dual (meaning exactly two) with the -āni ending, which is the nominative dual form. This ending both marks "two of them" and typically signals the word is functioning as the subject/doer of a sentence.
5.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — to gather, collect, bring together; a gathered group or assembly

6.meaning: Then by the permission / leave / sanction (of someone) — introducing that something occurred through an authorising will or grant of leave.
6.grammar: A noun preceded by two particles: 'fa-' ('then/so', linking to what precedes) and 'bi-' ('by/through', indicating means or cause). The '-i' ending on 'idhn' is genitive, required after the preposition 'bi-' and typically linking it to a following noun ('… of …').
6.root: ا-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — permission, leave, to give ear/heed

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: 'So that He may make known/known-by-experience' — to bring something to light and distinguish it through what actually happens, so it becomes manifest and proven (a knowing tied to outcome, not the mere awareness already possessed).
8.grammar: Prefix wa- ('and') + purpose particle li- ('so that') + a present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('He knows/makes evident'). The li- of purpose puts the verb in the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a ending, which is the form used after 'so that / in order to'.
8.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, to know

9.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
9.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

1.meaning: 'So that He may make known/known-by-experience' — to bring something to light and distinguish it through what actually happens, so it becomes manifest and proven (a knowing tied to outcome, not the mere awareness already possessed).
1.grammar: Prefix wa- ('and') + purpose particle li- ('so that') + a present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('He knows/makes evident'). The li- of purpose puts the verb in the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a ending, which is the form used after 'so that / in order to'.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They acted as hypocrites — they professed faith outwardly while concealing disbelief or ill intent inwardly; they were two-faced in religion.

parts.en: they played the hypocrite (Form III stem)

3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form III. The '-ū' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they did'). It denotes the completed act of behaving hypocritically — showing one thing while hiding another.
3.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — hypocrisy; a burrow with two exits (the image behind 'nifāq')

4.meaning: And it was said — a statement was uttered or a command was given (by an unnamed speaker).
4.grammar: A past-tense passive verb. The internal vowel pattern (qīla, with 'ī') marks it as passive — the doer is unspecified, so it means 'it was said' rather than 'he said.' The final '-a' is the standard ending of a third-person masculine singular past verb.

5.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
5.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

6.meaning: 'Come! / Come now!' — a call summoning people to approach or come forward, often used to invite a group toward a course of action.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group, masculine plural ('you all'). The -aw ending carries the plural 'you' addressees; the silent alif is a spelling convention written after this plural ending. It is an invitation to approach.

7.meaning: Fight! / Do battle! — a command to engage in combat against an opponent. Form III implies mutual fighting (one party against another).
7.grammar: An imperative (command) verb in Form III, addressed to a group. The '-ū' ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you all.' Form III conveys reciprocal action — to fight against an opposing party.

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
8.root: — (particle)

9.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
9.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative between two or more options, linking possibilities of which one applies.
11.grammar: A connecting particle meaning 'or'. Its base form is aw; the added -i is a 'helping' vowel given to the otherwise-silent final consonant to smooth the link to a following word that begins with a connecting (hamzat-waṣl) alif. It is not a case ending — particles do not take cases.

12.meaning: Defend! / Repel! / Ward off! — a command to push back, drive away, or hold off an attacker or harm.
12.grammar: An imperative (command) verb (Form I). It opens with a helping vowel ('i-') because the root cluster needs support to be pronounced. The '-ū' ending addresses the command to a masculine plural 'you all': 'push back / ward off.'
12.root: د-ف-ع (d-f-ʿ) — to push, repel, ward off, defend

13.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

14.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
14.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

15.meaning: We know / we would know — to have knowledge, awareness, or certain recognition of something.
15.grammar: A present/imperfect verb (Form I). The 'na-' prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The final '-u' is the indicative ending, used for an ongoing or general action ('we know / we do know') that is not negated or subordinated.

16.meaning: Fighting / armed combat / warfare — the act or instance of doing battle (a verbal noun naming the activity itself).
16.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action of fighting) in Form III. The '-an' ending ('tanwīn' fatḥa) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the direct object of a verb or for an indefinite specifier ('… some fighting').

17.meaning: Surely we would have followed you — to go after, accompany, side with, or obey someone. The opening 'la-' adds emphasis: 'we certainly would have followed.'
17.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form VIII, prefixed by emphatic 'la-' (often the answer to a conditional, 'we would surely have…'). The '-nā' ending marks a first-person plural subject ('we did'); the attached '-kum' is the object 'you (all),' giving 'we would have followed you.'
17.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

18.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
18.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

19.meaning: To / toward disbelief — 'kufr' is the active rejection or covering-over of faith and truth: ingratitude toward Allah and denial of what He has revealed.
19.grammar: A noun with two prefixes: 'li-' ('to/for', showing direction or purpose) and the definite article 'al-' (here 'l-'), making it 'the disbelief.' The '-i' ending is genitive, the case required after the preposition 'li-.'
19.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

20.meaning: On that day / that day — pointing back to a particular past day already in view; 'a day, at that time.'
20.grammar: A time-word ('day') joined to 'idhin' ('at that time'), together meaning 'on that day.' The '-in' ('tanwīn') compensates for an understood clause ('the day when…'). The form functions adverbially, locating an event at a specific past moment.

21.meaning: A comparative adjective meaning 'nearer, closer, more proximate' — describing something as having greater nearness, whether in space, time, or affinity.
21.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the 'afʿal pattern ('more …' / 'most …'). The -u ending is nominative, typically marking the word as a subject or as a predicate (the thing being described). It is commonly followed by 'to / for' (li-) to name what something is nearer to.

22.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
22.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

23.meaning: To / toward faith — 'īmān' is inner belief and trusting acceptance: to affirm and have faith in Allah, His messengers, and His revelation, with the heart's security and commitment.
23.grammar: A verbal noun (Form IV, the act/state of believing) with two prefixes: 'li-' ('to/for') and the article 'al-' ('the'), giving 'to the faith.' The '-i' ending is genitive, as required after the preposition 'li-.'
23.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, safety, to believe

24.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
24.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'
24.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — speech; saying, uttering, asserting

25.meaning: With their mouths — by means of what they utter or speak aloud (often contrasted with what their hearts truly hold).
25.grammar: A noun preceded by 'bi-' ('with/by') with an attached possessive pronoun. 'Afwāh' is the broken (irregular) plural 'mouths.' The '-i' ending is genitive after the preposition 'bi-'; the suffix '-him' means 'their,' so the whole reads 'with their mouths.'

26.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
26.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

27.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
27.grammar: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.
27.root: ل-ي-س (l-y-s) — negation, not-being

28.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
28.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

29.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the plural of qalb ('heart'), joined to the pronoun 'their'. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' (qalb) is the seat of understanding, intention, faith, and feeling, not merely the physical organ.
29.grammar: Qulūb is the broken (irregular) plural of qalb, 'hearts'. The -i ending is genitive: here it appears because the noun follows a preposition and because it is possessed by an attached pronoun. The suffix -him means 'their' (a masculine plural group), and its -i- vowel matches the preceding genitive ending. So the whole means 'hearts belonging to them'.
29.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about, change

30.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
30.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
30.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

31.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
31.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

32.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
32.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

33.meaning: They conceal, hide, or keep something hidden — deliberately suppressing knowledge or truth and withholding it from others.
