13.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
13.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

14.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they associated partners / they set up partners (with Allah)' — to ascribe partners or equals to Allah, the act underlying idolatry and polytheism.
14.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in a pattern meaning 'to make (someone) a partner'. The ending -ū marks a masculine-plural subject, 'they', so it reads 'they associated partners (with Allah)'.
14.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — sharing, partnership, associating partners

15.meaning: Harm, hurt, or an affliction — something offensive or injurious, ranging from a minor irritation or ailment to anything that causes discomfort or distress.
15.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending (written with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative: it marks 'a harm / some harm' as the object of a verb or as part of a descriptive phrase, with the 'n' sound signalling indefiniteness ('a/an').
15.root: أ-ذ-ي (ʾ-dh-y) — to harm, hurt, injure, cause discomfort

16.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
16.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (nunation with fatḥa). The accusative typically marks a verb's object or an indefinite quantity, and the doubled-n sound shows the word is indefinite ('many').
16.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

17.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
17.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

18.meaning: "You are patient / you endure steadfastly" — the act of a group exercising patience: self-restraint, perseverance, and steadfast endurance in the face of hardship.
18.grammar: A present/jussive verb. The ta-…-ū pattern marks a masculine plural addressee, 'you all'. The dropped final -na (taṣbirū rather than taṣbirūna) signals the jussive or subjunctive mood, typical after conditional particles ('if you are patient …').
18.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — patience, endurance, steadfastness

19.meaning: A verb meaning 'and you (plural) guard yourselves / are mindful (of Allah)' — to exercise God-conscious caution, shielding oneself from wrongdoing and divine displeasure. This is the verbal sense of taqwā.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form VIII (ittaqā 'to be wary, God-conscious'), second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The first tā' is the second-person present prefix; the second, doubled tā' results from Form VIII's infixed -t- assimilating with the root's initial wāw (wtaqā → ttaqā). The bare -ū ending (without final -na) marks the subjunctive/jussive mood, used after certain particles or to express purpose ('that you may be mindful'). The prefixed wa- means 'and.'
19.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect

20.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
20.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

21.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
21.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

22.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
22.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

23.meaning: Firm resolve, determination, or settled purpose — the firmness of will to carry something through. In a possessive (genitive) form, it conveys 'firm resolve of …' or 'the firm purpose of …'
23.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… OF …') or comes after a preposition. It signals that this noun is possessed by, or stands in relation to, whatever follows it.
23.root: ع-ز-م (ʿ-z-m) — to resolve firmly, to be determined

24.meaning: The matters, the affairs, the commands — the plural of 'amr,' covering things that are dealt with, ordered, or that come to pass. The definite article makes it 'the matters/affairs.'
24.grammar: A masculine broken (irregular) plural noun made definite by 'al-' ('the'). Its own opening hamza is a connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) that drops in pronunciation after the 'al-', so the cluster is read smoothly as 'al-umūr' even though the underlying noun is أُمُور. The final -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a possessing noun ('… of THE matters') or coming after a preposition.
24.root: أ-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; a matter/affair

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: He took, he seized — a past-tense verb meaning to take hold of, receive, or take up. With certain objects (like a covenant or pledge) it carries the sense of formally taking or binding. The subject is 'he'.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The bare stem with the final -a marks a completed action by a 'he' (third-person masculine singular) subject — 'he took'.

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: Covenant / solemn pact — a firm, binding agreement or treaty; a weightier, more emphatic term for a pledge that is firmly tied and ratified.
4.grammar: A noun built on a pattern denoting an instrument or firm binding (from 'to bind tightly'), hence a solemn, ratified covenant. The '-a' ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object — the covenant taken or made.
4.root: و-ث-ق (w-th-q) — to bind firmly, trust, make secure

5.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
5.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

6.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
6.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
6.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

7.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
7.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
7.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

8.meaning: An emphatic pledge or declaration: 'you shall most certainly make it clear / explain it.' The verb means to make plain, clarify, or expound something so it is unmistakable, here intensified and bound with a solemn assurance, with 'it' as the object.

parts.en: you make clear (present tense, 'you' masculine singular)

8.grammar: A present-tense verb (form II, intensive) addressed to 'you' (masculine singular), gripped on both sides by emphasis: the prefixed la- ('surely') and the attached heavy nūn (-nna, 'most certainly') turn it into a binding affirmation, the kind used in oaths or solemn promises. (A plural addressee would read tubayyinunna.) The attached -hu means 'it/him' as the thing made clear.
8.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct; to make plain

9.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
9.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

10.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
10.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

11.meaning: 'You (all) conceal it / keep it hidden.' The verb means to hide, suppress, or withhold something — especially knowledge or truth — keeping it from others, with 'it' as the thing concealed.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to 'you' (plural). The -ūna ending marks a plural masculine subject ('you all') and signals the ordinary (indicative) present tense — an action being done or habitually done. The attached -hu means 'it/him' as the object being concealed.
11.root: ك-ت-م (k-t-m) — to conceal, suppress, keep secret

12.meaning: 'So they cast it away / flung it behind them.' The verb means to throw down or discard something, often dismissively — to toss aside what one should have kept or honored. The leading 'fa-' adds 'then/so,' and 'it' is the object thrown.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb with the prefixed connector fa- ('then/so'), which links it to what came before and often implies consequence. The -ū ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they'), and the attached -hu means 'it/him' as the thing cast away.
12.root: ن-ب-ذ (n-b-dh) — to throw away, cast off, discard

13.meaning: Behind / beyond — an adverb of place meaning what lies behind or past something; it can also denote what is beyond or in addition to a thing.
13.grammar: An adverb of place (functioning like a preposition). The '-a' ending is the accusative, the standard form for such place-words; it links to a following noun to mean 'behind ___ / beyond ___'.
13.root: و-ر-ي (w-r-y) — that which is behind or hidden from view

14.meaning: Their backs — the plural noun 'ẓuhūr' ('backs', plural of 'ẓahr'), with the attached pronoun 'their'; the back as the rear of the body, often used in idioms for turning away.
14.grammar: A plural noun plus possessive pronoun. The '-i' ending before the pronoun is genitive, the form taken when a noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed; '-him' ('their') completes the possessive phrase 'their backs'.
14.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — the back; to appear, be outward/manifest

15.meaning: 'And they bought / traded for it,' i.e., took something in exchange, acquiring one thing at the price of another. The verb often carries the sense of a bad bargain — purchasing or trading away. The leading 'wa-' means 'and.'
15.grammar: A past-tense verb (form VIII) preceded by wa- ('and'). The -aw ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they') on a verb whose root ends in a weak letter. It describes a completed act of buying or exchanging.
15.root: ش-ر-ي (sh-r-y) — to buy, sell, exchange (trade one thing for another)

16.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
16.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

17.meaning: A price, a payment, the value or sum given in exchange for something.
17.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, commonly marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('a price').

18.meaning: 'A little / a small amount' — an adjective/noun meaning small in quantity, few, scant, or trifling.
18.grammar: A noun/adjective 'little' in the accusative case with indefinite marking (the -an ending, tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks an object or specifies amount/manner; the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite, 'a little.'
18.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — fewness; being little, scant, or small in amount

19.meaning: 'And how wretched / evil is …!' A fixed expression of blame and condemnation — the counterpart to 'how excellent!' It declares something thoroughly bad. The leading 'fa-' adds 'so/and.'
19.grammar: A frozen verb of blame (the opposite of ni'ma, 'how excellent'). It does not conjugate normally; it stands as an exclamation declaring something utterly bad or blameworthy. The prefixed fa- ('so/and') links it to the surrounding statement.
19.root: ب-أ-س (b-ʾ-s) — misery, hardship, wretchedness

20.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
20.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

21.meaning: A verb meaning 'they buy / they trade / they exchange' — to acquire something by giving up something else in return. It often carries the sense of a bad bargain when one trades away something precious.
21.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) form-VIII verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks 'they', and the inseparable -ūna suffix shows the base (indicative) form, expressing an ongoing or habitual act of buying/exchanging.
21.root: ش-ر-ي (sh-r-y) — to buy, sell, trade, exchange (a transaction)

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: Do (not) suppose / reckon / imagine — to think something to be the case, to deem or assume (often a mistaken estimation).
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The heavy '-anna' ending is the emphatic ('nūn of emphasis'), strengthening the verb — typically attached after a command or prohibition ('do not ever suppose…').
2.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to reckon, count, suppose, estimate

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They rejoice / are glad.' The verb means to feel joy, delight, or elation — sometimes wholesome gladness, sometimes exultant self-satisfaction depending on context.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb. The -ūna ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they') and signals the ordinary (indicative) present tense — an action ongoing or habitual.
4.root: ف-ر-ح (f-r-ḥ) — to rejoice, be glad, exult

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
5.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

6.meaning: 'They came / brought,' or 'they did/performed.' The verb means to come or to bring about — to arrive with something, or to carry out an act.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb whose root ends in a weak letter. The -aw ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they'). It describes a completed act of coming or bringing.
6.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive; to bring, do

7.meaning: 'And they love / are fond of.' The verb means to love, cherish, or desire — to hold dear and incline toward. The leading 'wa-' means 'and.'
7.grammar: A present-tense verb (form IV) preceded by wa- ('and'). The -ūna ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they') and signals the ordinary (indicative) present tense — an ongoing or habitual loving.
7.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — to love, hold dear, cherish

8.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
8.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
8.root: — (particle; no root)

9.meaning: 'That they be praised,' i.e., to receive praise or commendation from others. This is the passive sense — being lauded rather than doing the praising.
9.grammar: A passive present-tense verb in the subjunctive mood: it means 'they are praised,' with the subject receiving the action rather than doing it. The shortened -ū ending (the final nūn dropped) shows the verb is governed by a preceding particle such as 'that' or 'so that,' expressing a purpose or hoped-for outcome.

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
10.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

11.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

11.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

12.meaning: 'They do / make / perform' — a very general verb of doing, acting, or carrying out an action; the basic word for performing or making something happen.
12.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya-…-ū framing marks third-person masculine plural ('they'). The long -ū is the plural subject ending. The plain indicative would end in -na (yafʽalūna); its loss marks the verb as non-indicative. For a plural verb the same dropped -na is shared by two moods — the jussive (majzūm), triggered by particles such as 'lam' ('did not'), imperative 'li-,' and conditional 'in' ('if'), and the subjunctive (manṣūb), triggered by 'an' / 'lan' / 'kay' — so the bare form alone does not fix the mood; the governing particle does. The silent final alif (ـوا) is the usual spelling after this ending.

13.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
13.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

14.meaning: An emphatic warning: 'do not ever suppose / reckon them …' The verb means to think, assume, or reckon something to be the case. Here it carries heavy emphasis, with 'them' as the object of the supposition.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to 'you' (singular), reinforced by the attached heavy nūn (-nna), which adds strong emphasis — frequently after a command or prohibition ('do not ever …'). The attached -hum means 'them' as the object being supposed or reckoned.
14.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to reckon, count, suppose, think

15.meaning: 'In a place of safety / a means of escape, salvation, or triumph.' The noun denotes a refuge or attainment of success — escaping harm and reaching deliverance. The leading 'bi-' means 'in' or 'with.'
15.grammar: A feminine noun of place/instrument following the preposition bi- ('in/with'). The -in ending (with the feminine -t-) is genitive and indefinite ('a'), the case required after a preposition. The noun names a place or means by which one is safe or victorious.
15.root: ف-و-ز (f-w-z) — to triumph, succeed, attain safety

16.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
16.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

17.meaning: The punishment, torment, or chastisement — severe penalty or suffering inflicted as retribution.
17.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the punishment') or follows a preposition.

18.meaning: 'And for them / and they have.' A combination expressing possession or entitlement belonging to a group of males: 'and to/for them (belongs).' The particle li- conveys 'for' or 'belonging to,' and the attached pronoun refers to 'them.'
18.grammar: A possessive/benefactive phrase: the preposition li- ('for, belonging to') with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them,' masculine plural). Such 'for X' phrases commonly express that something belongs to or is owed to that party.
18.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

19.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
19.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.
19.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment, chastise

20.meaning: Painful, agonizing, deeply hurtful. An intensive adjective describing something that inflicts severe, grievous pain.
20.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl, conveying a strong, abiding quality ('truly painful'). The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the case of a subject or of a noun's basic naming form), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.

1.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and to Allah (belongs)' — expressing ownership or rightful belonging to Allah; the lām conveys possession or entitlement.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the prepositional phrase 'lillāhi'. This phrase is the preposition 'li-' ('to/for', here showing possession) prefixed to the name 'Allah'; when 'li-' attaches, the connecting hamza and the first lām of the definite article are elided in writing, leaving a single written lām for the preposition followed by the doubled (shadda-bearing) lām of the name. 'Allah' takes the -i (genitive) ending required after a preposition.

2.meaning: Kingdom, dominion, sovereign rule — full ownership and authority over a realm; the right and power to command and dispose.
2.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u marks the nominative case, used when the noun is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('the dominion is …'). The absence of nunation here points to its being made definite by a following possessor in a genitive link.
2.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule; kingship, dominion

3.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

4.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
4.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

5.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
5.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
5.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

7.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
7.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

8.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
8.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
8.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

9.meaning: 'All-Powerful,' 'fully able,' 'one who has complete power and capability.' An intensive form expressing that the one described possesses perfect, unrestricted power to do whatever is willed — a quality applied supremely to Allah.
9.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, established capability. The '-un' ending (tanwīn al-ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the 'subject/predicate' case) together with indefiniteness — typically the role of a subject or, very often, a predicate describing who or what something is.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

3.meaning: Creation / the act of creating — the bringing of things into existence, or the created order that results; also denotes how something is fashioned or formed.
3.grammar: A verbal noun ('creating / creation'). The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the word to a following noun ('the creation OF …') or follows a preposition.

4.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

5.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
5.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

6.meaning: And the alternation / difference — variation and succession one after another (as with turns of night and day), or divergence and disagreement between things.
6.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' A verbal noun (form VIII 'ikhtilāf') meaning succession/alternation or divergence. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically linking to a following noun ('the alternation OF …') or following a preposition.

7.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
7.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').

8.meaning: And the day / daytime — the period of light from dawn to sunset.
8.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and'; 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'n', said an-nahār). A noun for the daylight hours. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the day').
8.root: ن-ه-ر (n-h-r) — daylight; (also) river, flowing

9.meaning: Surely signs, tokens, or clear indications; evidences that point to a greater truth. The prefixed lām adds emphasis ('surely / indeed').
9.grammar: An emphatic particle 'la-' ('surely') joined to an indefinite feminine plural noun ('signs'). The -āt- is the sound feminine plural marker; the final -in (nunation) marks it indefinite. For this plural pattern the -in form serves for both the accusative and the genitive case.

10.meaning: 'for the possessors / owners of' — a phrase meaning those who possess or are endowed with something, governed by 'for' (li-); it is used to attribute a quality to people ('those of …').
10.grammar: The preposition li- ('for, to') + ulī, the oblique (accusative/genitive) plural of a word meaning 'possessors of, those having.' Ulū/ulī has no singular from its own root and always stands in construct with a following noun ('those endowed WITH …'). The -ī form here is the oblique case required after the preposition.
10.root: — (no triliteral root; a defective noun meaning 'possessor of')

11.meaning: The kernels, cores, or innermost parts — figuratively the faculties of sound reason and understanding, the discerning intellect that grasps the heart of a matter. The prefixed "al-" makes it definite ("the").
11.grammar: A definite plural noun (singular "lubb"). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… OF …") or follows a preposition. Here the genitive marks it as the thing possessed after a possessor-word.

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: 'They remember / make mention of,' i.e., to call to mind, invoke, or mention — both inward recollection and outward utterance, often of Allah.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The -ūna ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they') and signals the ordinary (indicative) present tense — an ongoing or habitual remembering and mentioning.
2.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
3.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

4.meaning: 'Standing / standing upright' — the verbal noun of standing, here describing a state ('while standing'). It can also carry the sense of being upright or steadfast.
4.grammar: A singular verbal noun (maṣdar) — the action-noun of standing — used here to describe a state. The -an ending is accusative and indefinite, functioning to describe the manner or circumstance in which something is done ('while standing'). It answers 'how?' or 'in what state?'
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright

5.meaning: 'And sitting / seated' — the verbal noun of sitting, here describing a state ('while sitting'). The leading 'wa-' means 'and.'
5.grammar: A singular verbal noun (maṣdar) — the action-noun of sitting — preceded by wa- ('and'), used here to describe a state. The -an ending is accusative and indefinite, functioning to describe the manner or circumstance ('while sitting'). It answers 'how?' or 'in what state?'
5.root: ق-ع-د (q-ʿ-d) — to sit, be seated, remain

6.meaning: 'And upon / on,' a combination of 'and' with the preposition meaning 'on, upon, over' — indicating resting on a surface, or an obligation/duty laid upon someone.
6.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to the preposition ʿalā ('on/upon'). As a preposition, it places whatever noun follows it into the genitive case and conveys position upon, or a duty resting on, something.

7.meaning: 'Their sides / flanks' — the parts of the body along which a person lies down. With the attached pronoun it means 'their sides.'
7.grammar: A masculine broken (irregular) plural noun with the attached pronoun -him ('their'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word follows a preposition and is also possessed ('… of their sides' / 'their sides'). The attached -him marks a plural possessor, 'their.'
7.root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side, flank; to be beside

8.meaning: 'And they ponder / reflect deeply,' i.e., to think over something attentively, turning it about in the mind to draw out meaning. The leading 'wa-' means 'and.'
8.grammar: A present-tense verb (form V, which adds the sense of doing something to/for oneself — here sustained inner thought) preceded by wa- ('and'). The -ūna ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they') and signals the ordinary (indicative) present tense — ongoing or habitual reflection.
8.root: ف-ك-ر (f-k-r) — to think, ponder, reflect

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

10.meaning: Creation / the act of creating — the bringing of things into existence, or the created order that results; also denotes how something is fashioned or formed.
10.grammar: A verbal noun ('creating / creation'). The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the word to a following noun ('the creation OF …') or follows a preposition.

11.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
11.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

12.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
12.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

13.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

13.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

14.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
14.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

15.meaning: 'You created / brought into being.' The verb means to create, to originate and shape something out of nothing, addressed to a single 'you.'
15.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ta ending marks the subject as 'you' (masculine singular) — the one addressed performed the act. It describes a completed act of creating.

16.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
16.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

17.meaning: 'In vain, falsely, without purpose' — that which is futile, baseless, or empty of truth; the opposite of what is true and well-founded.
17.grammar: An active participle/noun meaning 'something false or futile.' The -an ending is accusative and indefinite, here typically describing the manner or purpose of an action ('in vain, for nothing'). It answers 'how?' or 'to what end?'
17.root: ب-ط-ل (b-ṭ-l) — to be false, vain, void, futile

18.meaning: 'Glory be to You / how far above all flaw You are' — a set exclamation declaring Allah utterly free of any imperfection, partner, or unworthy attribute, paired with 'You.'
18.grammar: A verbal noun, subḥān ('glorification, utter freedom from imperfection'), bound to the attached pronoun -ka, 'You/Your' (one masculine addressee). It stands in the accusative (-a ending) as the exclamatory object of an understood verb ('I declare Your absolute glory') — a fixed formula of praise.
18.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — glorifying, declaring (Allah) free of all imperfection

19.meaning: An appeal: 'so guard us / protect us, shield us.' The verb is a plea to be safeguarded from harm. The leading 'fa-' adds 'so/then,' and 'us' is the object of protection.
19.grammar: A command (imperative) verb from a root with a weak letter, reduced to a short form, with the prefixed fa- ('so/then'). It is a direct request — when addressed to Allah it carries the force of supplication ('protect us'). The attached -nā means 'us' as the ones to be guarded.
19.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield (the root of taqwā)

20.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
20.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

21.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
21.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

1.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

1.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
1.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

2.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
2.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

3.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
3.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

4.meaning: 'You admit / cause to enter, bring in.' The verb means to make something or someone go into a place. This is the causative sense, addressed to a single 'you.'

parts.en: you cause to enter (present tense, form IV, 'you')

4.grammar: A present-tense causative verb (form IV) addressed to 'you' (masculine singular), here in the shortened (jussive) mood, which for a sound verb ends in a silent sukūn (تُدۡخِلۡ, no case vowel). The final short -i is not part of the verb's mood: it is a helping kasra inserted only to break the awkward consonant cluster that forms when this silent ending meets a following word beginning with a connective hamza. It is purely a smoothing vowel of pronunciation. The verb means 'to cause to enter / admit.'

5.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire as a blazing element, and by extension the well-known fire of punishment. The definite article makes it 'the Fire,' a specific, recognized fire rather than fire in general.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('the' + 'fire'), feminine. The article's lām assimilates into the following 'n' (shown by the doubling on nār). The final -a is the accusative case ending, which typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or the object of certain particles.
5.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — to give light, shine, illuminate (the noun nār, 'fire,' derives from this sense of light/blaze)

6.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
6.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

7.meaning: 'You have disgraced him / put him to shame, humiliated him.' The verb means to bring disgrace, abasement, or ignominy upon someone, with 'him' as the object.
7.grammar: A past-tense causative verb (form IV) from a root with a weak letter. The -ta ending marks the subject as 'you' (masculine singular), and the attached -hu means 'him' as the one disgraced. It describes a completed act of shaming or humiliating.
7.root: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — to be disgraced, humiliated, put to shame

8.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
8.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

9.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'for/to the wrongdoers' — al-ẓālimūn being those who do wrong or injustice, who put things out of their rightful place; in religious usage especially those who wrong their own souls through disbelief or transgression.
9.grammar: A definite active participle (a 'doer' noun, 'those who wrong') in the masculine plural, governed by the preposition li- ('for, to'). The plural ending -īna is the genitive/accusative plural form, required here after the preposition. The single written lām after li- is the definite article 'the', its own letter merged into the preposition.
9.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to do wrong, oppress; injustice

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: Helpers, supporters, defenders — those who come to one's aid and rally to one's side, particularly in a cause.
11.grammar: A broken (internally restructured) plural noun, 'helpers'. The ending -in is the indefinite genitive marker (tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('... of ...'); the doubled-n sound ('nunation') signals that it is indefinite ('helpers / any helpers').
11.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, give victory

1.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

1.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
1.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

2.meaning: 'Indeed we …' — an emphatic opener that combines a particle of strong affirmation ('truly, certainly') with the pronoun 'we', stressing and confirming the statement that follows about the speakers.
2.grammar: The emphatic particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('we'). 'Inna' introduces a sentence and lends it certainty and emphasis, while '-nā' is its subject, identifying the speakers as 'we'. This is the fuller, uncontracted form (innanā) of the commonly contracted innā; the extra nūn belongs to the longer pronominal base used to keep the doubled nūn of 'inna' and the nūn of the pronoun distinct rather than merged.

3.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we heard / we listened' — the act of perceiving sound or a message, often carrying the further nuance of heeding or taking in what was said.
3.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The attached ending -nā marks the subject as 'we', so the action is something a group did and finished: 'we heard'.

4.meaning: An active participle meaning 'one who calls out, an announcer, a herald' — a person who proclaims or summons others with a raised voice.

parts.en: accusative ('-an') ending, with tanwīn marking it indefinite

4.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) from Form III. The final -an is the accusative case with tanwīn ('a/an'): it marks the word as an indefinite object of a verb, or as a state/circumstance describing someone.
4.root: ن-د-و / ن-د-ي (n-d-w/y) — to call out, summon, proclaim

5.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he calls out, he summons, he proclaims' — the act of calling to someone, often from a distance or with announcement.
5.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb in Form III. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The final -ī is the verb's weak third root letter (from ن-د-و/ي), which is fully retained here; that retention is the mark of the indicative mood, since the subjunctive adds a vowel to it (يُنَادِيَ) and the jussive drops it entirely (يُنَادِ).
5.root: ن-د-و / ن-د-ي (n-d-w/y) — to call out, summon, proclaim

6.meaning: To / toward faith — 'īmān' is inner belief and trusting acceptance: to affirm and have faith in Allah, His messengers, and His revelation, with the heart's security and commitment.
6.grammar: A verbal noun (Form IV, the act/state of believing) with two prefixes: 'li-' ('to/for') and the article 'al-' ('the'), giving 'to the faith.' The '-i' ending is genitive, as required after the preposition 'li-.'
6.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, safety, to believe

7.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
7.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

8.meaning: 'Believe!' — a command to a group: have faith, trust, and affirm. Built on the verb meaning to attain security and to believe, it calls people to embrace faith.
8.grammar: A command (imperative) verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the verb meaning 'to believe / to have faith'. The -ū ending directs the command to a second-person masculine plural audience, 'you all — believe!'.
8.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust, faith

9.meaning: 'By/in your Lord' — combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the noun 'Lord' (the Master, Sustainer, and Nurturer who owns, provides for, and brings to maturity) with the pronoun 'your (plural)'.
9.grammar: A preposition attached to a noun carrying a possessive pronoun. The preposition bi- ('with/by/in') puts the noun into the genitive case, reflected in the -i vowel of rabbi. The suffix -kum means 'your' addressing a plural group.
9.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master, to nurture and sustain

10.meaning: 'So we believed / we had faith' — the act of coming to faith, trusting, and affirming the truth, attributed to a 'we' subject, introduced by a connective 'so/then'.

parts.en: so / then (connective showing result or sequence)

10.grammar: A prefixed connective fa- ('so/then') on a Form IV perfect (completed-action) verb. The suffix -nā marks the subject as 'we' and the perfect form indicates a completed act ('we believed / have believed').
10.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be safe, secure; to trust, believe

11.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

11.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
11.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

12.meaning: 'So forgive!' — a command to pardon and cover over wrongdoing, to wipe away faults; when addressed to Allah it is a plea, 'forgive us'. The opening 'so/then' links it to a preceding reason.
12.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person, prefixed by 'fa-' ('so, then'), which connects it to something previously stated as its cause. The verb's bare, vowel-less ending (-ir, with no added vowel) is the form a direct order takes. To 'forgive' here carries the root sense of covering over and concealing a fault.

13.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
13.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

14.meaning: Our sins — wrongdoings or offences attributed to 'us'; the plural 'sins/faults' joined to the speakers.
14.grammar: A masculine plural noun ('sins') with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -a ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon — e.g. that which is forgiven or removed).
14.root: ذ-ن-ب (dh-n-b) — sin, offence, fault

15.meaning: 'And efface / blot out / remove' — a command to wipe away or cover over (sins, faults), removing their trace and consequence. The verb conveys both forgiving and erasing.

parts.en: efface, blot out, expiate (Form II command)

15.grammar: A connective wa ('and') on a Form II imperative (a command). The stem is intensive/causative in meaning ('cause to be covered/wiped away'); the silent (sukūn) ending on the final consonant is typical of a singular command addressed to one person ('you, do this!').
15.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; (Form II) to cover over / expiate

16.meaning: 'From us / away from us' — the preposition 'from, away from, off of' joined to the pronoun 'us', indicating removal or separation away from the speakers.
16.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. ʿan means 'away from / off of' (motion or removal away from something), and the suffix -nā is the object 'us'.

17.meaning: 'Our evil deeds / misdeeds / bad acts' — the plural of a word for an evil or harmful action, a fault or wrongdoing, joined to 'our'.
17.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun with a possessive pronoun. The -i vowel before -nā is the genitive ending, which here links the noun to the possessor ('… OF us', i.e. 'our'). The suffix -nā means 'our'.
17.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil, to do harm

18.meaning: 'And take us in full / cause us to pass away' — a command from the verb meaning to take something completely; applied to a soul it means to receive it fully at death, hence 'cause us to die' (as a gathering-back, not loss).

parts.en: take fully, gather back (Form V stem)

18.grammar: A connective wa ('and') on a Form V imperative (command) with an attached object. Form V here means 'to take/receive in full'. The final weak letter is dropped in the command form, and -nā is the object 'us' ('take us fully').
18.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to be complete, to fulfil; (Form V) to take in full / gather back

19.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
19.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

20.meaning: 'The truly righteous / the devoutly good / the pious' — the plural of a noun for those abundant in goodness, dutiful obedience, and sincere virtue, with the definite article 'the'.
20.grammar: A definite plural noun. The final -i is the genitive case: it typically appears when the word follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the righteous'). The plural pattern denotes those who abound in goodness.
20.root: ب-ر-ر (b-r-r) — to be dutiful, pious, abundantly good

1.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

1.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
1.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

2.meaning: 'And give us / grant us / bring to us' — a command to give or bestow, joined to 'us' as the recipient, with a connective 'and'.
2.grammar: A connective wa ('and') on a Form IV imperative (command) from a weak-ending verb, with an attached pronoun. The final weak vowel of the command is reflected before the object -nā ('us'), the one receiving the giving.
2.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to bring, give, bestow

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: 'You promised us' — a completed-action verb meaning 'to promise, pledge, undertake', with 'you (singular)' as the one promising and 'us' as those to whom the promise is made.

parts.en: you (masculine singular subject); the root's final d assimilates into this t, doubling it

4.grammar: A perfect (completed-action) Form I verb. The suffix written with a doubled tā' (-tta) marks the subject as 'you' (masculine singular): the root's final d has assimilated into the subject's t, producing the geminate. The further suffix -nā is the object 'us'. So: a completed promising done by 'you' toward 'us'.
4.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, give one's word

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

6.meaning: 'Your messengers / your envoys' — the plural of a word for one sent with a message (a messenger, apostle, emissary), joined to 'your (singular)'.

parts.en: your (masculine singular), with genitive linking vowel

6.grammar: A plural noun with a possessive pronoun. The -i vowel before -ka is the genitive ending, which here links the noun to its owner ('messengers OF you' = 'your messengers'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressing one male.
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; (noun) one who is sent, a messenger

7.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
7.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

8.meaning: 'You disgrace / humiliate / put to shame us' — a verb meaning to bring shame, disgrace, or humiliation upon someone, with 'you' as subject and 'us' as object.
8.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) Form IV verb. The tu- prefix marks a second-person singular subject ('you'). This is a weak-ending verb whose final yā' is dropped by regular phonological elision before the attached object -nā; this happens in the ordinary indicative and is not a jussive or subjunctive shortening. The suffix -nā is the object 'us' ('you put us to shame').
8.root: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — to be disgraced, humiliated, put to shame

9.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
9.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
9.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

10.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
10.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

11.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
11.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

12.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

13.meaning: 'You break / fail to keep / go back on' — a present-tense verb meaning to break a promise, default on a pledge, or fail to fulfil what was undertaken.
13.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) Form IV verb. The tu- prefix marks a second-person singular subject ('you'). The final -u is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement or ongoing fact ('you break / do break').
13.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, succeed; (Form IV) to break a promise, default

14.meaning: 'The appointed promise / the tryst / the pledged appointment' — a noun for a fixed promise or an appointed time and place agreed upon, with the definite article 'the'.
14.grammar: A definite noun. The final -a is the accusative case, which commonly marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The pattern denotes a fixed appointment or settled promise.
14.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, appoint a time

1.meaning: 'So He responded / answered favourably' — a completed-action verb meaning to answer a call or prayer and grant the request, introduced by a connective 'so/then'.
1.grammar: A connective fa- ('so/then') on a Form X perfect (completed-action) verb. The bare stem with final -a indicates a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it') and a completed act ('he responded'). Form X here carries the sense of answering and granting a request.
1.root: ج-و-ب (j-w-b) — to answer, respond; (Form X) to respond favourably to a request

2.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

3.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Nurturer who owns, provides, and brings to maturity) joined to the pronoun 'their'.
3.grammar: A noun with a possessive pronoun. The -u vowel before -hum is the nominative ending, typically marking the word as the subject/doer. The suffix -hum means 'their', referring to a masculine plural group.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master, to nurture and sustain

4.meaning: That I — the subordinating particle 'that' fused with the pronoun 'I', used to introduce a noun clause stating a fact about oneself.
4.grammar: The particle 'anna' is a subordinating complementizer meaning 'that'; it introduces a factive noun clause (e.g. as the content of 'I inform you that …'). It is not in itself emphatic — its function is to subordinate the clause, not to assert 'indeed' (that sense belongs to the separate particle 'inna'). 'anna' governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative; the attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I/me') serving as its subject.

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: 'I let go to waste / I allow to be lost / I squander' — a present-tense verb meaning to let something be lost, wasted, or rendered fruitless, with 'I' as subject.

parts.en: let go to waste, cause to be lost (Form IV stem)

6.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) Form IV verb. The u- prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). The final -u is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement ('I let go to waste'); Form IV gives the causative sense 'cause to be lost'.
6.root: ض-ي-ع (ḍ-y-ʿ) — to be lost, wasted; (Form IV) to let go to waste

7.meaning: 'Deed / work / action' — a noun denoting a deed, labour, or act that one performs.
7.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) and is also the form a noun takes when followed by a noun it is linked to ('the deed OF …').

8.meaning: 'A doer / a worker / one who acts' — an active participle (the one performing) from the verb 'to work, do', in its indefinite form ('a worker').

parts.en: genitive ('-in') ending with tanwīn marking it indefinite

8.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) from Form I. The ending -in is the genitive case with tanwīn ('a/an'): it marks the word as indefinite and as following a preposition or linked to a preceding noun ('… OF a doer').
8.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to work, do, act

9.meaning: 'From you / among you (plural)' — indicating a part taken out of, or belonging to, a group of people being addressed.
9.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun -kum ('you all,' masculine plural). Together they express partition or origin: a part drawn 'from / among' the addressed group.

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

11.meaning: 'A male' — a noun denoting a male, of human beings or animals.

parts.en: genitive ('-in') ending with tanwīn marking it indefinite

11.grammar: A singular noun. The ending -in is the genitive case with tanwīn ('a/an'): it marks the word as indefinite and typically links it to a preceding noun or follows a preposition ('… OF a male').

12.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
12.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

13.meaning: A female — a female being, whether human or animal; the counterpart of 'male'.
13.grammar: A singular noun denoting a female. It ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case, so its grammatical role is shown by context rather than by a final vowel.

14.meaning: A phrase meaning 'some of you' or 'one part of you'. It singles out a portion of an addressed group, often paired with 'to/for another' to express a reciprocal relationship within that group.
14.grammar: A noun meaning 'a part/some' carrying the -u ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or doer in its clause. The attached -kum means 'of you all' (plural), so the whole means 'some part of you'.
14.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, some

15.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
15.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

16.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
16.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
16.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

17.meaning: 'So those who / then they who' — a connective 'so/then' joined to a relative pronoun meaning 'those who' (a masculine plural group identified by what follows).
17.grammar: A connective fa- ('so/then') on a relative pronoun. 'Alladhīna means 'those who / the ones who' and introduces a description; it refers to a masculine plural group and its form does not change for case.

18.meaning: They emigrated / migrated — they left their homes and abandoned a place, especially departing for the sake of faith.
18.grammar: A past-tense verb of the mutual/effortful (form III) pattern, carrying the sense of cutting oneself off from one's home and people by migrating. The -ū ending means 'they' (masculine plural) as the doers of a completed action. (The written final alif is a silent spelling convention.)
18.root: ه-ج-ر (h-j-r) — leaving, departing, migration

19.meaning: 'And they were driven out / expelled / forced to leave' — a passive completed-action verb meaning to be made to go out or be expelled, with 'they' as those expelled.

parts.en: were driven out, expelled (Form IV passive stem)

19.grammar: A connective wa ('and') on a Form IV perfect (completed-action) verb in the passive voice ('were …-ed'). The vowelling (u–i) marks it as passive; the suffix -ū marks a masculine plural subject ('they'). So: 'they were driven out'.
19.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out; (Form IV) to bring/drive out

20.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
20.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

21.meaning: Their homes or dwellings; the places where they live. 'Diyār' is the plural of 'dār,' a house, abode, or region one inhabits.
21.grammar: A plural noun followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The -i vowel on the stem is the genitive case, here triggered by the attached possessor and typical after prepositions or in possessive linkage ('the homes of…').

22.meaning: 'And they were harmed / hurt / persecuted' — a passive completed-action verb meaning to be subjected to harm, injury, or persecution, with 'they' as those harmed.

parts.en: were harmed, hurt (Form IV passive stem)

22.grammar: A connective wa ('and') on a Form IV perfect (completed-action) verb in the passive voice ('were …-ed'). The internal vowelling marks it as passive; the suffix -ū marks a masculine plural subject ('they'). So: 'they were harmed'.
22.root: أ-ذ-ي (ʾ-dh-y) — to harm, hurt, injure, cause suffering

23.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
23.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
23.root: — (particle)

24.meaning: My way, path, or road — and by extension a course of conduct or a cause one travels toward; with the attached 'my' it denotes the path belonging to the speaker.
24.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the first-person singular possessive ending -ī ('my'). When that pronoun is attached, it both claims ownership and stands in the place where a case-vowel would otherwise show.
24.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, course

25.meaning: And they fought, did battle, or struggled against an opponent — a mutual, reciprocal combat (the form implies engaging an enemy who fights back).
25.grammar: A past-tense verb in the mutual/reciprocal pattern (qātala), prefixed with 'and'. The ending -ū marks a completed action done by a masculine-plural 'they'.

26.meaning: And they were killed or slain — the action of killing carried out upon them by another (passive: they are the ones killed, not the killers).
26.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice, shown by the internal vowel pattern qu-ti-, prefixed with 'and'. The ending -ū marks a masculine-plural 'they' as the ones acted upon.

27.meaning: I shall most certainly blot out, cover over, and wipe away — to efface wrongs so they are concealed and their consequence removed; the wording carries an emphatic vow.
27.grammar: A present/future verb in the intensive (kaffara) pattern. The la- prefix plus the -anna ending together form a solemn emphatic vow ('I will surely, definitely…'); the u- prefix marks the doer as 'I'.
27.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — covering, concealing

28.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
28.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

29.meaning: Their evil deeds, misdeeds, or wrongs — bad actions and the harm or offence they carry; with the attached pronoun, the misdeeds belonging to them.
29.grammar: A feminine sound plural noun (singular sayyiʾa) with the attached possessive 'their'. The -i vowel before -him reflects the genitive/possessive linkage to that pronoun.
29.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — evil, harm, badness
