30.meaning: And I shall most certainly bring them in, cause them to enter, or admit them — to make someone go inside a place; the wording carries an emphatic vow, with 'them' as those admitted.
30.grammar: A present/future causative verb (adkhala, 'to make enter'). The la- prefix with the -anna ending make a solemn emphatic vow; the u- prefix marks 'I' as the doer, and -hum is the object 'them'.

31.meaning: 'Gardens' — the plural of a lush, walled garden thick with trees whose foliage covers the ground. The root sense is concealment by dense greenery; it is the standard word for the gardens of Paradise.
31.grammar: An indefinite sound feminine plural noun ('gardens'). The '-in' (tanwīn) ending marks it as indefinite ('some gardens'), and for this plural form it stands in the oblique case (genitive or accusative), used after prepositions/possessives or as a direct object.
31.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide (hence a dense garden)

32.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
32.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

33.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
33.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

34.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
34.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').

35.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
35.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.

36.meaning: A reward, recompense, or requital — the good return granted for what one has done.
36.grammar: A masculine noun, indefinite (no 'the'). The -an ending (tanwīn) marks the accusative case, often used for the object of a verb or in an explanatory/adverbial sense ('as a reward').

37.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
37.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

38.meaning: 'In the presence of / from with / from the side of' — a noun of place and source meaning nearness or 'with,' used for what is in someone's keeping, possession, or vicinity, and figuratively what proceeds from them.
38.grammar: An adverbial noun meaning 'at / with / in the presence of,' here in the genitive case (the -i ending), as happens when it follows a preposition or links to a following noun ('the presence OF …'). It typically expresses 'from the side of' or 'in the keeping of' someone.
38.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — being at, near, or with; presence and proximity

39.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
39.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

40.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
40.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
40.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

41.meaning: 'With him / in his keeping / that he has' — combining the locational word 'ind ('at, with, in the presence/possession of') with the pronoun 'him'. It conveys that something is held by, present with, or belongs to him.
41.grammar: 'ʿinda' is an adverb of place/possession that always governs a following word in the genitive; here it takes the attached pronoun -hu ('him/his'). The -a on 'ʿinda' is its fixed accusative-style ending as an adverbial. The pronoun -hu means the thing is located with, or owned by, a single male.

42.meaning: Goodness, beauty, or excellence — the quality of being fine, fair, and pleasing; the best or finest instance of something.
42.grammar: A masculine noun. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate ('it is …'). It lacks nunation here because it is bound to a following noun in a possessive ('the goodness/best OF …') construction.

43.meaning: The reward, recompense, or requital — the good return for one's deeds, here made definite ('the').
43.grammar: The same noun made definite by 'the' (al-). The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('the … OF …') or follows a preposition.

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: It should deceive, delude, or beguile you — to lull someone with a false impression so they are taken in; with an emphatic force and 'you' as the one deceived.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine 'he/it' as doer, the emphatic -anna ending ('surely/definitely'), and the object -ka, 'you'. Such wording commonly conveys a warning ('let it not deceive you').

3.meaning: The moving about, going to and fro, or turning back and forth — restless coming-and-going from one state or place to another.

parts.en: moving about, fluctuating, going to and fro

3.grammar: A verbal noun of the taqallaba pattern (to turn/shift about repeatedly). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence ('the moving about [is/does …]').

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
5.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: The lands, regions, or countries — settled territories and their cities (plural of balad).
7.grammar: A plural noun made definite by 'the' (al-). The -i ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as following a preposition or as the second noun in a possessive 'of' link.

1.meaning: Provision, enjoyment, or maintenance; a beneficial gift of goods, comfort, or sustenance that one is given to make use of, typically for a limited time.
1.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the indefinite nominative — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for the thing being stated to exist ('there is a provision').
1.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to provide enjoyment/benefit; goods, comfort

2.meaning: Little, few, small in amount, or scant — slight in quantity or duration.
2.grammar: An adjective/noun, indefinite. The -un ending (tanwīn) is nominative, the case typically used for a subject or a predicate ('[it is] little').

3.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
3.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

4.meaning: Their place of return, abode, or dwelling — the destination where one comes to rest or take shelter; with the attached pronoun, the lodging belonging to them.
4.grammar: A place-noun (the spot where one takes shelter) with the attached possessive 'their'. Because it ends in a fixed long vowel (ā), its case does not change in spelling; the pronoun -hum supplies the 'their'.
4.root: أ-و-ي (ʾ-w-y) — taking shelter, giving refuge, lodging

5.meaning: Hell / Jahannam — the proper name of the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter.
5.grammar: A proper name (the name of Hell), treated as a feminine, non-fully-inflecting noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, marking it as the subject/predicate of a statement ('… is Jahannam'). Because it is a proper name of this type, it does not take the usual final '-n' (tanwīn) of ordinary nouns.

6.meaning: And how evil / wretched (it is)! — wa joined to biʾsa, a fixed verb of blame used to condemn something as bad, the opposite of niʿma ('how excellent'). It expresses strong disapproval.
6.grammar: Conjunction wa- ('and') plus biʾsa, a frozen verb of blame ('how wretched is …') that does not change for tense. It introduces strong condemnation of whatever follows as its subject, the counterpart of niʿma ('how good is …').

7.meaning: The resting-place / bed / cradle — a spread-out surface prepared to lie or settle upon; figuratively the abode or 'couch' that has been made ready for someone.
7.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-' = 'the') meaning 'bed, resting-place.' The final -u is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the noun as the subject or predicate of a sentence ('… and an evil resting-place it is'). The pattern denotes a place or thing made smooth and spread out.
7.root: م-ه-د (m-h-d) — to spread out, make level/smooth; a bed or cradle prepared for rest

1.meaning: But, however, rather — a particle that sets off a correction or contrast with what came before, redirecting the statement.

parts.en: kasra of the light (reduced) particle form

1.grammar: A contrastive particle meaning 'but/however'. This is the light/reduced form of the emphatic لٰكِنَّ (lākinna): the doubled nūn is elided and the particle no longer governs a following noun. The final kasra (-i) belongs to the identity of this reduced form rather than being mere pronunciation liaison.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They were mindful of Allah / guarded themselves'. This is the act of taqwā: being conscious of Allah, guarding oneself against wrongdoing out of reverence for Him, and shielding oneself from His displeasure. Past tense, masculine plural.

parts.en: to be mindful of Allah / guard oneself

3.grammar: This is a past-tense verb of the reflexive/intensive pattern (form VIII), conveying that the subjects actively guarded and protected themselves. The '-aw' (written ـوا) ending marks a masculine plural subject acting in completed past time ('they did').

4.meaning: Their Lord, Master, and Sustainer — 'rabb' is the one who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached pronoun, the Lord who is theirs.
4.grammar: A masculine noun with the possessive 'their' attached. The -a vowel before -hum marks the accusative case, the case typically used for the object of a verb.

5.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
5.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

6.meaning: Gardens — lush, enclosed places of greenery, trees, and shade; the plural of a single garden, evoking abundant, sheltered groves.
6.grammar: A feminine plural noun, indefinite. The final -un (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite ('gardens'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a predicate ('they are …').
6.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — covering, concealing (a garden's foliage covers the ground)

7.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
8.root: — (preposition)

9.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
9.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').

10.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
10.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.

11.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
11.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.

12.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
12.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

13.meaning: An offering of welcome, a lodging prepared for a guest, or a hospitable provision laid out on arrival.
13.grammar: A masculine noun, indefinite. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks the accusative, commonly used here for an object or in an explanatory sense ('as a welcome-gift').
13.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — descending, alighting, being a guest

14.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
14.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

15.meaning: 'In the presence of / from with / from the side of' — a noun of place and source meaning nearness or 'with,' used for what is in someone's keeping, possession, or vicinity, and figuratively what proceeds from them.
15.grammar: An adverbial noun meaning 'at / with / in the presence of,' here in the genitive case (the -i ending), as happens when it follows a preposition or links to a following noun ('the presence OF …'). It typically expresses 'from the side of' or 'in the keeping of' someone.
15.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — being at, near, or with; presence and proximity

16.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
16.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

17.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
17.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

18.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
18.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').
18.root: — (adverb of place)

19.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
19.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

20.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
20.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
20.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

21.meaning: For the righteous, the dutiful, the truly good — 'abrār' are those abounding in piety and kindness; the prefixed 'for/to' marks them as recipients or beneficiaries.

parts.en: the righteous, the dutiful, the good

21.grammar: A plural noun (singular barr) with 'the' and the preposition 'for/to' (li-). The -i ending is genitive, the case always required after a preposition like li-.

1.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
1.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

2.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
2.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

3.meaning: People of / folk of / those belonging to — the family, followers, or possessors of something (as in 'people of the Book'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with a thing.
3.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/folk of'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('people OF …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.
3.root: ء-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, people belonging to

4.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
4.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

5.meaning: Surely whoever, indeed the one who — combines an emphasizing 'truly/surely' with 'who/whoever', introducing the person(s) about whom something is affirmed.
5.grammar: The relative/conditional pronoun 'who/whoever' prefixed with the emphatic la- ('surely, truly'). It is an indeclinable word — it has no case ending and keeps one fixed form.

6.meaning: He believes, has faith, trusts securely — to affirm something as true with the heart and place trust in it; an ongoing or characteristic believing.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb in the (āmana) pattern. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine 'he/it' as the doer, and the final -u (unmarked here) indicates the ordinary, unconditioned present ('he believes / does believe').

7.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
7.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
7.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

8.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
8.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

9.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
9.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
9.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

10.meaning: To you / toward you (plural) — a preposition expressing motion or direction reaching a destination, joined with 'you all' as that destination.
10.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, toward'), whose ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached, plus -kum ('you all'). Together they mark the end-point or recipient of an action — the direction 'toward' or 'unto' a group.

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

12.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
12.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
12.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

13.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
13.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
13.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

14.meaning: Humbly submissive, lowly and reverent — those whose hearts and bodies are stilled in awe and quiet submission before something greater.
14.grammar: An active participle (describing the doer of the act) in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending is the plural form used for the object or oblique role (as opposed to -ūna for the subject).
14.root: خ-ش-ع (kh-sh-ʿ) — humility, reverent submission, stillness in awe

15.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
15.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

16.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
16.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

17.meaning: A verb meaning 'they buy / they trade / they exchange' — to acquire something by giving up something else in return. It often carries the sense of a bad bargain when one trades away something precious.
17.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) form-VIII verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks 'they', and the inseparable -ūna suffix shows the base (indicative) form, expressing an ongoing or habitual act of buying/exchanging.
17.root: ش-ر-ي (sh-r-y) — to buy, sell, trade, exchange (a transaction)

18.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
18.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
18.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

19.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
19.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

20.meaning: A price, a payment, the value or sum given in exchange for something.
20.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, commonly marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('a price').

21.meaning: 'A little / a small amount' — an adjective/noun meaning small in quantity, few, scant, or trifling.
21.grammar: A noun/adjective 'little' in the accusative case with indefinite marking (the -an ending, tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks an object or specifies amount/manner; the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite, 'a little.'
21.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — fewness; being little, scant, or small in amount

22.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
22.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

23.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
23.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

24.meaning: "Their reward / wage / recompense" — payment or recompense earned for work or conduct, whether a worldly wage or an otherworldly reward, bound to a 'their'.
24.grammar: A masculine singular noun with an attached possessive pronoun 'hum' ('their', masculine plural). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being asserted to exist.
24.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — to reward / recompense / hire

25.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
25.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

26.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
26.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
26.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

27.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
27.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

28.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
28.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

29.meaning: Swift, quick, fast — describing one who is rapid in carrying out something. Used of Allah, it conveys that an action (such as reckoning) is accomplished with utter speed.
29.grammar: An adjective in the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (denoting a strong, inherent quality). The final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case; with no tanwīn here it is in a possessive construction, 'swift of …,' linking it to a following noun.
29.root: س-ر-ع (s-r-ʿ) — to be swift, quick

30.meaning: The reckoning, accounting, or calling to account — the tallying and settling of deeds; also calculation or counting in a general sense.
30.grammar: A definite verbal noun with the article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i (kasra) marks the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or as the second part of a possessive pair ('… of the reckoning').

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: Be patient! Endure steadfastly, bear up, hold firm — a command to remain constant and not give way under hardship.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) verb. The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine-plural 'you (all)'; the initial i- is a helping vowel added because the verb's stem would otherwise begin with an unvoweled consonant.

5.meaning: And outdo one another in patience! Persevere against others' endurance, holding out longer than they do — patience set in mutual contest.

parts.en: endure in contest, outlast in patience

5.grammar: A command verb in the mutual/competitive (ṣābara) pattern, which adds the sense of contending with another. The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine-plural 'you (all)'.

6.meaning: And stand guard! Hold the frontier, stay tied to your post, remain on the alert — to bind oneself in readiness, especially guarding a border or being constant in devotion.

parts.en: stand guard, hold the frontier, stay posted

6.grammar: A command verb in the (rābaṭa) pattern, built on the idea of binding/tying oneself fast. The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine-plural 'you (all)'.
6.root: ر-ب-ط (r-b-ṭ) — binding, tying fast, stationing at a post

7.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'guard yourselves / be mindful and on your guard.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself by being conscious of Allah and shielding oneself from wrongdoing and its consequences.
7.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you (all).' The -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressees ('you all'). The pattern (form VIII, from waqā 'to protect') gives the sense of taking protective care for oneself.
7.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
8.root: — (proper name)

9.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

9.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

10.meaning: You succeed, prosper, attain what is sought, and thrive — to win true and lasting well-being and reach one's goal.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb in the (aflaḥa) pattern. The tu- prefix marks the second person 'you', and the -ūna ending makes it masculine-plural and signals the ordinary, unconditioned present ('you [all] succeed / will succeed').
